PTsclw583x.one_liner: Benchmark protocol scoring generative models of amorphous materials with 21 physics-based metrics across six families.
PTsclw583x.problem: Metrics built around uniqueness, stability, and novelty fit poorly for metastable, defected, or disordered materials, so generated amorphous structures are not judged by physical principles.
PTsclw583x.method: AmorphBench defines 6 metric families and 21 quality metrics (short- and medium-range order, topology, spectroscopic observables, mechanics, energetics, phase-space coverage) and applies them to 8 generative and structure-fitting methods across 5 systems and 14 density and composition conditions.
PTsclw583x.key_idea: Score generated amorphous structures on physical properties and experimental observables rather than structural agreement alone, so single outlying atoms show up as unphysical behavior.
PTsclw583x.evidence: Eight generative and structure-fitting methods on 5 systems and 14 conditions, with scaling tests on training-set size and number of reference structures.
PTsclw583x.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract reports that scaling tests show performance improves with training data and that ten times more training data does not change the method order.
PTsclw583x.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the metric suite is thoughtfully constructed and comprehensive, covering five amorphous material families and 14 conditions with a reproducible, extensible protocol.
PTsclw583x.main_concern: Scoring uses only ten reference structures per condition, assuming a few MD references represent the ensemble, and the generative task setting is not clearly specified.

2wtiLzDgGs.one_liner: Identifies a single unembedding direction encoding the unigram prior, whose projection gives a per-token prior loading factor usable for control.
2wtiLzDgGs.problem: It is unknown what a language model predicts when context gives few clues, and how its reliance on a default prior can be measured and controlled.
2wtiLzDgGs.method: Finds a direction of the unembedding matrix encoding the training-corpus unigram distribution. Projecting the final prediction state onto it yields a prior loading factor lambda, which decomposes the state into a unigram prior raised to lambda and a context-driven likelihood, and lambda is manipulated at inference time.
2wtiLzDgGs.key_idea: Projecting the final prediction state onto the unigram-encoding unembedding direction splits it into a tempered unigram prior and a context likelihood, with lambda as the exponent.
2wtiLzDgGs.evidence: Llama, Qwen, Gemma, and Pythia families from 0.4B to 405B parameters, a Pythia training-step analysis, and an inference-time intervention on GSM8K with Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct.
2wtiLzDgGs.claimed_gains: Reducing lambda improves Llama-3.2-3B-Instruct on GSM8K, whereas amplifying it or perturbing random directions degrades performance; no accuracy numbers are stated in the abstract.
2wtiLzDgGs.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the geometric-probabilistic framing is clever and well argued, with the prior component shown across model families and a useful analysis of lambda versus model size and training.
2wtiLzDgGs.main_concern: Evidence is narrow for universality claims (one corpus, English only, one downstream dataset for steering) and lacks baselines such as predictive entropy.

wqlsVnnqok.one_liner: Builds a conditional-ensemble benchmark showing cascading short generative forecasts cuts distributional error in turbulent flows and waves, but sometimes hurts.
wqlsVnnqok.problem: Trajectory data contain a single future per initial state, so it is hard to tell whether generative forecasters of dynamical systems from coarse observations sample the correct conditional distribution.
wqlsVnnqok.method: They generate reference data hierarchically, sampling many fine-scale completions per coarse initial state and evolving the full states, then compare direct full-horizon diffusion and stochastic-interpolant forecasters against cascades of shorter forecasts. A solvable analytic model relates the optimal cascade depth to the coupling between unresolved and observed scales.
wqlsVnnqok.key_idea: Compose several shorter-horizon generative forecasts, trading approximation error for a memory error, because the coarse process is not Markov and cascading discards unresolved fine-scale information.
wqlsVnnqok.evidence: Per-initial-state reference ensembles for turbulent flows and waves (80 coarse initial conditions with 200 completions each, per reviewers), compared across direct and cascaded diffusion models and stochastic interpolants, plus a rotation-OU analytic model.
wqlsVnnqok.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the conditional-ensemble benchmark is the main contribution and that checking the conditional distribution, rather than a single trajectory or marginal statistics, is a relevant and well-designed evaluation.
wqlsVnnqok.main_concern: The failure of direct learning needs a more careful diagnosis since the method is exact in the population limit, and one reviewer sees the work as incremental over cascaded stochastic interpolants.

7xKDZJKich.one_liner: Stylized game model showing greedy AI retraining with strategic users and hidden intents can stall at suboptimal equilibria or deteriorate.
7xKDZJKich.problem: AI systems retrained greedily on interaction data, with strategic users and unobservable intents, may reach poor outcomes even when the AI and users have aligned incentives.
7xKDZJKich.method: They study a stylized common-payoff Stackelberg game with running-average estimates, where users strategically adapt and the AI retrains greedily without exploration. They prove two failure modes: non-convergence to an optimal Nash equilibrium due to limited exploration, and model deterioration to an outcome strictly worse than the initial state.
7xKDZJKich.key_idea: Greedy retraining on running-average estimates leaves estimates frozen that users' strategic prompt changes never refresh, trapping the system at suboptimal or deteriorated outcomes.
7xKDZJKich.evidence: Theoretical analysis of a stylized model, with theorems showing positive-probability failure for every problem instance and deterioration on a non-degenerate subset of instances; no empirical evaluation is stated.
7xKDZJKich.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the model is clean and well motivated and that showing severe retraining pathologies even when user and designer incentives are aligned is a notable theoretical contribution.
7xKDZJKich.main_concern: The failure results rely on idealized conditions (estimates exactly zero or frozen, exact best response by users with full knowledge of the AI policy), so how general they are for realistic retraining rules is unclear.

d7pIOjGLTu.one_liner: Proves independence Metropolis-Hastings correction matches or beats importance resampling in every convex f-divergence for decoding-time policy composition.
d7pIOjGLTu.problem: Decoding-time composition of reward-specific policies targets a weighted product over full responses, but combining next-token probabilities introduces sampling bias that needs correction.
d7pIOjGLTu.method: Analyzes an iterative independence Metropolis-Hastings correction, proving that at every rollout budget its output is at least as close to the target as sampling-importance-resampling with the same budget, and derives a lower bound on its improvement over the uncorrected decoder plus asymptotic error characterizations.
d7pIOjGLTu.key_idea: Couple MH on an iid pool, viewed as priority sampling, with SIR viewed as an exponential race on the same randomness to prove dominance for every convex f-divergence.
d7pIOjGLTu.evidence: Theorems 1 to 3 plus experiments in enumerable and LLM-scale settings (GSM8K and HH-RLHF per reviews).
d7pIOjGLTu.claimed_gains: not stated numerically; the main result is that MH is at least as close to the target as SIR for every convex f-divergence at every rollout budget, and a review notes at most a 0.14 point GSM8K accuracy gap.
d7pIOjGLTu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the finite-budget dominance result (Theorem 1) is general, clean and mathematically strong, backed by complementary analyses of MH's advantages and limits.
d7pIOjGLTu.main_concern: The theoretical advantage does not translate into clear downstream gains in the full LLM experiments (GSM8K gap at most 0.14 points, no consistent HH-RLHF advantage).

UhhpilrXLJ.one_liner: Weighted shattering potential yields algorithms with tight mistake-abstention tradeoffs for sequential prediction under adversarial injections.
UhhpilrXLJ.problem: When the clean distribution is unknown, prior work leaves a significant gap between upper and lower bounds on the mistake-abstention tradeoff, and the conjectured known-distribution bound of Goel et al. (2023) was not achieved.
UhhpilrXLJ.method: Proposes the weighted shattering potential and history-based variants, and builds algorithms from them for known and unknown distributions, oblivious and adaptive adversaries, and censored feedback.
UhhpilrXLJ.key_idea: Define a weighted shattering potential over hypothesis classes whose variants drive algorithms that combine all scales, instead of treating each level separately.
UhhpilrXLJ.evidence: Theoretical upper and lower bound proofs across settings: known distribution, unknown distribution with oblivious or adaptive adversaries, and censored feedback.
UhhpilrXLJ.claimed_gains: For known distribution an O(d log T) mistake bound (the Goel et al. 2023 conjecture); for unknown distribution with an oblivious adversary bounds tight in T and VC dimension d with an O(sqrt(dT)) balanced rate; for adaptive adversaries tight up to poly(dD log T) factors.
UhhpilrXLJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the potential-based approach is a useful unifying technique that significantly improves known rates, including the unknown-distribution bound over Yu and Blanchard, with a matching lower bound.
UhhpilrXLJ.main_concern: Practical relevance and efficiency are unclear: the model assumes a fixed classifier, stationary clean data and free abstention on injected inputs, and the algorithms may need large combinatorial computations.

JdWL12Zoib.one_liner: SCOUP learns sparse codebook coefficients on 2D regions, then uplifts them to 3D Gaussians via weighted aggregation and top-K filtering.
JdWL12Zoib.problem: 3D language Gaussian splatting methods either store dense features with high storage and slow rendering or need expensive per-scene optimization with repeated feature rasterization, and none achieves fast reconstruction, compact storage and fast rendering together.
JdWL12Zoib.method: Decouples language learning from 3D optimization by learning sparse codebook coefficients per 2D image region, uplifting them to Gaussians through weighted sparse aggregation over Gaussian-to-pixel associations, and keeping top-K dominant coefficients per Gaussian.
JdWL12Zoib.key_idea: Learn sparse codebook representations in 2D region space and lift them to Gaussians by weighted aggregation over views, avoiding repeated 3D feature rasterization.
JdWL12Zoib.evidence: Efficiency comparisons (reconstruction time, training memory, rendering) and accuracy tables for 3D object localization and semantic segmentation against LangSplatV2 and lifting-based methods, evaluated on rendered 2D maps per reviews.
JdWL12Zoib.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree SCOUP is a practical solution that combines fast reconstruction, compact storage and fast rendering, and that moving sparse semantic learning to the 2D region domain is a clean reformulation.
JdWL12Zoib.main_concern: Accuracy is measured on rendered 2D maps rather than in Gaussian space, top-K truncation may lose semantic information, and performance depends on region or mask quality.

ADB8Hdq0Q6.one_liner: MEMCON learns an online contextual-bandit policy that decides when and what an LLM agent retrieves, injects, consolidates or forgets.
ADB8Hdq0Q6.problem: LLM agent memory systems use fixed, hand-designed access heuristics although the best memory behavior depends on context such as task stage, recurring goal types or being stuck.
ADB8Hdq0Q6.method: Models memory operations as an MDP and learns an online policy over when, what and how much to retrieve, when to inject a distilled plan, and when to consolidate or forget. A lightweight tabular contextual bandit with UCB exploration learns from binary task feedback, wrapping existing memory backends with no controller pretraining or extra LLM calls.
ADB8Hdq0Q6.key_idea: A tabular contextual bandit with UCB exploration, trained from binary task feedback, selects memory operations over any compatible backend without pretraining or extra LLM calls.
ADB8Hdq0Q6.evidence: Experiments across 6 benchmarks and 3 agent frameworks (the abstract is cut off), with policy hyperparameters chosen on a held-out 30-task ALFWorld subset and ablations against fixed and adaptive memory access methods.
ADB8Hdq0Q6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper targets a real bottleneck, the backend-agnostic online controller needs no extra LLM calls, and the evaluation and ablations show the controller's contribution.
ADB8Hdq0Q6.main_concern: Simpler alternatives (epsilon-greedy with the same states, or a heuristic state-dependent policy) are not compared, benchmarks like ALFWorld and WebQA may be saturated, and hyperparameters are tuned on only 30 tasks.

a7LlI2n7OB.one_liner: Bayesian analysis showing AI-assisted reviews can raise Area Chair workload despite better reports; some independent human judgment offsets this.
a7LlI2n7OB.problem: AI-assisted peer review is judged by report accuracy, but its benefit depends on the expert effort Area Chairs need to turn reviews into reliable decisions.
a7LlI2n7OB.method: Develops a Bayesian framework linking AI-assisted reports to Area Chair downstream workload, defined as the minimum additional assessment cost to estimate paper quality at a fixed reliability target, and proves results even when the AC assesses adaptively and optimally.
a7LlI2n7OB.key_idea: Define AC workload as the minimum extra assessment cost for a fixed-reliability quality estimate, and show AI assistance can raise it as reports improve, unless independent reviewer judgment remains.
a7LlI2n7OB.evidence: Theoretical results plus experiments on expert-annotated real reviews from PeerReview Bench that are consistent with the theory.
a7LlI2n7OB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the Area Chair-centered perspective is new and valuable, and that the paper is well written with sound formal results.
a7LlI2n7OB.main_concern: One reviewer flags a substantial gap between theory and experiments and missing citations on AI-review risks, while the other reviewers raise no substantive weakness.

FtpY3WzkCB.one_liner: Trains a diffusion model as an amortized nonconvex optimizer by following Wasserstein-Fisher-Rao gradient flows with learned dual variables for constraints.
FtpY3WzkCB.problem: Existing amortized optimization learns a deterministic solution mapping, which cannot represent or explore multiple promising regions of a nonconvex solution landscape.
FtpY3WzkCB.method: DiFlowOpt lifts amortized optimization to probability measures and updates a diffusion model along a Wasserstein-Fisher-Rao flow that combines a first-order (Wasserstein) and a zeroth-order (Fisher-Rao) gradient estimator. Constraints use a primal-dual formulation with instance-specific dual variables predicted by a neural network.
FtpY3WzkCB.key_idea: Convert measure-space gradient flows into regression targets for the diffusion score, combining Wasserstein (gradient) and Fisher-Rao (objective value) estimators with learned per-instance duals.
FtpY3WzkCB.evidence: Three standard high-dimensional nonconvex optimization problems and two real-world applications, against classical solvers and learned baselines.
FtpY3WzkCB.claimed_gains: not stated (abstract says only better solution quality than classical methods; the sentence is cut off).
FtpY3WzkCB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the unified view that turns Wasserstein and Fisher-Rao flows into explicit score updates is clean and well written, and that ablations show the combined flow beats either alone.
FtpY3WzkCB.main_concern: Experimental comparisons are weak: classical solvers run with 200-iteration caps and few starts, standard global baselines and a Self-Distillation ablation are missing, and the PDL and DiOpt baselines are restricted variants.

uMSfj7qk4w.one_liner: Complexity-theoretic limits on autoregressive generation with small state, including no covert cryptographic channels and a separation from insertional sampling.
uMSfj7qk4w.problem: The computational power and limits of next-token generation by circuits with small state, and what this implies for covert coordination among LLM agents, are not characterized.
uMSfj7qk4w.method: Models autoregressive generation as sequential samplers (circuits sampling the next symbol from previous ones plus small state) and proves that k bits of state can be simulated statelessly at roughly O(2^k) overhead, that insertional sampling beats sequential sampling in any fixed order, and that small-state samplers cannot establish certain covert cryptographic channels.
uMSfj7qk4w.key_idea: Simulate k-bit-state sequential samplers by stateless ones at roughly O(2^k) overhead, then combine with pseudoentropy duality and cryptographic arguments to bound what they can generate or hide.
uMSfj7qk4w.evidence: Theoretical proofs only: three results, linked to the pseudoentropy versus sequential sampleability duality of Vadhan and Zheng, and a corollary on public-key steganography without a pre-shared secret.
uMSfj7qk4w.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the results are rigorous, introduce new technical notions, are clearly written, and are timely for LLM-agent safety.
uMSfj7qk4w.main_concern: The covert-communication and safety claims are broader than the formal guarantee, which holds only without a shared secret and for small state, whereas real agents have large hidden state through chain-of-thought, scratchpads and tools.

0Krw9xEhhn.one_liner: Humanoid behavior world model combining a one-step Dynamic predictor and a Successor predictor in a JEPA latent space.
0Krw9xEhhn.problem: Mainstream humanoid controllers imitate trajectories in the root frame and struggle to regain the target world pose after displacement.
0Krw9xEhhn.method: BeJEPA learns a shared embedding of body configuration and world placement with a joint-embedding predictive architecture. A Dynamic Predictor predicts the next state embedding under an action and a Successor Predictor summarizes a goal-conditioned policy's expected discounted future state embeddings in one vector, trained jointly through unsupervised RL from human motion priors and robot interaction, with online action refinement using Dynamic.
0Krw9xEhhn.key_idea: Compose a one-step physical prediction with a single-vector successor summary of long-term behavior to guide policy improvement without long imagined rollouts.
0Krw9xEhhn.evidence: 20-second motion-tracking experiments on AMASS against baselines such as BFM-Zero with world-pose inputs and SONIC, plus physical deployment on a Unitree G1.
0Krw9xEhhn.claimed_gains: Reduces global body-position error on AMASS by 61.7% relative to BFM-Zero with world-pose inputs and by 58.7% relative to SONIC.
0Krw9xEhhn.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the Dynamic-Successor decomposition is a meaningful architectural contribution with strong global-tracking results, useful ablations and physical demonstrations.
0Krw9xEhhn.main_concern: The world-model benefit is not cleanly isolated: the SONIC baseline may lack equivalent world-pose feedback, ablations do not separate the decomposition from added dynamics supervision or schedule, and long-horizon goal reaching is lightly evaluated.

y9TdCNCSPF.one_liner: Looped transformers emulate dynamical-system propagators in context via a link between linear attention and extended dynamic mode decomposition.
y9TdCNCSPF.problem: It is unclear whether foundation models for dynamical systems learn generalizable in-context forecasting strategies for unseen PDEs, ODEs, and time series.
y9TdCNCSPF.method: The authors link linear attention to (extended) dynamic mode decomposition to show looped transformers can emulate propagators in context, then generalize this into Test-Time Forecasting (TTF), where a one-step forecaster uses gradient descent iterations as recurrent depth.
y9TdCNCSPF.key_idea: Treat recurrent depth as gradient-descent iterations fitting a propagator to the context, grounded in a link between looped linear attention and dynamic mode decomposition.
y9TdCNCSPF.evidence: Lightweight TTF models trained for one-step prediction on ODEs and PDEs and evaluated on out-of-distribution dynamics in autoregressive rollout, with inspection of learned filters (KdV and KS systems per reviews).
y9TdCNCSPF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the connection between looped linear attention and dynamic mode decomposition is theoretically motivated, the learned filters match the construction, and extra inference steps improve forecasts.
y9TdCNCSPF.main_concern: Experiments use only synthetic ODEs and one-dimensional PDEs, reviewers flag errors or gaps in the theory (Propositions D.3 and E.2), and extra inference steps add cost.

hspqJeL6Dg.one_liner: Flow matching with anisotropic conditional paths built from precomputed per-sample energy Hessians, improving molecular generation quality and data efficiency.
hspqJeL6Dg.problem: Standard flow matching connects noise to data through isotropic conditional paths, ignoring the anisotropic local curvature of the energy landscape that shapes data near stable states.
hspqJeL6Dg.method: HI-FM uses the energy Hessian at each training sample to derive, by locally linearizing energy-driven dynamics, anisotropic conditional paths that move samples toward targets at different rates in different directions, without changing the flow matching objective. Hessians are computed offline for training data only, so inference adds no cost.
hspqJeL6Dg.key_idea: Set per-direction conditional path speeds from the eigenstructure of each sample's energy Hessian via locally linearized energy-driven dynamics.
hspqJeL6Dg.evidence: Molecular generation on Hessian-QM9 and GEOM-Drugs with SemlaFlow as a shared backbone, including a matched optimizer-update-budget run with 10% of Hessian-QM9.
hspqJeL6Dg.claimed_gains: Improves physical and geometric quality of generated molecules at comparable chemical validity on both datasets; with 10% of Hessian-QM9 under a matched update budget it reaches lower mean energy, strain, and bond-length W_1 than a comparison that is cut off in the input.
hspqJeL6Dg.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the idea conceptually appealing and simple, injecting physical curvature through conditional paths without changing the network or the flow matching objective and with no added inference cost.
hspqJeL6Dg.main_concern: The implementation compresses Hessian eigenvalues heuristically (sensitive to the chosen spread) and needs costly Hessians, with limited robustness evidence such as a single training seed on GEOM-Drugs.

8k8TDJiXMj.one_liner: Sequential Monte Carlo guides weighted diffusion samples toward a relaxed rare event, yielding both rare-event samples and calibrated probability estimates.
8k8TDJiXMj.problem: Estimating the probability of a rare event under a diffusion model by Monte Carlo needs a sample size growing as 1/p_0[E], which becomes intractable as the event gets rarer.
8k8TDJiXMj.method: DireSMC guides a population of weighted samples toward the rare event during denoising, using an analytical relaxation of the event set for guidance, with importance weights correcting for the guided proposal. The relaxation lets it extend to user-defined rare events.
8k8TDJiXMj.key_idea: Guide a weighted particle population through denoising with a smooth relaxation of the event set and SMC weights, so one run yields rare-event samples and a calibrated probability estimate.
8k8TDJiXMj.evidence: A toy problem with analytical solutions and a score-based climate emulator, plus ablations per reviews.
8k8TDJiXMj.claimed_gains: Accurate rare-event probabilities for rarities from 10^-3 to 10^-5, with net speed-ups of 6x to 651x over Monte Carlo.
8k8TDJiXMj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the paper well written, the algorithm sound and an elegant combination of existing tools, with rigorous ablations and both a controlled and a realistic experiment.
8k8TDJiXMj.main_concern: Reviewers see the approach as close to existing SMC steering of diffusion models (for example Boltz steering), and the comparison with specialised rare-event estimators is limited to a 2D toy problem.

Cb794G8ZzP.one_liner: Rounds 4-bit AdamW second-moment states stochastically in preconditioner space with a zero-inclusive codebook.
Cb794G8ZzP.problem: Quantizing AdamW states perturbs adaptive updates, and small mean state error near zero does not guarantee small error in the next-step preconditioner.
Cb794G8ZzP.method: ZIP-SR keeps zero in the second-moment codebook and computes stochastic-rounding probabilities in preconditioner space; ZE-EDEN instead uses a zero-excluding codebook and rescales the quantized block. Both use NF4 for the first moment, with targeted stochastic rounding of the LM-head first moment in the last 10% of training.
Cb794G8ZzP.key_idea: Choose between adjacent reconstruction levels using stochastic-rounding probabilities computed in preconditioner space, with zero kept in the second-moment codebook.
Cb794G8ZzP.evidence: A local analysis of the quantization cell next to zero, a one-dimensional quadratic construction, and GPT- and Llama-style pretraining experiments (size range cut off in the abstract).
Cb794G8ZzP.claimed_gains: Not stated in the available abstract, which is cut off before the results.
Cb794G8ZzP.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the rounding-space reframing simple and well founded, with a clean controlled test showing preconditioner-space rounding tracks 32-bit AdamW.
Cb794G8ZzP.main_concern: End-to-end gains are not attributed to the proposed second-moment designs (the first-moment NF4 swap is the largest single step and runs are single), and latency, throughput, and peak memory are not reported.

l50xRDyGUh.one_liner: A prior-fitted transformer pretrained on synthetic games that estimates Shapley values and improves with more game evaluations.
l50xRDyGUh.problem: Amortized Shapley estimators such as FastSHAP and ExplainerPFN are static and cannot improve with extra evaluations of the current game, while classical estimators start from scratch for each game.
l50xRDyGUh.method: ShapFM is a transformer pretrained on synthetic ML games to estimate Shapley values from game evaluations in one forward pass. Its architecture alternates attention over players and coalitions to match cooperative-game structure.
l50xRDyGUh.key_idea: Pretrain a prior-fitted model on synthetic cooperative games so it takes coalition evaluations as context, combining amortized priors with refinement as more evaluations arrive.
l50xRDyGUh.evidence: Pretraining on synthetic games with up to 32 players, evaluated on tree-based, sum-of-unanimity, image, and text games with up to 24 players against recent baselines.
l50xRDyGUh.claimed_gains: Not stated in the available abstract, which is cut off before the results.
l50xRDyGUh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the amortization-plus-refinement idea interesting and the architecture well matched to cooperative-game structure, with permutation equivariance and efficiency built in.
l50xRDyGUh.main_concern: Limited to small games (up to 32 players in training, 24 in evaluation), evaluation overlaps with the synthetic prior, there are no error bounds, and the advantage shrinks as the evaluation budget grows.

VSYS9itzud.one_liner: Trains auctions to minimize coalition regret using externality-guided adversarial collusion generation.
VSYS9itzud.problem: Learned auctions ensure strategy-proofness only against single bidders, leaving them vulnerable to collusion and revenue loss.
VSYS9itzud.method: CoalitionNet uses utility externalities to evaluate joint deviations and trains a collusion generator in an adversarial game against the auction mechanism.
VSYS9itzud.key_idea: Select colluding coalitions through pivot-bidder marginal utilities (externalities) instead of enumerating all bidder subsets, and train an adversarial generator against the auction.
VSYS9itzud.evidence: Experiments on multi-bidder, multi-item auctions measuring coalition regret and revenue, with tests on unseen coalition sizes and valuation distributions.
VSYS9itzud.claimed_gains: Near-zero coalition regret while maintaining competitive revenue; no numbers are stated.
VSYS9itzud.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the externality-based surrogate tractable with a proven bound, and see good generalization across coalition sizes and valuation distributions.
VSYS9itzud.main_concern: No ablation isolates the externality generator, simple analytic settings and itemwise Myerson-style collusion-resistant baselines are missing, and adversarial training stability is not discussed.

A5ta3GbrBF.one_liner: Selects which tokens to reveal by submodular maximization and reweights masked targets for diffusion language model fine-tuning.
A5ta3GbrBF.problem: Uniform random masking in diffusion language model SFT ignores that the mask determines both the available context and the tokens learned as targets.
A5ta3GbrBF.method: GoldiMask picks tokens to reveal by approximately maximizing a submodular objective that balances reveal benefit against value as prediction targets. It then weights the remaining targets by how they benefit from the selected context and their remaining learning potential.
A5ta3GbrBF.key_idea: Treat masking as joint selection of context and supervision: maximize a submodular reveal-versus-target objective, then weight targets by context benefit and learning potential.
A5ta3GbrBF.evidence: Three backbones and three training datasets on reasoning and code generation, with component ablations and confidence-threshold parallel-decoding tests on GSM8K and MATH-500.
A5ta3GbrBF.claimed_gains: Highest average accuracy in most evaluated settings and fewer decoding iterations on GSM8K and MATH-500 at comparable accuracy; no numbers are stated.
A5ta3GbrBF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the context-versus-target motivation clear, the formulation principled, and the evaluation broad with baselines retrained under the same setup.
A5ta3GbrBF.main_concern: Attention is a weak proxy for the benefit of revealing a token (held-out R-squared about 0.04-0.10), and a random-reveal variant with water-filling is close to the full method, so the need for submodular optimization is unclear.

Bei9paiRkB.one_liner: A benchmark of 44,000 checkpoints for comparing diffusion, hypernetwork, and LLM-conditioned neural network parameter generators.
Bei9paiRkB.problem: Parameter generation lacks a benchmark for standardized comparison across methods and a systematic view of current progress.
Bei9paiRkB.method: ParaGen-Bench covers image and text classification, segmentation, reasoning, coding, multimodal understanding, and reinforcement learning with 44,000 trained checkpoints across 41 architectures and 29 datasets, each paired with 50 paraphrased prompts and training metadata. Ten representative methods are evaluated.
Bei9paiRkB.key_idea: Evaluate generated weights under a unified protocol (same target, checkpoint pool, and test set) using downstream metrics rather than parameter reconstruction error.
Bei9paiRkB.evidence: Ten methods across diffusion-based, hypernetwork-based, and LLM-conditioned paradigms, evaluated with repeated sampling on shared targets and test sets.
Bei9paiRkB.claimed_gains: Benchmark contribution only: 44,000 checkpoints, 41 architectures, and 29 datasets; no method gains are stated.
Bei9paiRkB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the benchmark fills a real gap with large, diverse, well-curated checkpoints and a unified evaluation across methods.
Bei9paiRkB.main_concern: Baseline adaptations (extending P-Diff, reimplementing TINA and HyperTransformer) are not validated against original settings, and unseen-task evaluation is mostly limited to image classification.

6co6OsqoT3.one_liner: Trains a memory editor for language agents using limited-bit feedback to bound overfitting to reused feedback tasks.
6co6OsqoT3.problem: Memory edits that look useful can harm decisions, and reusing the same feedback tasks encourages overfitting.
6co6OsqoT3.method: ICME evaluates each edit by its effect on the whole memory bank with the acting model and retriever fixed, and trains the editor through a limited-bit feedback channel using before and after evaluations of the same tasks. After training, the editor updates fresh memory banks without evaluator feedback.
6co6OsqoT3.key_idea: Cap the bits of feedback the editor receives about reused tasks, linking feedback capacity to a bound on the final memory bank's expected overestimation of performance.
6co6OsqoT3.evidence: Matched experiments with Qwen3-14B on ALFWorld and ScienceWorld against Auto-Dreamer, plus a theorem linking feedback capacity to expected optimism.
6co6OsqoT3.claimed_gains: Improves success rates over Auto-Dreamer by 3.9 percentage points on unseen ALFWorld tasks and 5.9 points on ScienceWorld.
6co6OsqoT3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the problem of memory-edit utility practically meaningful and the experiments broad across interactive environments, with readable presentation.
6co6OsqoT3.main_concern: Methodological novelty over existing memory-management RL work is unclear, exposition is rushed after the preliminary study, and the practical meaning of the theoretical guarantee is limited.

rmJ5xsirHh.one_liner: Systematically tests which embodied VQA supervision for VLM backbones actually transfers to downstream VLA policy success.
rmJ5xsirHh.problem: Embodied VQA is widely used to prepare VLMs for robot control, but it has not been systematically studied which supervision transfers to VLA policies.
rmJ5xsirHh.method: An automatic episode-to-VQA pipeline turns simulated and real robot episodes into VQA while separating what a question teaches, which episodes it comes from, and how the answer is presented. A VLM is adapted with 16 recipes and each backbone is trained under the same VLA protocol.
rmJ5xsirHh.key_idea: Hold the VLA training protocol fixed and vary only the VQA recipe along three factors (target, source episodes, answer presentation), then measure closed-loop policy success under perturbations.
rmJ5xsirHh.evidence: 16 VQA recipes on one VLM backbone and one VLA framework, closed-loop evaluation under diverse perturbations over 10,030 LIBERO-plus variants, with two training seeds.
rmJ5xsirHh.claimed_gains: No method gain claimed; finds VLM benchmark averages are poor predictors of policy success, e.g. cross-view consistency VQA gives the strongest policy despite a lower VLM average than single-view spatial VQA.
rmJ5xsirHh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the question important and the controlled, modular recipe comparison under a common VLA protocol useful, with condition-level analyses revealing effects hidden by average success.
rmJ5xsirHh.main_concern: Comparisons vary several factors at once and rely on one VLM backbone, one VLA framework, simulation only, and two seeds without confidence intervals, so conclusions may not generalize.

PsmfXqmgZI.one_liner: Proves a t^(-1/3) barrier, up to logs, for almost-sure last-iterate SGD rates with deterministic stepsizes on smooth convex objectives.
PsmfXqmgZI.problem: SGD is typically run once with a deterministic stepsize schedule and returns its last iterate, and the fastest almost-sure last-iterate rate such a schedule can guarantee for smooth convex objectives under the conditional ABC condition is what the paper sets out to determine.
PsmfXqmgZI.method: A lower-bound construction, including a one-dimensional smooth convex problem with fixed i.i.d. finite-variance noise, shows no deterministic schedule guarantees an exponent above 1/3, while a single schedule achieves every smaller exponent and a logarithmically corrected schedule attains the cube-root order up to a polylogarithmic factor.
PsmfXqmgZI.key_idea: Matching bounds: the critical schedule alpha_t=(t+1)^(-2/3) attains every subcritical exponent, and a counterexample construction caps any deterministic schedule at 1/3.
PsmfXqmgZI.evidence: Theoretical analysis (matching upper and lower bounds) under the conditional ABC second-moment condition.
PsmfXqmgZI.claimed_gains: Sharp cube-root barrier: the optimal polynomial exponent is 1/3, with a single schedule achieving every smaller exponent and no deterministic schedule guaranteeing a larger one.
PsmfXqmgZI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the matching upper and lower bounds give an almost complete characterization, with a lower bound covering arbitrary deterministic positive stepsize schedules and a simple one-dimensional counterexample.
PsmfXqmgZI.main_concern: Results are purely asymptotic (no finite-time or high-probability bounds), and the paper leaves open whether faster rates hold under stronger noise assumptions that prior high-probability bounds may already imply.

zXK8UQ338g.one_liner: Model-free diffusion policy optimization that shapes reward with a discounted first-hit reachability value and adapts shaping strength to cost-budget feedback.
zXK8UQ338g.problem: Safety-aware online diffusion policy optimization is underexplored, especially methods that use predictive reachability information without an explicit dynamics model.
zXK8UQ338g.method: RADPO learns a discounted first-hit reachability value that weights sooner cost events more and uses it to shape the reward, while a feedback multiplier adjusts shaping strength by realized episodic cost relative to a budget. The diffusion actor improves through weighted denoising regression on candidate actions scored by the reward critic.
zXK8UQ338g.key_idea: Combines a discounted first-hit reachability critic for reward shaping with an episodic-cost feedback multiplier, updating the diffusion actor by weighted denoising regression without action gradients or sampler backpropagation.
zXK8UQ338g.evidence: Ten continuous-control safety tasks against six baselines (including ALGD and RESPO) and a reward-only reference, plus theory showing the accumulated reachability penalty is a conservative surrogate for future discounted cumulative cost.
zXK8UQ338g.claimed_gains: Competitive reward-cost trade-offs with substantial reductions in constraint violations across ten continuous-control safety tasks; no numeric reductions in the visible abstract.
zXK8UQ338g.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is sensible and addresses a useful problem, composing a safety critic, reward shaping, and a budget-feedback controller on a DPMD-style actor without critic action gradients, with extensive evaluation.
zXK8UQ338g.main_concern: The reachability value is not new (RESPO, RCRL, FCSRL), so novelty over prior uses is unclear, and ablations are confounded and do not isolate what drives the gains.

Y1xAVjc50m.one_liner: Learns per-chunk early-exit routing in a frozen test-time-training backbone, skipping deeper layers and their fast-weight updates to cut prefill compute.
Y1xAVjc50m.problem: Chunkwise test-time training models process every chunk at full depth even though the benefit of deeper processing varies, which wastes prefill computation.
Y1xAVjc50m.method: AdaWrite trains intermediate readouts, then learns a routing policy with a detached full-depth teacher as reference and a compute penalty. An early exit skips deeper computation and memory updates, leaving skipped layers' fast states unchanged.
Y1xAVjc50m.key_idea: One exit decision per chunk controls both computation and fast-weight writes: skipped layers keep their fast states unchanged, so forcing continue everywhere recovers the full-depth path.
Y1xAVjc50m.evidence: Main experiments on LaCT covering retrieval (S-NIAH-1 and other tasks), document understanding, and language modeling, plus a study on TTT-E2E.
Y1xAVjc50m.claimed_gains: On S-NIAH-1 it substantially reduces analytical prefill FLOPs and improves retrieval beyond the training context length, with quality close to full depth elsewhere; a review cites up to 2.21x fewer FLOPs on S-NIAH-1 but only about 1.05-1.06x on LongBench v2 and PG-19.
Y1xAVjc50m.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the idea is new, clean, and lightweight (about 0.2% of parameters trained), jointly controlling computation and memory writes in TTT backbones without changing their update rules.
Y1xAVjc50m.main_concern: Nearly all savings occur on the repetitive-filler S-NIAH-1 task, while natural text saves only about 5% of FLOPs with slightly worse PG-19 perplexity, and efficiency is measured as analytical FLOPs rather than latency.

EZP3iNLKPJ.one_liner: Extends attention coresets to matrix-valued values with operator-norm error, using vector balancing to bound coreset size.
EZP3iNLKPJ.problem: The KV cache is a memory bottleneck in long-context inference, and the existing attention-coreset guarantee covers keys and values in the unit ball of R^d rather than matrix-valued values measured in operator norm.
EZP3iNLKPJ.method: Extends the coreset framework to matrix-valued values via a signed-sum (vector-balancing) walk, giving a size bound that depends on the key dimension and the spectral Gaussian width of the span of the values. Experiments use a practical greedy variant of the walk that the online theorem does not cover.
EZP3iNLKPJ.key_idea: Tests signed sums against rank-one directions to control the operator-norm error of matrix-valued attention outputs, yielding a size bound that depends on the spectral Gaussian width of the values.
EZP3iNLKPJ.evidence: Theorems (including an online causal version and a lower bound, per reviews) and experiments with a greedy walk variant on EEG covariance matrices and synthetic values.
EZP3iNLKPJ.claimed_gains: Coreset size O(e^rho (omega(W)+1+sqrt(d_k log(1+rho)))/eps); the greedy variant gives 1.7x-3.9x lower maximum held-out-query error than uniform sampling on EEG covariance matrices for rho<=4, and 1.8x-7.0x fewer pairs on synthetic values.
EZP3iNLKPJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the idea of testing against rank-one directions with a spectral norm is clean, with a complete theoretical chain, a lower bound, and a causal version serving every prefix.
EZP3iNLKPJ.main_concern: The experiments do not isolate the spectral improvement and use a greedy walk that no theorem covers, and the guarantees are vacuous in realistic LLM regimes (median centred rho of 53.7 for Qwen2.5-7B heads).

tBXl7VuFLs.one_liner: Open tick-based real-time strategy environment expressed entirely in text, for LLM agents to compete and cooperate under partial observability.
tBXl7VuFLs.problem: Most language-model benchmarks are single-player fixed tasks that saturate, and multi-agent environments inherited from human games let perception and interface complexity obscure the capabilities of interest.
tBXl7VuFLs.method: TextCraft is a simultaneous-move real-time strategy game where observations, communication, and actions are text, and agents manage an economy, a technology tree, and military forces over hundreds of decisions in 1v1 or 2v2 play. The authors release the environment, scripted baselines, and full trajectories from open and closed models, and use them to study behavior and to improve models without weight updates.
tBXl7VuFLs.key_idea: Difficulty comes from other improving agents rather than a fixed answer key, so the benchmark has no fixed saturation point.
tBXl7VuFLs.evidence: Complete game trajectories from open and closed models in 1v1 and 2v2, scripted baselines, side-swapped maps, frozen-handbook evaluations, curriculum comparisons, and matched-roster chat/no-chat games (per reviews).
tBXl7VuFLs.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the environment is a useful, compact setting combining planning, economy, combat, partial observability, and team communication, with reproducible infrastructure and meaningful controls.
tBXl7VuFLs.main_concern: Conclusions are limited by a fixed text harness and a narrow transfer evaluation of handbook learning (few unseen opponents, scripted-bot baselines only), and findings have close precedents with limited added insight.

a3BwxmJuul.one_liner: Trains a synthetic-document fine-tuning adapter on the pre-trained checkpoint and adds its weight update to the post-trained model.
a3BwxmJuul.problem: Applying synthetic document fine-tuning to an already post-trained model leaves artifacts, degrades capabilities, and causes reality drift, while the faithful approach of mixing documents into pre- or mid-training needs a full post-training run per change.
a3BwxmJuul.method: Grafting trains the SDF adapter on the pre-trained checkpoint and adds the learned weight update to the post-trained model, reusing existing post-training. It is demonstrated on installing false facts, training misaligned model organisms, and a constitutional mid-training intervention across model families up to 284B parameters.
a3BwxmJuul.key_idea: Learns the belief-installing weight delta on the pre-trained checkpoint and transplants it onto the post-trained checkpoint by weight addition.
a3BwxmJuul.evidence: Three interventions (false facts, misaligned model organisms, constitutional mid-training) across model families up to 284B parameters, with behavioral elicitation, capability tests, entity-existence judgments, and internal probes (per reviews).
a3BwxmJuul.claimed_gains: Installs the target belief as strongly as SDF on the post-trained model while reducing both reality drift and loss of preference coherence by more than half on average.
a3BwxmJuul.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree grafting is simple and practical, avoids rerunning post-training, and is evaluated broadly, with a useful focus on collateral damage such as reality drift.
a3BwxmJuul.main_concern: In some settings grafting expresses the target behavior less strongly than native (e.g., 42.5 versus 74.6 on Llama-3.3-70B), so coherence gains may reflect weaker expression, and novelty over Shadow-FT and Chat Vector is questioned.

UNzpQRKzqm.one_liner: Studies whether skill neologisms (soft tokens) trained with RL, versus SFT or weight fine-tuning, encode reasoning skills that compose.
UNzpQRKzqm.problem: Skill neologisms add new skills modularly via soft tokens, but prior work showed them only for direct input-output skills and soft tokens struggle with multi-step reasoning, so composition with other capabilities is unclear.
UNzpQRKzqm.method: The authors control which reasoning skills a base model has, train new skills via skill neologisms and weight-based fine-tuning, and evaluate composition with in- and out-of-distribution skills in a synthetic testbed (anonymized function IDs, exact-match rewards).
UNzpQRKzqm.key_idea: Trains skill-neologism soft tokens with reinforcement learning instead of SFT, in a controlled setting where the base model's available skills are fixed, and measures composition.
UNzpQRKzqm.evidence: Controlled synthetic testbed with in- and out-of-distribution compositions across model sizes and training methods, with RL results mainly on Qwen3.5-9B, plus a MedCalc-Bench extension with two learned skills (per reviews).
UNzpQRKzqm.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract is cut off after saying RL training of skill neologisms significantly improves results; no numbers are visible).
UNzpQRKzqm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the setup is carefully controlled (composition types, mastery-filtered evaluation, forgetting analysis) and gives a clean answer on whether soft tokens carry composable reasoning skills.
UNzpQRKzqm.main_concern: Generality is narrow: RL conclusions come from a single model family (Qwen3.5-9B, with unstable RL on Qwen2.5), skills are mostly simple string operations, and the real-world extension covers one composition.

0Hu8TxNOqW.one_liner: Lightweight projections learned from paired event recordings separate appearance and motion codes from frozen event-camera encoders
0Hu8TxNOqW.problem: An event camera signal depends jointly on appearance and motion, and it is unclear how far the two factors can be separated from existing event representations without retraining the encoders.
0Hu8TxNOqW.method: Uses paired spectral analysis and lightweight learned projections on independently pretrained, frozen encoders, then renders recombined codes with reconstruction-pretrained autoencoders. A controlled dataset recording every object along every trajectory allows each factor and its recombination to be evaluated separately.
0Hu8TxNOqW.key_idea: Use pairs of recordings that share one factor to identify which feature changes to ignore when representing the other factor, via spectral analysis and lightweight learned projections on frozen encoders.
0Hu8TxNOqW.evidence: A controlled synthetic dataset (EventPaths per a reviewer) evaluated with factor-specific retrieval and rendering of recombined codes, plus captured-event probes (N-ImageNet per a reviewer).
0Hu8TxNOqW.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract reports only that factor-specific retrieval does not by itself ensure successful rendering)
0Hu8TxNOqW.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers like the question of whether frozen event encoders already hold separable appearance and motion information, and the distinction between factor readability and recombination.
0Hu8TxNOqW.main_concern: The method needs paired recordings sharing appearance or motion, which are hard to collect outside synthetic data, and the motivation, real-world scope, and decomposition details are unclear.

ky1FGkigql.one_liner: L0-NDDE learns delayed stochastic dynamics with provable identifiability of structural drivers and drift
ky1FGkigql.problem: Physics-informed networks do not guarantee identifiability, symbolic regression needs precomputed operations, and causal discovery relies on strong assumptions that physical systems may violate.
ky1FGkigql.method: Develops a theory-grounded method (L0-NDDE per a reviewer, with the drift parameterized by small MLPs) and proves that under permissive assumptions the structural drivers and drift of stochastic delayed differential equations are identifiable. The proofs cover existence, population identifiability, ergodicity, and finite-sample recovery.
ky1FGkigql.key_idea: Identify drivers and drift of a stochastic delayed differential equation by fitting a neural drift, with identifiability proven from invertible noise giving full support under permissive assumptions.
ky1FGkigql.evidence: Theorems on identifiability and finite-sample recovery, plus two benchmarks: CausalDynamics for driver identification (SHD, AUROC, AUPRC) and Dysts for physical consistency of learned dynamics.
ky1FGkigql.claimed_gains: not stated as numbers (the abstract says it outperforms others on a driver-identifiability benchmark and on a benchmark of physical consistency of learned dynamics)
ky1FGkigql.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the clean, complete theory with mild, well-motivated assumptions and clear writing, along with strong driver-identification results.
ky1FGkigql.main_concern: The experiments barely test delayed systems (all 35 Dysts test systems are ODEs) and the realizability assumption is never verified.

KJUfTO9Ywo.one_liner: Functional ANOVA decomposition of activations plus causal interventions traces how LLMs compose relations among three cyclic-concept tokens
KJUfTO9Ywo.problem: It is unclear how relational information among input tokens is represented and processed across transformer layers.
KJUfTO9Ywo.method: Studies activations from prompt ensembles that require inferring relationships among three tokens of a cyclic concept (months, hours, weekdays, musical notes). Decomposes them with an exact functional ANOVA (with Fourier-based mode fractions, per reviewers) and tests the pairwise and three-token joint terms with ablation, replacement, and steering.
KJUfTO9Ywo.key_idea: Decompose activations with an exact orthogonal functional ANOVA to isolate joint dependence among tokens, then test which joint terms are causally used via ablation, replacement, and steering.
KJUfTO9Ywo.evidence: Llama, Qwen, Gemma, and Mistral model families across four cyclic concepts, with geometric analysis and causal interventions.
KJUfTO9Ywo.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract says restricting models to the causally relevant joint representations improves next-token prediction accuracy, without figures)
KJUfTO9Ywo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the exact, orthogonal decomposition paired with causal interventions, and the finding that some geometrically organized terms are causally inert.
KJUfTO9Ywo.main_concern: The claim of revealing the mechanism is overstated: only narrow template variants of a cyclic task are tested and it is not shown how the three-token representation is computed.

6AW6w2aEoB.one_liner: Tapered Language Models decrease MLP width monotonically across depth at a fixed parameter budget, improving perplexity and downstream accuracy
6AW6w2aEoB.problem: Language models allocate parameters uniformly across depth even though layers contribute non-uniformly to the final output.
6AW6w2aEoB.method: In a controlled fixed-budget experiment, more MLP capacity in earlier layers and less in later layers improves perplexity over uniform width, while the reverse hurts. Tapered Language Models make MLP width decrease monotonically with depth under a fixed total budget, using a smooth cosine schedule selected once on a 440M Transformer and transferred unchanged.
6AW6w2aEoB.key_idea: Reallocate MLP intermediate width from later to earlier layers along a smooth cosine schedule while holding total parameters and FLOPs fixed.
6AW6w2aEoB.evidence: Six comparisons against matched uniform baselines across three architectures (Transformer, Gated Attention, Titans) at 760M and 1.3B parameters, plus a layer-novelty analysis.
6AW6w2aEoB.claimed_gains: Tapering improves average downstream accuracy and perplexity over matched uniform baselines in all six comparisons across three architectures at 760M and 1.3B parameters, with identical parameter count and FLOPs.
6AW6w2aEoB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the controlled fixed-budget experiment clean and the gains consistent across three architectures, with the layer-novelty analysis motivating the tapering.
6AW6w2aEoB.main_concern: Some gains are small (about 0.3 points of accuracy) with unquantified variability, there is a throughput and memory cost at 1.3B, and behavior at larger scale is unknown.

untGC2eNiN.one_liner: Turns specified benchmark tasks into underspecified POMDP interactions to measure whether LLM agents identify the user's intended task.
untGC2eNiN.problem: Benchmarks evaluate execution of fully specified tasks, but real user tasks are ambiguous and the assistant must first infer the intended task.
untGC2eNiN.method: The framework converts specified tasks into interactions in which the model must infer a latent task from partial, evolving user intent through a simulated user validated post hoc with a human study. It then tests belief-state planning and post-training with supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning.
untGC2eNiN.key_idea: Hide the target task among candidates, let the assistant elicit intent through dialogue, and score task recovery with a separate probe over candidates, isolating understanding from execution.
untGC2eNiN.evidence: Shopping, coding, and professional work settings with 14 evaluated models, a human study on a random subset of tasks, and belief-state planning and SFT plus RL post-training interventions.
untGC2eNiN.claimed_gains: Models recover the user's intended task 16-22% of the time under ambiguity; humans recover 51% of intended tasks versus a 32% model average, beating 13 of 14 evaluated models.
untGC2eNiN.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating task discovery from execution is a useful, reusable evaluation design applicable to any benchmark with specified tasks, with careful probe construction and cross-domain coverage.
untGC2eNiN.main_concern: The ranking probe sees the candidates while the assistant does not, so correct ranking does not show correct commitment, and the human-versus-model comparison uses a small subset without turn counts.

4GfA56qfHi.one_liner: Controlled comparison of 10 transcriptome pretraining recipes trained on shared corpora, probed on expression, biological tasks, and RNA question answering.
4GfA56qfHi.problem: Differences in pretraining methods and training data make it hard to tell which transcriptome foundation model approach works best for a given use case.
4GfA56qfHi.method: The authors train six single-cell and four bulk models from scratch on one shared corpus per modality following literature-inspired recipes, then evaluate expression probing, five biological tasks, and RNA question answering by connecting the frozen models to Qwen. They also test whether LogME transferability scores early in pretraining predict downstream performance.
4GfA56qfHi.key_idea: Hold the pretraining corpus fixed within each modality and vary only the recipe, with untrained models and simple baselines as controls, to attribute effects to pretraining itself.
4GfA56qfHi.evidence: Ten recipes at matched depth and width, evaluated on expression probing, five biological tasks (including TCGA and PANACEA), and RNA question answering through a Qwen connection, with a retrospective LogME analysis.
4GfA56qfHi.claimed_gains: not stated; findings are qualitative (pretraining improves classification over untrained models for every recipe, but its effect on perturbation prediction is inconsistent).
4GfA56qfHi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the shared-corpus, matched-architecture design with untrained and simple baselines is a controlled way to test whether pretraining helps, and that good probing scores need not imply good biological prediction.
4GfA56qfHi.main_concern: The conclusions are hedged and partly known from prior work, and the early LogME selection result is retrospective and exploratory with only four or six recipes per comparison.

MpU3ve2c3E.one_liner: Systematic study showing how training and test negative construction changes measured performance and ranking of sequence-based PPI models.
MpU3ve2c3E.problem: Protein-protein interaction models are trained and evaluated against sampled, unobserved protein pairs treated as negatives because experimentally established non-interactions are scarce, and how this construction affects model comparison is unclear.
MpU3ve2c3E.method: Keeps positives, protein-disjoint splits, class balance, and model selection fixed while independently varying training and evaluation negatives across six constructions and four sequence-based models, three of which use protein language model representations. Partner-shuffling and pooled-embedding controls probe pair dependence.
MpU3ve2c3E.key_idea: Cross training-negative and test-negative constructions under otherwise fixed conditions so performance differences can be attributed to how negatives are built.
MpU3ve2c3E.evidence: Six negative constructions and four sequence-based models on protein-disjoint splits, plus external sources with assay non-detections or curated negatives.
MpU3ve2c3E.claimed_gains: Changing only the test negatives shifts AUPRC by up to 0.26 and changes the top-ranked architecture, and negatives matched to true partners in pLM space reduce pLM-based models to near-chance.
MpU3ve2c3E.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the study is cleanly designed and well controlled, with training and test negatives crossed so differences can be attributed to negatives, and with thorough baselines and available code.
MpU3ve2c3E.main_concern: Conclusions are not very actionable and may be partly artifacts: ESM-matched negatives are built in the same representation space the ESM-based models take as input, error bars are missing, and external results sit near chance.

m9rZUsqldV.one_liner: PC-DAPS keeps several candidate solutions in one diffusion sampling run and prunes those with low prior consistency, without ground truth.
m9rZUsqldV.problem: For ambiguous nonlinear inverse problems such as phase retrieval, diffusion samplers can lock onto measurement-consistent modes unsupported by the prior, and best-of-k evaluation hides this.
m9rZUsqldV.method: PC-DAPS, a variant of Decoupled Annealing Posterior Sampling, maintains multiple candidates in one run and, as annealing noise decreases, prunes and replaces weaker candidates by prior consistency.
m9rZUsqldV.key_idea: Keep multiple interacting candidates alive during annealing and replace those with low denoising-based prior consistency, so mode selection waits until the prior can distinguish them.
m9rZUsqldV.evidence: Nonlinear inverse problems such as phase retrieval and linear inverse problems, with reviews citing FFHQ phase retrieval outcome tables and matched mean-of-k comparisons.
m9rZUsqldV.claimed_gains: Reduces prior-inconsistent samples and improves sample quality on nonlinear inverse problems while preserving quality and diversity on linear ones; the abstract gives no numbers.
m9rZUsqldV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper exposes a real failure of DAPS hidden by ground-truth best-of-k evaluation and that the method reduces implausible reconstructions.
m9rZUsqldV.main_concern: The prior-consistency score and pruning are not validated, since pruning may discard valid low-probability modes and posterior fidelity is not shown.

ccyaUp74tp.one_liner: Trains a price-independent probe on frozen reasoning-model hidden states to predict outcome beliefs, then fits a linear stopping policy.
ccyaUp74tp.problem: Reasoning LLMs overthink, wasting tokens and sometimes replacing a correct answer with a wrong one, and stopping policies trained directly on utility are tied to one token price.
ccyaUp74tp.method: BELT trains a compact probe on frozen hidden states to predict four outcomes at each reasoning step (current answer correct, final answer correct, a correct answer appears later, final answer same as current). A linear policy on these beliefs maximizes stopping utility, accuracy minus per-token cost, so changing the price refits only the policy.
ccyaUp74tp.key_idea: Separate price-independent outcome-belief prediction from a cheap linear stopping policy so the learned representation is reused across token prices.
ccyaUp74tp.evidence: Two reasoner families (Qwen3 and OLMo3 per reviews) on math benchmarks with math-to-code transfer, compared with stopping baselines such as OSP using banked reasoning trajectories.
ccyaUp74tp.claimed_gains: not stated; the visible abstract says outcome beliefs yield higher utility than raw hidden states or features trained directly on stopping utility, and the averaged results are cut off.
ccyaUp74tp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree separating outcome prediction from price-dependent stopping control is well motivated, cuts controller training cost, and is backed by comprehensive experiments.
ccyaUp74tp.main_concern: Evaluation is narrow and offline (banked trajectories, filtered integer-answer math sets, few backbones), gains over the strongest baseline are modest, and OLMo3 is compared only with OSP-1.

F3joF1TsqO.one_liner: Flow-matching EEG generator constrained to satisfy bipolar-montage linear identities, conditioned on a physiological state vector.
F3joF1TsqO.problem: Current bipolar EEG generators violate the exact linear identities between bipolar channels, a failure hidden by reported fidelity gains.
F3joF1TsqO.method: MontageFlow is a flow-matching model whose output is restricted to signals satisfying the bipolar identities. It is also conditioned on a physiological state vector encoded from the whole EEG window, drawn at generation time from a prior fitted in latent space.
F3joF1TsqO.key_idea: Restrict the flow model's output space to signals that satisfy the bipolar-channel linear identities by construction, and condition on a window-level physiological state vector to prevent oversmoothing.
F3joF1TsqO.evidence: Three large-scale bipolar-montage benchmarks, with physiological checks (power spectrum, alpha peak, amplitude over time) and ablations per the reviews.
F3joF1TsqO.claimed_gains: Improves TS-FID by 1.6-3.0x over the closest rival across 3 benchmarks while ensuring montage consistency.
F3joF1TsqO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the paper well organized, with physiologically meaningful evaluation checks and supporting ablations.
F3joF1TsqO.main_concern: Reviewers question the premise (EEG is recorded against a common reference, so a fixed bipolar difference layer would also guarantee the identities) and note that much of the gain comes from latent conditioning rather than the montage constraint.

mJw7cMWbku.one_liner: Models multimodal loss as four summed power laws: redundancy, two unique channels and synergy, varying paired-data budget.
mJw7cMWbku.problem: Existing multimodal scaling laws fit multimodality terms empirically and never vary how much data is multimodally paired at fixed per-modality data budgets.
mJw7cMWbku.method: Models are trained in three environments with sweeps over data size and pairing budget. A new law makes total data-attributable loss the sum of four power laws, one each for redundancy, a unique channel per modality, and synergy.
mJw7cMWbku.key_idea: Decompose data-attributable loss into four information-channel power laws, with synergy gated by a critical threshold of paired data.
mJw7cMWbku.evidence: Training sweeps over data sizes and pairing budgets in three environments, including a controlled Digits task and real tasks such as VQA and NLVR2 per reviews; mainly supervised classification.
mJw7cMWbku.claimed_gains: The law predicts multimodal loss with 3.2% error on fit tests versus 10.4% error for the best pairing (abstract excerpt cuts off here).
mJw7cMWbku.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that varying the paired-example count at fixed data budgets is an important, under-explored question and that the four-channel law is interpretable and predicts better than existing laws.
mJw7cMWbku.main_concern: The link between partial information decomposition and an additive four-power-law loss is assumed rather than derived, and identifying the channels in real tasks is indirect.

6Pk3ygy5Aw.one_liner: Scaling law predicting loss from model size, tokens, rewrite fraction and natural-data epochs, charging the compute spent generating rewrites.
6Pk3ygy5Aw.problem: It is unclear how much compute to spend rewriting pretraining data and whether a model trained on rewrites can outperform its rewriter.
6Pk3ygy5Aw.method: They fit a rewriting scaling law in a compute-limited setting (a third-party rewriter trained with more compute) and a data-limited setting (a fixed seed set with a same-size rewriter pretrained on it).
6Pk3ygy5Aw.key_idea: Model loss as a function of size, tokens, rewrite fraction and epochs, with rewrite generation charged to the compute budget so the optimal fraction can be solved per budget.
6Pk3ygy5Aw.evidence: FineWeb-Edu runs in both settings, a 33x FLOPs extrapolation to a 22B-parameter model checked against the forecast, and bits-per-byte comparisons with the rewriter.
6Pk3ygy5Aw.claimed_gains: The optimal rewrite fraction rises from under 10% at 3x10^18 FLOPs to 32% at 10^22 FLOPs, and a 22B model extrapolated 33x in FLOPs lands within 1.1% of the predicted loss.
6Pk3ygy5Aw.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the framework fills a gap on rewrite mixing ratios and consider the 33x extrapolation credible given a scale-invariance check.
6Pk3ygy5Aw.main_concern: Fitted constants are specific to one rewriter and dataset, and the claim of beating the rewriter rests on the instruct checkpoint while its base model scores better.

RmyLhyL7Mu.one_liner: Two-stage agentic verifier for computer-use safety: a rubric generator, then a probing agent that inspects the post-execution environment.
RmyLhyL7Mu.problem: Verifiers using screenshots and general safety criteria miss subtle harms and cannot tell what actually changed in the environment.
RmyLhyL7Mu.method: A rubric generator reasons over the task and agent trajectory to write task-specific completion and safety rubrics. A probing agent follows the rubrics to interact with the post-execution environment, collect evidence, and judge safety and completion.
RmyLhyL7Mu.key_idea: Pair reasoning-heavy task-specific rubric generation with a tool-using agent that gathers grounded evidence from the final environment state.
RmyLhyL7Mu.evidence: Two computer-use safety benchmarks, including AutoElicit-Bench, with ablations and comparisons against passive verifiers.
RmyLhyL7Mu.claimed_gains: On AutoElicit-Bench, SCOUT achieves 75.4 unsafe F1 and 74.5 completion F1 (the comparison with baselines is truncated in the abstract).
RmyLhyL7Mu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem matters and see inspecting files and environment state with generated checklists as a sensible, simple design with promising results.
RmyLhyL7Mu.main_concern: The contribution is limited beyond orchestrating existing rubric and agentic-verification ideas, and comparisons are not fully controlled across fresh executions.

xv6L0dmyqE.one_liner: A 0.6B model extracts main content from HTML and chooses keep, edit, delete or rewrite, replacing heuristic scraping and filters.
xv6L0dmyqE.problem: Pretraining corpora cleaned by hand-written heuristics are capped by the coarseness and accuracy of the rules.
xv6L0dmyqE.method: ReScraper is trained on supervised data curated from three teacher models to extract main content from raw data, then choose among keeping the page, editing out noisy lines and spans, deleting it, or rewriting it.
xv6L0dmyqE.key_idea: One small model does extraction and cleaning together, selecting among keep, edit, delete and rewrite for each page.
xv6L0dmyqE.evidence: Pretraining 400M, 1.4B and 2.8B models on data curated from the same crawled pool, compared with rule-based, model-based and multi-agent baselines, plus analyses of each operation.
xv6L0dmyqE.claimed_gains: Improves DCLM Core score by a relative 3.8-4.7% over the strongest baseline at each of the 400M, 1.4B and 2.8B scales.
xv6L0dmyqE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the unified small curation model promising and credit downstream pretraining validation at three scales with detailed operation analyses.
xv6L0dmyqE.main_concern: One data pool is reused at different repetition levels across scales, and the student configuration appears selected on the reported DCLM metric, so margins may be inflated.

iXZZ8t2AJp.one_liner: Sparse attention via priority sampling over a black-box MIPS oracle, with bounds on how many keys must be retrieved.
iXZZ8t2AJp.problem: It is unclear how many keys a black-box MIPS oracle must retrieve to produce an epsilon-accurate attention estimate.
iXZZ8t2AJp.method: They unify prior approaches through priority sampling and prove retrieval bounds for one index, log n indices, and tradeoffs between them. They then show that augmenting keys and queries yields a simple estimator (SoftmaxLift per reviews) with one index and O(1/eps^2) keys.
iXZZ8t2AJp.key_idea: Estimate softmax attention by priority sampling of keys returned by MIPS, with key and query augmentation bypassing the single-index lower bound.
iXZZ8t2AJp.evidence: Upper and lower bounds in the black-box framework, plus LLM inference experiments against top-k and sampling baselines at 128K and 1M contexts using RULER.
iXZZ8t2AJp.claimed_gains: With one index, Theta(sqrt(n)/eps) keys are necessary and sufficient; with Theta(log n) indices, O(log n + 1/eps^2) keys suffice; with augmentation, one index and O(1/eps^2) keys suffice.
iXZZ8t2AJp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the theoretical framework with matching lower bounds and the simple SoftmaxLift estimator, which beats top-k baselines at matched retrieval budgets.
iXZZ8t2AJp.main_concern: Practical benefit is limited: at 1M context the speedup comes with a RULER drop from 85.42 to 58.33 on eight examples, and few sparse-attention baselines are compared.

Wxo2lhW3z8.one_liner: Extends proportional fairness (the core) from single partitions to whole clustering hierarchies, with existence, impossibility, and approximation results.
Wxo2lhW3z8.problem: Proportional fairness is defined only for a single partition, not for hierarchical clustering that represents data at multiple levels of granularity.
Wxo2lhW3z8.method: The paper defines the local core (proportional fairness at each split) and the global core (at every partition in the hierarchy) under maximum-loss and average-loss objectives, then proves existence and impossibility results and gives approximation algorithms that double the coalition size threshold.
Wxo2lhW3z8.key_idea: Require core stability at every split (local core) or at every partition (global core) of the hierarchy, and relax the coalition-size threshold to obtain approximations.
Wxo2lhW3z8.evidence: Theory only: existence and impossibility proofs and approximation algorithms; reviewers note there are no experiments.
Wxo2lhW3z8.claimed_gains: Under maximum loss a local-core hierarchy always exists, doubling the coalition size threshold gives a global 16-core for maximum loss and a global 8n-core for average loss, and a non-centroid clustering in the core always exists for k = 2 while for k ≥ 3 the core can be empty.
Wxo2lhW3z8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper is clearly written and gives clean theoretical results, including resolving the k = 2 existence question of Caragiannis et al. for non-centroid clustering.
Wxo2lhW3z8.main_concern: Reviewers say the paper has no experiments or demonstrated practical use, the average-loss guarantee scales with n and is vacuous for large datasets, and the k = 2 result is existential rather than constructive.

e120gKdoLF.one_liner: BFP periodically reallocates a fixed budget of protected parameter directions by estimated output influence, freeing the rest for new-task learning.
e120gKdoLF.problem: In continual learning of vision-language models, protecting historical knowledge can impose an avoidable cost on new-task learning (protection-induced plasticity loss).
e120gKdoLF.method: Protection-induced plasticity loss is measured with paired runs that start from identical model and optimizer states and differ only in retained protection. Budgeted Functional Protection (BFP) periodically reallocates a fixed number of protected directions according to their estimated influence on outputs.
e120gKdoLF.key_idea: Cap protection at a fixed rank and periodically re-pick which directions to protect by their estimated influence on model outputs, rather than accumulating protection.
e120gKdoLF.evidence: A paired-run diagnostic and VLCL benchmarks under a common training budget compared with Pi-CCA, with ten paired runs, retrieval and classification results and multiple backbones per reviews.
e120gKdoLF.claimed_gains: On VLCL, BFP improves image-to-text and text-to-image Recall@1 over Pi-CCA by 1.11 and 1.06 percentage points and reduces pretrained accuracy drop from 3.02 to 1.37 points.
e120gKdoLF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paired-run diagnostic is a well-controlled, reusable way to measure the plasticity cost of protection, and that BFP is a simple method with bounded memory cost and gains over recent baselines.
e120gKdoLF.main_concern: The stability-trap evidence rests mainly on the authors' own uncapped growing-protection variant and a narrow adaptation setting, so its existence in deployed methods is inferred, and BFP's originality over OGD, GPM and CoSO-style methods is limited.

Zia17Ahafr.one_liner: Replaces a contiguous window of tabular foundation model blocks with a closed-form, label-free affine map at little accuracy cost.
Zia17Ahafr.problem: In-context tabular foundation models stack many transformer blocks with high compute and memory cost, although tabular tasks may not need deep architectures.
Zia17Ahafr.method: A closed-form, label-free affine translator replaces a contiguous window of up to 96% of the blocks and leaves the rest unchanged; it is fitted per dataset and applied to eight tabular foundation models.
Zia17Ahafr.key_idea: Fit a closed-form affine map from teacher activations before a block window to those after it, skipping the window while keeping the remaining blocks.
Zia17Ahafr.evidence: Eight tabular foundation models evaluated on 171 classification datasets, with controls that drop the same blocks without the map, three seeds, and an appendix comparison to GBDTs.
Zia17Ahafr.claimed_gains: Replacing half of a model's blocks costs at most 0.002 median AUROC across all architectures, and up to 96% of blocks can be replaced.
Zia17Ahafr.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the study has a clear scope, strong controls, multi-family evidence and useful ablations showing the compression result is consistent.
Zia17Ahafr.main_concern: The 'effectively shallow' claim exceeds the evidence: the affine map is fitted per task, transfers poorly across schemas, and the study does not explain why it works.

JqpwsHYBW6.one_liner: Derives PAC-Bayesian generalisation bounds for physics-informed learning whose complexity scales with the input-gradient energy of each loss.
JqpwsHYBW6.problem: Generalisation of physics-informed machine learning with unbounded losses is poorly understood, and existing analyses do not capture how physical structure affects learning from finite data.
JqpwsHYBW6.method: They build component-wise PAC-Bayes bounds with a calibration procedure that gives computable input-gradient complexities and a residual-tail correction for rare large-gradient events, then treat data fidelity, PDE residual, initial and boundary conditions jointly with one complexity penalty.
JqpwsHYBW6.key_idea: Bound each loss's generalisation gap by its input-gradient energy, with a tail correction for rare large gradients and one shared PAC-Bayes penalty across components.
JqpwsHYBW6.evidence: Experiments on six types of PDEs with diagnostics and ablations (e.g., sample size) compare the bounds against bounded-loss and sub-Gaussian certificates, as described in the reviews.
JqpwsHYBW6.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper is clearly written, handles unbounded losses, and links generalisation complexity to input-gradient energy with extensive diagnostics.
JqpwsHYBW6.main_concern: Technical novelty over the existing empirical input-gradient PAC-Bayes bound of Casado et al. 2024 is unclear, and the guarantee rests on population-level assumptions that cannot be verified from finite samples.

8cy4HA8wRa.one_liner: Personalized federated co-training that adapts reliance on collaboration per client and weights client predictions at the example level.
8cy4HA8wRa.problem: Many personalized FL methods fail to beat local and centralized baselines under data heterogeneity, leaving unclear when and whom clients should trust.
8cy4HA8wRa.method: FEDMOSAIC is a personalized federated co-training method that dynamically balances local and collaborative objectives and weights client contributions at the example level, with a convergence analysis and a client-level differentially private variant.
8cy4HA8wRa.key_idea: Each client adaptively sets how strongly it relies on a consensus of peers' predictions, and each peer's contribution is weighted per example by an expertise score.
