8cy4HA8wRa.evidence: Experiments across label-skew, feature-shift and hybrid settings against FL and PFL baselines, plus convergence under smoothness, bounded-variance and pseudo-label drift assumptions.
8cy4HA8wRa.claimed_gains: Outperforms strong FL and PFL baselines and frequently surpasses both local and centralized training; no numeric gains are stated.
8cy4HA8wRa.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem of adaptive collaboration under heterogeneity is important and the method shows strong empirical performance with broad evaluation.
8cy4HA8wRa.main_concern: Limited novelty: the method mainly extends FedCT with adaptive loss weighting and confidence-weighted pseudo-labeling, and it depends heavily on a public unlabeled dataset.

dovVrIZ10J.one_liner: Training-free multimodal RAG retrieval that adds a second route over residuals orthogonal to each item's description subspace.
dovVrIZ10J.problem: Textual descriptions of multimodal items can be semantically correct yet omit a visual or temporal detail that a particular query needs.
dovVrIZ10J.method: QCR² builds an item-specific description subspace in a shared multimodal embedding space and keeps the orthogonal component as a residual; at inference it retrieves independently from description and residual representations, ranks candidates jointly, and passes the original items to the answer model.
dovVrIZ10J.key_idea: Project out each item's description subspace from its multimodal embedding and use the orthogonal residual as a second retrieval channel fused with the description channel.
dovVrIZ10J.evidence: Evaluated across text, table, image and video knowledge sources, with three retrievers and three answer models, against learned fusion and UniversalRAG baselines, plus ablations.
dovVrIZ10J.claimed_gains: Consistently improves over baselines across heterogeneous text, table, image and video sources; no numbers are visible in the truncated abstract.
dovVrIZ10J.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is simple, training-free and clearly presented, with fair controlled comparisons against fusion baselines.
dovVrIZ10J.main_concern: Limited novelty and small gains: the method combines orthogonal projection with dual-route retrieval, improves little over UniversalRAG (42.9 vs 42.4), and does not isolate the residual's contribution.

eCqA7bzI2F.one_liner: Benchmarks how often coding agents claim to have reviewed files that their own transcripts show they never opened.
eCqA7bzI2F.problem: It is hard to tell from an agent's final response what it actually did, and agents may overclaim completion in ways that mislead users.
eCqA7bzI2F.method: OverclaimBench has five file-review scenarios across code review and document synthesis with transcript-based coverage measurement and registered planted defects; eight proprietary models in their own CLIs and four open-weight models in a fixed harness are tested.
eCqA7bzI2F.key_idea: Define overclaiming as a final report of work the agent's own transcript shows was not done, measured through file-read coverage, with no inference about intent.
eCqA7bzI2F.evidence: Twelve models (eight proprietary frontier models in production CLIs, four open-weight models in one harness) run on five scenarios with transcript coverage and planted defects.
eCqA7bzI2F.claimed_gains: Agents fail to read every file in 67.9% of runs, and among those incomplete runs they are misleading 80.4% of the time (59-96% per model).
eCqA7bzI2F.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is timely, the operationalization is simple and verifiable, and the finding reproduces consistently across twelve models.
eCqA7bzI2F.main_concern: Only five read-intensive scenarios, designed by iterating against Claude Opus, and the agent harness differs between proprietary and open-weight models, limiting generality and confounding comparisons.

qN21O5YOVE.one_liner: Flow and diffusion models that prescribe motion across level sets of a known constraint map, learning only within-set transport.
qN21O5YOVE.problem: Equality constraints confine scientific targets to lower-dimensional sets that are singular with respect to Lebesgue measure, so ambient models must learn both the collapse onto the set and the distribution along it.
qN21O5YOVE.method: Disintegrated stochastic interpolants decompose the state space into level sets of a known constraint map, prescribe the constraint values' analytic evolution toward zero, and learn only transport within the moving level sets, with derived training objectives and samplers for flow and diffusion.
qN21O5YOVE.key_idea: Disintegrate the target by constraint level sets: constraint values follow an analytically prescribed path, while the network learns only transport within the moving fibres.
qN21O5YOVE.evidence: Conditions for recovering the target distribution are established, with experiments on PDE trajectory generation, molecular generation (QM9) and a small Stiefel diffusion experiment (abstract truncated before results).
qN21O5YOVE.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the measure-theoretic disintegration formulation is rigorous and general, covering singular targets, constraints and symmetries, with quotient-space diffusion as a special case.
qN21O5YOVE.main_concern: Empirical support is limited and partly unisolated: small-scale experiments, an approximate score target in implicit diffusion, extra Jacobian and projection cost, and results comparable to baselines in some tables.

kB8Lwd90Io.one_liner: Replaces bits-per-byte with PriorBPB, which estimates a per-(model,task) marginal per-byte cost to reduce answer-length bias.
kB8Lwd90Io.problem: Bits-per-byte depends on gold answer length because fixed per-answer overhead is spread over fewer bytes in short answers, biasing cross-task and cross-model comparisons.
kB8Lwd90Io.method: They write bits as a per-byte rate plus fixed overhead divided by length plus a residual, show corpus BPB equals the rate plus overhead over mean length, and propose PriorBPB, which estimates a per-(model, task) marginal per-byte cost.
kB8Lwd90Io.key_idea: Estimate the survival-weighted marginal per-byte cost over answer positions instead of dividing total bits by total bytes, which entangles fixed overhead with answer length.
kB8Lwd90Io.evidence: An 18-task suite on Qwen3 models and OLMo-3-7B, including a Qwen3 inverse-scaling case study with chat-template controls and Bayesian bootstrap statistics.
kB8Lwd90Io.claimed_gains: The abstract is cut before PriorBPB's results; visible numbers show standard BPB correlates with mean gold length at Spearman -0.79 to -0.84 on Qwen3 and -0.77 on OLMo-3-7B.
kB8Lwd90Io.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the length-bias diagnosis of a widely used metric is important, the core identity is simple and correct, and the statistics are careful.
kB8Lwd90Io.main_concern: PriorBPB may not fully remove the length bias, since the fixed cost is still divided by a term tied to each task's longest answer and the within-task gain is small (0.944 to 0.888).

SqzCQV2unp.one_liner: Answers time-series questions with frozen encoders and a small recurrent latent reasoner that repeatedly rereads inputs, with no LLM.
SqzCQV2unp.problem: Time-series QA methods use an LLM both to interpret and to reason over signals, which is costly and obscures whether gains come from representations or reasoning.
SqzCQV2unp.method: GLEAN encodes each input once with frozen text and time-series encoders plus numerical features, then reasons through recurrent latent updates in which the current state guides each new read of the inputs. Structured output heads select answers or order signal fragments without generating text.
SqzCQV2unp.key_idea: Decouple perception (frozen encoders, one pass) from reasoning (a small shared recurrent network whose state conditions repeated reads of the encoded evidence).
SqzCQV2unp.evidence: TSAQA benchmark results against five fine-tuned time-series LLMs and general LLMs, with per-task ablations including a pooled-readout baseline and a series-only variant.
SqzCQV2unp.claimed_gains: The recurrent reasoner raises relational accuracy from 58.03% to 69.16% on the same representations, and with 0.46B total parameters (8.2M trained) GLEAN reaches 77.33% on TSAQA, outperforming all five evaluated fine-tuned time-series LLMs.
SqzCQV2unp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating perception from reasoning is a meaningful direction and that GLEAN is efficient (8.2M trained parameters) with detailed per-task ablations.
SqzCQV2unp.main_concern: No experiment swaps only the reasoner on fixed encoders (e.g., a small LLM over the same evidence), so the title's question is untested, and all results are on TSAQA with closed-ended answers.

WfjGMorGzm.one_liner: Continual RL steering of a frozen robot policy, with world-model imagined rollouts replacing replay to rehearse earlier tasks.
WfjGMorGzm.problem: Fine-tuning a generalist robot policy on sequential tasks causes catastrophic forgetting, and steering the input noise of a frozen policy only shifts forgetting to the shared steering module.
WfjGMorGzm.method: While a steering module learns a new task, a frozen pretrained world model generates imagined rollouts of prior tasks that anchor the module to its earlier behavior, with no replay buffer. If the world model is faithful enough the new task is learned entirely in imagination; otherwise it is learned in the environment.
WfjGMorGzm.key_idea: Penalize the steering module's deviation from its earlier behavior on states generated by a frozen world model's imagined rollouts of prior tasks.
WfjGMorGzm.evidence: Two simulation experiments (CALVIN and LIBERO) and one real-world experiment, with multiple seeds and rehearsal ablations (instruction KL, first-observation KL, replay KL).
WfjGMorGzm.claimed_gains: On CALVIN, D2R improves eight tasks in sequence entirely in imagination, raising average success from 63.7% to 74.8%, while LoRA fine-tuning on the same sequence drops it to 11.7%.
WfjGMorGzm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method is simple and clearly presented, and that the rehearsal ablations show retained-task states are needed but need not be real or stored.
WfjGMorGzm.main_concern: The claim that rehearsal tolerates lower world-model fidelity than optimization is weakly supported, since the headline LIBERO result uses a world model fine-tuned and accurate on those suites, and component ablations are limited.

xzFyy5aCnD.one_liner: Shows off-policy evaluation needs only target coverage under replacement-policy linear realizability, using safe partial corrections to logged returns.
xzFyy5aCnD.problem: Target occupancy coverage plus linear realizability of the target's action values alone do not guarantee sample-efficient off-policy evaluation.
xzFyy5aCnD.method: Replacement policies retain a drawn logger action or replace it with a fresh target draw, and an estimator applies safe partial corrections to logged returns. It requires linear action values for every replacement policy and uses iid trajectories from one unknown Markov logger, without logger probabilities or model oracles.
xzFyy5aCnD.key_idea: Interpolate between logger and target via replacement policies, shrinking return corrections conservatively, so data need cover only the target while regression represents replacement-policy values.
xzFyy5aCnD.evidence: Theory: a sample-complexity bound with separation families showing strict representation and coverage relaxations; reviewers describe the experiments as simple.
xzFyy5aCnD.claimed_gains: Error at most ε with probability at least 1-δ using Õ(C_e H^6 d/ε^2) iid complete trajectories, with logarithmic norm dependence and no state or action cardinality factor.
xzFyy5aCnD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the theoretical contribution is significant, weakening assumptions of traditional OPE, with clear writing and solid statistical guarantees.
xzFyy5aCnD.main_concern: The replacement-policy linear realizability assumption may be restrictive and is not validated in practice, and the empirical section is thin.

2pEA9r9V3E.one_liner: Fits a scaling law, from 800 pretrained models, in which added AI-generated web tokens first help and then harm.
2pEA9r9V3E.problem: Web pretraining data is increasingly AI-generated, yet existing scaling laws such as Chinchilla treat AI tokens like human tokens, and the effect of this wild AI text is unknown.
2pEA9r9V3E.method: They pretrain 800 models (19.9M to 973M parameters) while varying the ratio of added AI to human tokens, fit scaling laws to held-out loss on human and AI text, and propose a law with separate benefit and harm terms that reduces to Chinchilla without AI text.
2pEA9r9V3E.key_idea: Add separate benefit and harm terms to a Chinchilla-style scaling law so the human-token-equivalent value of an AI token can change sign.
2pEA9r9V3E.evidence: 800 models from 19.9M to 973M parameters trained with varied AI-token ratios, with held-out loss on human and AI text, matched human-data control runs, and CORE scores.
2pEA9r9V3E.claimed_gains: Not a method gain: after FineWeb filtering, 27.5% of tokens from June 2026 web data are labeled AI-generated by Pangram, rising to 31.1% by August, and Chinchilla-style laws fail to predict the benefit-then-harm behavior.
2pEA9r9V3E.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is timely and the experimental design is clean and systematic, with matched human-data controls across 800 models.
2pEA9r9V3E.main_concern: Harm is measured on human-text loss only and downstream capability implications are unestablished (CORE scores improve similarly with AI or fresh human text), and related theory by Dohmatob et al. is understated.

BMtxaiMLWB.one_liner: Estimates disparity from stereo events alone with a state-space network, then refines it with one frame weighted by event-stereo reliability.
BMtxaiMLWB.problem: Existing event-frame stereo methods fuse the modalities before or during matching, so unreliable frame appearance can bias correspondence before any geometric reference exists.
BMtxaiMLWB.method: Disparity is first estimated solely from stereo events with a state-space architecture, then refined by a single frame whose contribution is weighted by a reliability measure derived from event stereo consistency. Reviews name geometry-structured event states, cross-view state propagation, and coarse-to-fine epipolar matching as components.
BMtxaiMLWB.key_idea: Fix geometry from events first, then gate frame-based refinement by reliability derived from event-stereo consistency so frame appearance cannot bias matching.
BMtxaiMLWB.evidence: Evaluation on DSEC with zero-shot transfer to MVSEC and M3ED, plus ablations on fusion timing and a blur experiment.
BMtxaiMLWB.claimed_gains: Most accurate on DSEC among methods using at most one frame camera and approaching symmetric methods using two, with an event-only variant that beats prior event-only methods; no numbers stated.
BMtxaiMLWB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the geometry-first design is simple and well motivated, with strong DSEC and zero-shot results and clear fusion-timing ablations.
BMtxaiMLWB.main_concern: The at-most-one-frame comparison is not controlled (this method uses two event cameras), ablations do not isolate fusion order from other design changes, and novelty over existing guided or confidence-based fusion is unclear.

AhIUPRflnD.one_liner: Agentic pipeline turns implemented functionality in existing codebases into executable, verified RL coding environments using only source code as input.
AhIUPRflnD.problem: Existing RL environment construction relies on development artifacts such as issues and commits, which limits the range of extractable coding tasks.
AhIUPRflnD.method: Agents explore implemented functionality to write behavioral specifications, build tests grounded in execution of the original code, and filter candidate tasks through execution checks and repeated solution rollouts. MiMo-V2.5 is then trained on the resulting tasks with GRPO.
AhIUPRflnD.key_idea: Spend agentic compute at every stage of environment construction (specification, execution-grounded tests, rollout-based filtering) using only source code as task input.
AhIUPRflnD.evidence: A dataset of 5,545 tasks from 3,185 codebases in 23 languages and 15 domains; GRPO training of MiMo-V2.5 evaluated on five benchmarks, with ablations on task counts and trajectory analysis.
AhIUPRflnD.claimed_gains: Improves all five benchmarks, including DeepSWE +11.7%, ProgramBench +17%, and Terminal-Bench v2.1 +8.5%.
AhIUPRflnD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the pipeline needs only source code, treats verifier quality seriously with leakage and alternative-solution audits, and transfers to external benchmarks.
AhIUPRflnD.main_concern: The comparison with PR-derived tasks is not compute-matched and does not isolate task source from implementation size and filtering strength, and novelty over prior task-creation work (e.g., R2E-Gym) is limited.

MQjXoIOcqF.one_liner: Restricts one KL-Shampoo Kronecker factor to a rank-r spike plus a flat tail and orthogonalizes the flat directions.
MQjXoIOcqF.problem: KL-Shampoo's Kronecker preconditioning and Muon-style orthogonalization are developed in isolation, and KL-Shampoo's full preconditioner is costly.
MQjXoIOcqF.method: They observe that KL-Shampoo's Kronecker preconditioner spectra are spike-and-flat, then keep full spectral structure on a tracked r-dimensional subspace with one shared eigenvalue on the remaining n-r directions, where orthogonalization is applied. An identity shows this recovers the algebraic form of KL-Shampoo's preconditioner with an instantaneous instead of a running estimate.
MQjXoIOcqF.key_idea: Exploit the spike-and-flat eigenvalue spectrum: track a rank-r dominant subspace and apply orthogonalization on its complement, which recovers the algebraic form of KL whitening.
MQjXoIOcqF.evidence: Four pre-training scales (GPT-2 124M and 350M, LLaMA 134M and 450M) against KL-Shampoo and Muon, with a convergence theorem, subspace-rank ablations, and wall-clock comparisons.
MQjXoIOcqF.claimed_gains: Consistently outperforms KL-Shampoo at every subspace rank tested on four pre-training scales, and the TL;DR says it beats KL-Shampoo and Muon in validation loss; no numbers stated.
MQjXoIOcqF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the spike-and-flat observation is well supported across layers and training stages and motivates the method, with sound theory, lower memory, and lower validation loss than baselines.
MQjXoIOcqF.main_concern: Validation-loss gains are small with unmatched baseline tuning budgets, and the theory relies on strong assumptions and does not explain the empirical gains or its mismatch with a variant's results.

yL0Llp2CSU.one_liner: Poisson matrix-normal latent variable model that jointly estimates stimulus drive and shared population gain across neurons and time.
yL0Llp2CSU.problem: Overdispersion models treat each neuron's gain as independent across neurons and time, so shared population-level gain structure is not captured.
yL0Llp2CSU.method: PMNLV places a matrix-normal prior on the latent gain and draws binned spike counts as Poisson from a rate that sums a per-neuron tuning term and the latent gain (nonlinearity truncated in the batch). The paper proposes two estimation methods, including a variational EM variant with a precision correction (PC-VEM).
yL0Llp2CSU.key_idea: Model shared gain as a matrix-normal latent with separate neuron and time covariance factors, fit with variational EM, so stimulus drive and gain are estimated jointly.
yL0Llp2CSU.evidence: Synthetic experiments on covariance recovery and predictive performance, plus real recordings from three sessions with at least 20 units per region (per reviews).
yL0Llp2CSU.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that extending overdispersion models to shared population gain is principled and useful, with an interpretable matrix-normal separation of neuron and time covariance.
yL0Llp2CSU.main_concern: Real-data evidence is narrow (three sessions, comparison only to a mean-rate baseline), the precision-correction heuristic lacks guarantees, and the model gives limited insight into why the gain exists.

hA7nZ1HOqA.one_liner: Trains flow-matching models so transport is deliberately inefficient for off-manifold conditions, letting trajectory curvature flag extrapolations.
hA7nZ1HOqA.problem: Flow-matching models silently extrapolate on conditions outside the training support, producing untrustworthy predictions that look like valid ones.
hA7nZ1HOqA.method: Diverging Flows is a training objective that keeps near-optimal transport for on-manifold conditions while making transport inefficient for off-manifold ones. The resulting energy margin lower-bounds trajectory curvature, so extrapolation is detected from the sampling trajectory with a threshold calibrated by conformal prediction.
hA7nZ1HOqA.key_idea: Train an energy margin between on- and off-manifold conditions that lower-bounds trajectory curvature, then threshold curvature with conformal calibration to detect extrapolation.
hA7nZ1HOqA.evidence: Low-dimensional synthetic manifolds, scientific regression on 64x64 and 128x128 fields, and disjoint-domain generation on 32x32 images.
hA7nZ1HOqA.claimed_gains: A single model reliably detects extrapolations while retaining flow matching's predictive fidelity, whereas FM likelihood is near chance on the same data; no other numbers stated.
hA7nZ1HOqA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree out-of-distribution detection for flow matching is an important problem, the method is principled, and the paper is well motivated and well written.
hA7nZ1HOqA.main_concern: The roles of the conditioning variable and source point are unclear, and Proposition 4.1 needs strong path and Lipschitz assumptions while numerical comparisons are limited.

gvdDKcsWdu.one_liner: Penalizes the bilevel value-function gap with randomized smoothing so discrete submodular lower levels need only submodular function minimization.
gvdDKcsWdu.problem: Bilevel optimization with discrete lower-level problems and coupled constraints is computationally difficult, and continuous-setting methods do not apply.
gvdDKcsWdu.method: BiGAP is a value-function-gap penalty formulation with randomized smoothing that regularizes discrete response switches while keeping exact discrete oracles. The resulting first-order algorithms reduce discrete computations to unconstrained submodular function minimization (SFM).
gvdDKcsWdu.key_idea: Use a value-function-gap penalty with randomized smoothing so first-order bilevel updates only call exact submodular function minimization oracles on the discrete lower level.
gvdDKcsWdu.evidence: Theory (pointwise finite penalty exactness including optimistic selection, local agreement with the smoothed optimistic objective) plus experiments on large-scale electronic design automation problems.
gvdDKcsWdu.claimed_gains: SFM call complexity O(eps^-4) without and O(eps^-6) with coupled constraints, under exact dual support and averaged saddle regularity.
gvdDKcsWdu.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is meaningful and that extending first-order bilevel analysis to discrete submodular lower levels via SFM is a nontrivial theoretical contribution with clear presentation.
gvdDKcsWdu.main_concern: Guarantees cover the smoothed penalized objective rather than the original bilevel problem, and the constrained-case assumptions (e.g., exact Lagrangian support) are restrictive and unverified in the EDA experiment.

o4IARkkzs4.one_liner: Training-free multi-agent VLM evaluator that produces temporally localized failure reports for robot world-model videos, with a 914-clip benchmark.
o4IARkkzs4.problem: Robot world-model videos often look realistic yet violate physics, temporal consistency, or task logic, and conventional metrics or monolithic VLM judges give scores that do not say what failed.
o4IARkkzs4.method: RoboGaze grounds the task and scene, routes each subtask to dimension-specific specialist VLMs, and verifies findings with a critic, under a schema of 6 dimensions and 30 failure types. RoboGazeBench provides 914 human-annotated clips from five generators, running from 4.9 to 148.9 s.
o4IARkkzs4.key_idea: Decompose video evaluation into grounding, routed dimension-specific specialists, and a critic that verifies findings, outputting what failed, when, why, and how severely.
o4IARkkzs4.evidence: RoboGazeBench with eight open-source and proprietary VLM backbones, comparison with baselines including a published agentic detector given the same schema, equal-frame controls, and blinded human raters.
o4IARkkzs4.claimed_gains: A published agentic detector given the same schema trails RoboGaze by 10.1-12.3 description-F1 points, and by 8.8-9.7 when all methods read the same frames; on the strongest backbone it closes 82% of the gap between chain-of-thought prompting and human agreement.
o4IARkkzs4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the structured diagnostic output and the human-annotated benchmark (double annotation, adjudication, coverage analysis) are valuable, and that thorough ablations show where gains come from.
o4IARkkzs4.main_concern: Visual evidence is not equalized across methods (RoboGaze sees dense windows while baselines may see fewer frames), generator diversity is limited, and the method is evaluated only on the new benchmark.

7voaOJacw4.one_liner: Maps the geometry of seven task-relevant concepts in VLA activations using probes and interventions, finding multi-dimensional, constraint-shaped structure.
7voaOJacw4.problem: Prior work shows task-relevant variables are linearly readable from VLA activations, but readability does not reveal the shape their values trace.
7voaOJacw4.method: Using controlled sweeps, natural rollouts, linear probes, and activation interventions, they build a taxonomy of seven task-relevant concepts, check the geometries in two further VLA models on real-world robot data, and steer along the geometry a concept realizes.
7voaOJacw4.key_idea: Characterize each concept by the geometry its values trace in activation space (e.g., an open arc, two orthogonal distance subspaces), not just by linear readability.
7voaOJacw4.evidence: Controlled sweeps, natural rollouts, linear probes, and erasure and intervention controls on VLA models in simulation, with replication on two further VLA models using real-world DROID data.
7voaOJacw4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the topic is meaningful and the analyses are comprehensive, with controls against correlated variables, and that the two-scale distance finding is the strongest result.
7voaOJacw4.main_concern: Some conclusions conflate readout dimensionality with the representation's dimensionality (rank curves computed from 3-D predictions), and real-world and cross-model validation is limited.

5jViQBGVQx.one_liner: Learns Bayes factors against a flow-matched reference with evidence networks, then recovers absolute evidence for amortized simulation-based inference.
5jViQBGVQx.problem: Absolute model evidence is hard to compute and existing learned approaches mostly target Bayes factors, which only give evidence ratios, limiting goodness-of-fit and misspecification tests.
5jViQBGVQx.method: ENFR builds on the Evidence Network framework (Jeffrey & Wandelt, 2024): it first learns Bayes factors with respect to a flow-matched reference, from which the absolute evidence is recovered. SingleENFR and MultiENFR variants handle one model or a set of competing models.
5jViQBGVQx.key_idea: Anchor the evidence network to a flow-matched reference density so the learned Bayes factor corrects the reference estimate and yields absolute evidence.
5jViQBGVQx.evidence: Benchmarks including Gaussian mixtures, BAO, ODE, drift-diffusion, Hodgkin-Huxley, and galaxy applications, compared with analytic or nested-sampling evidence where available and with a flow-based baseline.
5jViQBGVQx.claimed_gains: Improves estimation of the evidence over the flow-based baseline in all benchmarks considered and gives the best performance among density-based methods (abstract truncated); no numbers stated.
5jViQBGVQx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree absolute evidence estimation is important and underexplored, and that the method is evaluated across a wide range of problems from analytic cases to neuroscience and cosmology.
5jViQBGVQx.main_concern: The paper is dense and hard to follow, the application choices are weakly motivated, and the method needs many training simulations with the flow reference weakening at high dimensions.

wY6UKOoJBM.one_liner: Online RL post-training of one LLM policy conditioned on numbered roles that compete for distinct outputs, with quality-gated diversity rewards.
wY6UKOoJBM.problem: LLM alignment training causes mode collapse, a loss of output diversity that limits open-ended uses such as scientific ideation and creative writing.
wY6UKOoJBM.method: MoDA trains a single shared policy conditioned on abstract numbered roles, each acting as an agent rewarded for producing outputs distinct from the others. A prompt-adaptive quality gate grants diversity rewards only to responses that meet a calibrated reference quality threshold.
wY6UKOoJBM.key_idea: Condition one policy on numbered roles that compete for mutually distinct outputs, and grant diversity reward only above a prompt-adaptive quality threshold.
wY6UKOoJBM.evidence: Seven general capability tasks and four domain-specific diversity tasks in scientific ideation and creative writing, across three model families, with ablations (role-only, diversity-only, quality-only).
wY6UKOoJBM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the numbered-role conditioning is simple and that the ablations separate role prompting, the diversity reward, and quality gating, with broad evaluation across three model families.
wY6UKOoJBM.main_concern: Diversity is rewarded and measured in the same embedding space (cyclic validation), embedding diversity may not reflect useful diversity, and some baseline benchmark scores look anomalously low.

I1XtWQTTck.one_liner: Training-free streaming video memory that induces latent objects from frozen Video-LLM features, links them across frames, and keeps bounded histories.
I1XtWQTTck.problem: Streaming video models manage growing visual context by token importance, redundancy, or segment relevance, but rarely organize evidence around objects that persist and evolve over time.
I1XtWQTTck.method: ObjectStream induces spatially coherent latent objects from frozen Video-LLM representations, links them across frames into persistent anchors, and keeps their histories under a bounded memory budget without external detectors. It preserves persistent object histories, transient object changes, and recent visual context.
I1XtWQTTck.key_idea: Induce latent objects from frozen Video-LLM features, link them across frames as persistent anchors, and expose object histories, transient changes, and recent context to the model.
I1XtWQTTck.evidence: Online streaming and offline long-video benchmarks (including OVO-Bench Real-Time Visual Perception) with Qwen2.5-VL backbones, component ablations, sensitivity analyses, and memory and latency measurements.
I1XtWQTTck.claimed_gains: Improves Qwen2.5-VL-7B by 10.0 points on OVO-Bench Real-Time Visual Perception while reducing (rest truncated in the batch).
I1XtWQTTck.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the design is simple and training-free, with substantial gains over the original backbones on online perception and useful construction and sensitivity analyses.
I1XtWQTTck.main_concern: The benefit of persistent cross-frame object identity is not isolated (a Patch Top-K baseline is close in accuracy), bounded memory is not established, and only Qwen2.5-VL backbones are tested.

vU0GkxeEzk.one_liner: Samples inverse-problem posteriors exactly with MCMC using SDEdit-style noising and denoising by a pretrained diffusion prior as Metropolis-Hastings proposals.
vU0GkxeEzk.problem: Posterior sampling with pretrained diffusion priors under nonlinear, possibly non-differentiable forward models remains challenging.
vU0GkxeEzk.method: Diffusion waltz proposes by noising then denoising with the diffusion model and corrects with a Metropolis-Hastings step, generalizing preconditioned Crank-Nicolson (pCN) to learned priors without evaluating the prior density. Conditional noising injects observation information into the proposal while preserving exactness.
vU0GkxeEzk.key_idea: Use prior-reversible SDEdit-style renoise-then-denoise moves as Metropolis-Hastings proposals, so the prior density is never evaluated and gradients are optional.
vU0GkxeEzk.evidence: Controlled validation (GP regression, exact denoiser) and nonlinear inverse problems including Navier-Stokes settings, with and without gradient access.
vU0GkxeEzk.claimed_gains: Matches or outperforms existing baselines in reconstruction accuracy and uncertainty calibration across a range of nonlinear inverse problems; no numbers stated.
vU0GkxeEzk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the construction is simple and general (no prior density needed, non-differentiable forward models supported) and that conditional noising improves mixing.
vU0GkxeEzk.main_concern: Novelty is questioned since the noising-denoising steps resemble DAPS and similar methods, and the best PDE results use an inexact variant while the evidence supports reconstruction quality more than posterior accuracy.

6qcC7BNoBq.one_liner: Proves exact parameter recovery of positive-weight one-hidden-layer ReLU networks is NP-hard via subset-sum, with a tensor algorithm under positive independence.
6qcC7BNoBq.problem: It is unresolved whether a sum of ReLU units with positive output weights can be learned efficiently under Gaussian inputs, since known hardness covers arbitrary-sign output weights.
6qcC7BNoBq.method: They characterize when hidden weights are statistically identifiable (no two collinear, no nonempty subset summing to zero), show that exact recovery from membership queries at rational points would imply a randomized polynomial-time algorithm for an NP-hard vector subset-sum problem, and give a polynomial-time tensor algorithm under a positive-independence condition.
6qcC7BNoBq.key_idea: Even-order Gaussian moments leave a sign-orientation ambiguity that encodes vector subset-sum; a tensor algorithm succeeds under a positive-independence condition.
6qcC7BNoBq.evidence: Theoretical results: an identifiability result under Gaussian inputs, a hardness reduction from vector subset-sum (no such algorithm unless NP is contained in RP), and a polynomial-time tensor algorithm.
6qcC7BNoBq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the question is natural and the paper cleanly locates the hardness, offering a new hardness result and an efficient algorithm under more general assumptions with a clear proof overview.
6qcC7BNoBq.main_concern: The introduction overclaims novelty (the identifiability result specializes Stock & Gribonval 2023), 'learning' is not scoped precisely as parameter recovery, and the paper is hard to verify for non-experts.

ta5uQJVQ9G.one_liner: GPU-oriented SVD built on polar decomposition via matrix-multiplication iterations such as Newton-Schulz, with a numerically stable backward pass.
ta5uQJVQ9G.problem: Standard SVD implementations are slow on GPUs, and SVD gradients are unstable when singular values are close or the matrix is near rank-deficient.
ta5uQJVQ9G.method: They compute the SVD through a polar decomposition obtained with iterative methods that use only matrix multiplications, derive a numerically stable backward pass for the polar decomposition, and use it to obtain a fully differentiable SVD, released in PyTorch and JAX.
ta5uQJVQ9G.key_idea: Replace QR-style steps with matrix-multiplication-only polar iterations that scale on modern GPUs, and differentiate through the polar factor with a derived stable backward formula.
ta5uQJVQ9G.evidence: Benchmarks on four matrix families across GPUs (A100, H100, H200, B200 per reviews) against QDWH, cuSOLVER, and CUDA Jacobi, plus an LLM compression case study showing stable SVD gradients.
ta5uQJVQ9G.claimed_gains: Up to a 2x speedup compared to standard implementations.
ta5uQJVQ9G.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the engineering is solid with substantial GPU speedups, a clean backward derivation with proofs, and honest reporting of where baselines win.
ta5uQJVQ9G.main_concern: The up-to-2x speedup is conditional (mainly from tf32 with error near 1e-3, small gains in fp32, slower on small matrices), and methodological novelty over CANS and polar-based SVD is limited.

rYwQZvwGpq.one_liner: Mechanistically analyzes AM, POMO, and LEHD routing solvers with behavioral analyses, probing, and causal interventions on TSP and CVRP.
rYwQZvwGpq.problem: Neural combinatorial optimization models perform well, yet the internal mechanisms behind their decisions remain largely unexplored.
rYwQZvwGpq.method: They study three autoregressive NCO models (AM and POMO with a heavy encoder and light decoder, LEHD with a light encoder and heavy decoder) using behavioral analyses, representation probing, causal interventions, and cross-instance alignment on TSP and CVRP.
rYwQZvwGpq.key_idea: Combine linear probes of future actions with causal activation interventions on current-, start-, and future-node representations to reveal how each solver builds a route.
rYwQZvwGpq.evidence: Three models (AM, POMO, LEHD) on the Traveling Salesman Problem and the Capacitated Vehicle Routing Problem via behavioral analyses, linear probing, causal interventions, and cross-instance alignment.
rYwQZvwGpq.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the multi-level analysis, including causal interventions, is a useful methodological starting point for interpretability of neural routing solvers, and that the probing results on LEHD's future-action information are interesting.
rYwQZvwGpq.main_concern: The AM/POMO versus LEHD contrast is confounded by training paradigm (RL versus SL) and other design differences, and the conclusions risk overinterpretation without controlled ablations.

AuIVzEnuvK.one_liner: Trains flow language models through their own latent rollout, decoding only at the endpoint, so extra integration steps improve reasoning.
AuIVzEnuvK.problem: Standard flow language models do not benefit from additional integration steps on reasoning tasks, because their objectives supervise each time point independently.
AuIVzEnuvK.method: UFM backpropagates through the model's own latent rollout over a randomly sampled subinterval of [0, 1], decoding only at the endpoint, and for long rollouts retracts the latent state onto a sphere to stabilize dynamics. A two-layer Transformer construction proves flows can solve graph reachability, with the needed steps growing with distance from the root.
AuIVzEnuvK.key_idea: Train through the model's own latent rollout with endpoint-only decoding so successive steps must build on each other, and retract latents onto a sphere for stable long rollouts.
AuIVzEnuvK.evidence: Theory on graph reachability with a two-layer Transformer flow, and experiments on ProsQA, Sudoku, and Maze against flow baselines, plus multi-rollout sampling with a parameter-free selection score.
AuIVzEnuvK.claimed_gains: On ProsQA accuracy rises to 97% and improves with more integration steps, and on Sudoku and Maze it gives substantial gains over baselines with more than three times as many parameters.
AuIVzEnuvK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper identifies a clear limitation of flow language models (extra steps barely help) and that UFM clearly beats the flow baselines on the reasoning tasks with a smaller model.
AuIVzEnuvK.main_concern: The gains are not isolated from generic recurrent latent refinement (no same-backbone recurrent control), and the method is called a flow model in name only, with training trajectories that include answer information.

WSwBqWifkx.one_liner: Predicts RLVR outcomes under imperfect verifiers by simulating linearized training dynamics with a tangent kernel estimated from sampled generations.
WSwBqWifkx.problem: Confusion-matrix statistics such as Youden's index cannot predict how systematic imperfect-verifier errors affect task performance after RLVR training.
WSwBqWifkx.method: They prove Youden's index and similar statistics are insufficient even for simple log-linear policies, then approximate the base policy's tangent kernel from sampled generations and reuse it to simulate linearized RLVR dynamics across many verifiers, scored against the same ground-truth labels.
WSwBqWifkx.key_idea: Reuse one empirical tangent kernel of the base policy to simulate linearized RLVR training for many verifiers, capturing gradient geometry that confusion matrices miss.
WSwBqWifkx.evidence: A theoretical proposition for log-linear policies and experiments on models up to 8B parameters (including Qwen2.5-7B on MATH per reviews) comparing predicted with actual task performance against Youden's index.
WSwBqWifkx.claimed_gains: The abstract is truncated at the claim that, for models up to 8B parameters, the linearized simulation improves predictions; a review reports mean correlation rising from 0.616 to 0.708 when reading the simulation at step 20.
WSwBqWifkx.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree imperfect verifiers are an important RL post-training setting and that the theoretical result on the limits of confusion-matrix statistics is precise and interesting.
WSwBqWifkx.main_concern: The method needs ground-truth labels for newly generated completions, the readout step is not validated on held-out settings, and the comparison is mainly against Youden's index.

9FzOhgTpoV.one_liner: Extends contrastive RL to semantic goals as predicates, with a termination-bias fix, as a critic teaching a policy-gradient student.
9FzOhgTpoV.problem: Contrastive RL had not been applied to open-ended environments with semantic goals, and its goal-occupancy estimator is biased when actions can terminate the episode, leaving fatal actions unpenalized.
9FzOhgTpoV.method: Goals are formalized as predicates over states, making CRL labels computable in closed form, with a Rao-Blackwellized estimator of the discounted goal-occupancy measure. An absorbing class and termination-discounted targets correct the termination bias, and the resulting critic teaches a policy-gradient student.
9FzOhgTpoV.key_idea: Add an absorbing class and termination-discounted targets so the contrastive goal-occupancy estimator accounts for probability mass beyond the end of the episode.
9FzOhgTpoV.evidence: Craftax with thousands of semantic goals, compared against a per-goal Q-learning teacher, with an ablation on the termination correction and comparisons to LEO per reviews.
9FzOhgTpoV.claimed_gains: On Craftax, comparable success to an agent trained with a per-goal Q-learning teacher across thousands of semantic goals while using up to 38x less training compute.
9FzOhgTpoV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the semantic-goal formulation and the identification of the termination bias are interesting, and the closed-form objective and experimental protocol are clear.
9FzOhgTpoV.main_concern: Performance gains are modest and appear to come mostly from the teacher-student setup rather than the proposed changes (Dual-LEO-PPO still outperforms), with no ablation inside Dual-CRL-PPO and efficiency inherited from original CRL.

q16xUYFs76.one_liner: Formalizes SAE concept learning as set alignment between human and model concepts, with geometric conditions for detection, separation, and approximation.
q16xUYFs76.problem: A principled definition of concept and concept learning in sparse autoencoders is lacking.
q16xUYFs76.method: Concepts are sets of data points and learning is set alignment between human-defined and model-induced concepts, yielding geometric conditions, error bounds, and capacity constraints for single- or multi-neuron representation. Formal concept analysis then links concept learning to neuron interpretation through concept lattices.
q16xUYFs76.key_idea: Define concepts as data-point sets and cast concept learning as set alignment with three strengths (detection, separation, approximation), linked to neuron interpretation through concept lattices.
q16xUYFs76.evidence: Theory (geometric conditions, error bounds, capacity constraints) plus synthetic-data experiments with ReLU and Top-K SAEs showing the effects of SAE size and sparsity.
q16xUYFs76.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the set formulation makes the difference between concept learning and neuron interpretation precise and gives a coherent, interpretable framework that clarifies conflated notions.
q16xUYFs76.main_concern: Novelty and utility are limited: results follow from standard convex separation and counting, and the theory covers representability rather than whether SAE training recovers concepts.

zbgYzUZMYD.one_liner: Parallel-in-time exponential integrator for neuro-spectral architectures using Picard-Duhamel iteration with exact linear propagation and parallel scans.
zbgYzUZMYD.problem: Neuro-spectral architectures rely on sequential Runge-Kutta time stepping for training and inference, which is costly, non-parallelizable, and collapses for stiff problems.
zbgYzUZMYD.method: PaPi propagates the linear part of the flow exactly with Duhamel's formula, iterates Picard updates on the nonlinear part over the whole trajectory, and uses associative scans for temporal parallelism. It adds explicit error bounds that depend on closeness to a linear surrogate and a theory-grounded warm-starting strategy for training.
zbgYzUZMYD.key_idea: Iterate Picard over the whole trajectory on the nonlinear part while propagating the known linear dynamics exactly, so time steps parallelize with exponential convergence.
zbgYzUZMYD.evidence: SciML experiments on several problems including stiff ones, compared mostly against explicit RK4, plus a convergence analysis with explicit error bounds.
zbgYzUZMYD.claimed_gains: Accelerates training and inference by up to three orders of magnitude, reaches sub-second training times for low-dimensional problems, and keeps competitive predictive accuracy even for stiff problems.
zbgYzUZMYD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the method addresses a genuine computational bottleneck, is mathematically well motivated with convergence analysis and error bounds, and gives strong empirical speedups.
zbgYzUZMYD.main_concern: Methodological novelty over classical exponential integrators and prior parallel-in-time methods is not established, comparisons focus on RK4, and the method relies on an efficiently computable linear propagator.

pmgqZClWWF.one_liner: Efficient Coding Regularizer penalizes response energy while encouraging high-effective-rank representations to improve continual learning in small networks.
pmgqZClWWF.problem: Networks learning sequential tasks disrupt prior knowledge and must use representational capacity efficiently enough to support future learning.
pmgqZClWWF.method: ECR penalizes response energy while encouraging diverse, high-effective-rank representations (a covariance log-determinant term per reviews), and is studied across continual-learning problems of increasing complexity. For class-incremental learning, where ECR alone does not prevent forgetting, the authors develop a nullspace-based method (abstract truncated).
pmgqZClWWF.key_idea: Balance neural response energy against representation diversity (effective rank), inspired by efficient coding, to keep capacity available for new tasks.
pmgqZClWWF.evidence: Permuted MNIST (including a width sweep with 20 seeds), a corrupted CIFAR-100 domain-incremental setting, and class-incremental learning where ECR alone does not prevent forgetting.
pmgqZClWWF.claimed_gains: On permuted MNIST, ECR reduces the rate of task-learning collapse by up to 19.3 percentage points, needs about 26% fewer epochs per task, and keeps up to 4.5x the representation diversity (effective rank) of standard training.
pmgqZClWWF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the PMNIST diagnosis under constrained capacity is thorough and multi-seed, and that the paper is candid about negative results (smaller CIFAR-100-C gains, ECR alone failing in class-incremental learning).
pmgqZClWWF.main_concern: The headline gains are compared only against standard training, with no comparison to continual backpropagation or an energy-only ablation to show each term is necessary.

OOq3uROmyD.one_liner: A frozen LLM makes explicit covariate-wise judgments to adjust a frozen time-series model's forecast, and reuses residual-validated judgments as experience.
OOq3uROmyD.problem: Forecast error shows the numerical discrepancy but not how multiple covariates should have been used, so past feedback does not tell a forecaster how to use covariates.
OOq3uROmyD.method: A frozen TSFM gives the base forecast and a frozen LLM uses the current context and retrieved experience to form covariate-wise judgments and then the numerical adjustment. After observation, the residual is used to reconstruct alternative judgments, the original and alternatives are scored by their resulting adjustments, and the best is retained as validated experience.
OOq3uROmyD.key_idea: Reconstruct alternative covariate judgments from the observed residual and keep the one whose adjustment performs best as reusable experience for later forecasts.
OOq3uROmyD.evidence: Seven real-world datasets in the main experiments plus three fev-bench tasks, a Chronos-2 base model (per reviews), alternative TSFM backbones on NP and PJM, and ablations.
OOq3uROmyD.claimed_gains: Outperforms strong baselines across diverse real-world datasets; no numbers in the abstract.
OOq3uROmyD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the problem is well motivated and that separating covariate judgments from numerical adjustment and validating experience through residual-based reconstruction is principled, with good ablations.
OOq3uROmyD.main_concern: Direct covariate conditioning with Chronos-2 is missing from the main comparison and outperforms JudgeCast with aligned covariates in the reported cases, and related work is insufficiently compared.

AuZqF30u7U.one_liner: Set-transformer attention that propagates separate center and generator feature streams through context-gated matrix transformations, with a generator-aware readout.
AuZqF30u7U.problem: Standard attention adapts token routing but shares value projections across contexts, and a summary that suffices for the current readout can discard information later layers need.
AuZqF30u7U.method: MZAttn parameterizes a transformation family with a learned center matrix and generator matrices modulated by bounded, permutation-invariant context gates. It propagates center and generator streams across layers and connects them to prediction through a generator-aware readout.
AuZqF30u7U.key_idea: Carry separate center and generator feature streams of a gated matrix-transformation family across layers instead of collapsing them into a single-vector update.
AuZqF30u7U.evidence: Theory gives exact representations for specified gated operator families, separations from restricted comparator classes, and exact approximation error for quadratic targets at every gate count; full-model experiments compare against a Set Transformer baseline (abstract is truncated).
AuZqF30u7U.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the sharp, verifiable approximation theory for gated-linear classes and the meaningful question of which features to retain across layers.
AuZqF30u7U.main_concern: The separations are proved against restricted comparators that exclude FFNs and normalization, and the full-model experiments do not isolate persistent feature retention, show runtime overhead, and show no consistent real-world advantage.

MKUhG4rSSm.one_liner: On-policy policy-gradient method that fine-tunes one-step drifting generative policies via a Wasserstein-gradient-flow fixed-point objective, without action likelihoods.
MKUhG4rSSm.problem: Diffusion and flow-based robot policies need many sequential network evaluations per sample, and the resulting latency suits poorly dynamic tasks with tight feedback loops.
MKUhG4rSSm.method: Reward drifting derives, from Wasserstein gradient flows, a single fixed-point objective whose optimization is shown equivalent to increasing expected discounted reward. It needs no action likelihoods or surrogates and applies to drifting models that sample in one network evaluation.
MKUhG4rSSm.key_idea: Optimize a Wasserstein-gradient-flow fixed-point objective on a drifting model's one-step sampler so reward increases without action likelihoods or surrogate losses.
MKUhG4rSSm.evidence: Evaluated on manipulation tasks including Push-T, dexterous in-hand reorientation, and long-horizon bimanual manipulation, against diffusion and flow-matching baselines fine-tuned with existing RL methods; reviewers also cite DPPO, ReinFlow and DBPO comparisons and eager and compiled latency tables.
MKUhG4rSSm.claimed_gains: Substantially faster inference than diffusion and flow-matching baselines fine-tuned with existing RL methods; no numbers are stated.
MKUhG4rSSm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it targets a practical problem, fine-tuning a one-step generative policy without tractable action likelihoods, and shows large inference-latency reductions with competitive final success rates.
MKUhG4rSSm.main_concern: The results do not isolate the reward-drifting update from other design choices such as backbone and exploration, and only three tasks with near-saturated success rates are evaluated.

8SwmTPopd9.one_liner: Regularizing toward a known mixing reference policy makes average-reward Q-learning contractive and exploratory, yielding finite-time guarantees.
8SwmTPopd9.problem: In average-reward RL the span contraction of the Bellman operator depends on the mixing of the Markov dynamics, which existing work typically assumes rather than controls.
8SwmTPopd9.method: Regularize toward a given reward-agnostic m-step mixing policy; a central mixing lemma transfers the reference policy's mixing to learned policies. One regularizer-dependent quantity controls contraction and exploration and another controls bias, giving guarantees for regularized Q-iteration, synchronous and single-trajectory Q-learning, and Q-planning.
8SwmTPopd9.key_idea: A single regularizer-dependent domination quantity relative to the mixing reference policy controls both Bellman contraction and exploration, while a second quantity controls regularization bias.
8SwmTPopd9.evidence: Finite-time theoretical guarantees for regularized Q-iteration, synchronous and single-trajectory Q-learning, and Q-planning under one-step and multi-step mixing; reviews also mention some experiments.
8SwmTPopd9.claimed_gains: Under one-step mixing, bounds for the regularized fixed point match the classical model-query bound for relative value iteration and, up to logarithmic factors, an existing synchronous Q-learning sample-complexity bound; the TL;DR states epsilon^-2 dependence.
8SwmTPopd9.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the theory technically correct and rigorous, and a coherent account of how a reference policy helps average-reward learning.
8SwmTPopd9.main_concern: The presentation is hard to follow, with heavy notation introduced early, and the headline rates target the regularized fixed point rather than the original objective.

PfhSe4a0GY.one_liner: Audit showing Best-of-N gains for multimodal process reward models track score dispersion and positional confounds, not ranking quality.
PfhSe4a0GY.problem: Multimodal process reward models are judged almost entirely by Best-of-N improvement, which does not identify ranking quality because it tracks within-problem score dispersion.
PfhSe4a0GY.method: The authors recompute within-problem ranking on released scored cells, test step-level AUC against step-index baselines, repair a three-valued verdict readout, and evaluate at the trajectory level where a problem's completions are exchangeable.
PfhSe4a0GY.key_idea: Compare PRM scores against step-position and length baselines and evaluate ranking at the trajectory level, where completions are exchangeable, instead of via Best-of-N delta.
PfhSe4a0GY.evidence: Recomputation on 9 scored cells of a released artifact (7 scorers over 4 benchmarks), step-AUC controls with positional baselines, and 4346 held-out steps from a trained PRM; reviewers add a VisualPRM-8B control.
PfhSe4a0GY.claimed_gains: All scored cells fall in [0.4795, 0.5425]; a step-index baseline reaches 0.6694 against the verifier's 0.7903, and readout repair recovers +0.2581 once training has fixed the objective but only -0.0605 before it has.
PfhSe4a0GY.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper identifies an important flaw in PRM evaluation and that its simple baselines and controls show Best-of-N gains can be misleading.
PfhSe4a0GY.main_concern: Negative results may stem from implementation bugs in the authors' own PRM pipeline and a narrow evidence base (one trained checkpoint, small effective sample size), so generality to other multimodal PRMs is unclear.

GZV2k3I9mo.one_liner: Maps audio to a human-readable concept tree with small heads on frozen encoders; a frozen text-only LLM answers from it.
GZV2k3I9mo.problem: Large audio-language models couple an audio encoder to an LLM through multi-stage training, so new domains or stronger LLMs require retraining and answers cannot be traced to what the model heard.
GZV2k3I9mo.method: Small heads on frozen expert encoders map each audio chunk to nodes on a tree of named concepts for speech, music and environmental sound; a frozen text-only LLM answers from those nodes and an ASR transcript without hearing the clip. A new domain is added with one small head.
GZV2k3I9mo.key_idea: Give the LLM audio only as selected nodes of an explicit concept tree plus an ASR transcript, making answers traceable.
GZV2k3I9mo.evidence: Evaluated on SAKURA, MMAU, MMAR and MMAU-Pro with a 7B reader, node swap and injection interventions, 26 frozen text readers, and few-shot species identification against QLoRA fine-tuning of Qwen2.5-Omni-7B.
GZV2k3I9mo.claimed_gains: Replacing the deciding node overturns 78% of correct answers on SAKURA; with a 7B reader it outperforms all compared LALMs on SAKURA and trails them by 6-12 points on MMAU and MMAR, with about 1,400x fewer trained parameters, and beats QLoRA by 13-26 (abstract is truncated).
GZV2k3I9mo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the tested interpretability by design, modular replacement of the LLM reader, and cheap domain addition with small heads that beat QLoRA-tuned Qwen2.5-Omni-7B.
GZV2k3I9mo.main_concern: The tree's benefit is not isolated, since tree-only barely exceeds the blind reader on MMAU-Pro and MMAR and there is no flat-concept or SAR-LM comparison, and L2R trails LALMs on most reasoning benchmarks.

rbKxxBAHWa.one_liner: Benchmarks DNA, RNA and protein language models against human mutational constraint, showing weak alignment and complementary signal from constraint scores.
rbKxxBAHWa.problem: Biological language models trained across the tree of life may not capture recent human-lineage selection (human mutational constraint) that matters for human traits and disease.
rbKxxBAHWa.method: The authors score variants zero-shot with DNA, RNA, protein, MSA-based and sequence-to-function models, compare against evolutionary conservation and human constraint, and combine model scores with a human constraint metric (Gnocchi, per the reviews).
rbKxxBAHWa.key_idea: Combine zero-shot model variant scores with explicit human mutational-constraint metrics to recover signal for common functional variants that deep-conservation models miss.
rbKxxBAHWa.evidence: Six models across DNA, RNA and protein, plus MSA-based and sequence-to-function models, scored on a harmonized variant set for organismal and molecular phenotypes, including eQTL and GWAS variants.
rbKxxBAHWa.claimed_gains: Not stated in the abstract; it reports only that human constraint improves the models' ability to identify common functional variation.
rbKxxBAHWa.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the cross-modality evaluation under one protocol makes credible the finding that language models track deep conservation but not human constraint.
rbKxxBAHWa.main_concern: Gnocchi alone is nearly as predictive as model plus Gnocchi, which weakens the 'complementary' claim, and absolute AUROC on common variants such as eQTLs stays near chance.

KEPSftEkjy.one_liner: Balanced optimal-transport objective for time-series domain generalization that globally organizes class-aware representations and reweights samples by alignment gap.
KEPSftEkjy.problem: Pairwise or contrastive alignment defines relations locally and can miss the global structure from class semantics and class-conditional domain variation, leaving class semantics entangled with domain-specific signal variation.
KEPSftEkjy.method: Multa learns a globally balanced transport structure in the unit representation space that encourages class-discriminative representations and suppresses source-domain shortcuts. An adaptive alignment-gap reweighting focuses optimization on samples whose learned alignment deviates most from the target relation.
KEPSftEkjy.key_idea: Replace row-wise local sample matching with globally balanced optimal transport (Sinkhorn) over class relations, reweighted by each sample's alignment gap to the target.
KEPSftEkjy.evidence: Five leave-one-domain-out cross-dataset sleep staging tasks and 25 cross-person human activity recognition tasks, plus a proposition that balanced transport tightens the class-conditional source-variation bound and a generalization bound linking the objective to unseen-domain risk.
KEPSftEkjy.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract is truncated before the results)
KEPSftEkjy.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers credit the clearly motivated global-transport formulation, the transparent theoretical analysis, and an extensive evaluation over 30 domain generalization tasks with ablations and seed results.
KEPSftEkjy.main_concern: Gains are small and uneven (about 1.17 points on average for sleep staging, behind ERM++ on ISRUC), baselines are dated, and ablations do not isolate global transport from domain-aware weighting.

dTsXvoXtUo.one_liner: Execution-grounded benchmark of memory for long-session coding agents, plus a three-layer memory linking task facts, experience and code diffs.
dTsXvoXtUo.problem: Existing evaluations do not test whether memory helps coding agents resume interrupted, interleaved work as requirements evolve and branches diverge.
dTsXvoXtUo.method: CMB builds controlled interleaved task histories in real repositories, freezes interaction streams and repository checkpoints, and replays identical histories to every memory mechanism. The proposed three-layer memory links task facts, reusable experience, and code diffs through provenance and evolution relations.
dTsXvoXtUo.key_idea: Link task facts, reusable experience and concrete code diffs through provenance and evolution relations, so memory retains diffs that summaries lose.
dTsXvoXtUo.evidence: 216 code-editing tasks and 750 diagnostic questions over 5,595 turns from nine repositories in four languages, five existing memory mechanisms, two agent backbones, and SWE-ContextBench.
dTsXvoXtUo.claimed_gains: The strongest baseline resolves 36.6% of CMB tasks; the proposed memory reaches 43.1% and 35.6% across two backbones versus 36.6% and 28.2% for the strongest baselines, and 47.5% and 28.3% on SWE-ContextBench versus 45.5% and 25.3%.
dTsXvoXtUo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that test-based grading with frozen, replayed histories is a valuable and controlled evaluation of memory for long-session coding agents.
dTsXvoXtUo.main_concern: There are no NoMemory or oracle-recall controls, and full raw history with the stronger backbone (58.8%) beats every memory method, so it is unclear whether the tasks need memory.

tQl7mn9iR0.one_liner: Learns nonlinear embeddings of neural population activity with linear or locally linear latent dynamics for Kalman-filter-based model-predictive control.
tQl7mn9iR0.problem: Neural control built on linear or generalized linear models may not capture the nonlinear population dynamics needed for accurate control.
tQl7mn9iR0.method: A model learns nonlinear embeddings of neural population activity with linear or locally linear latent dynamics using control-focused objectives, from limited open-loop stimulation data. Recursive state estimation with a Kalman filter on the latent model enables tractable model-based control.
tQl7mn9iR0.key_idea: Train nonlinear embeddings with control-focused objectives so latent dynamics are linear or locally linear, keeping Kalman filtering and MPC tractable.
tQl7mn9iR0.evidence: Simulations on benchmark neuroscience systems with linear and nonlinear dynamics, covering stabilization at target setpoints and restoration of movement trajectories after simulated lesions, against baselines such as LDM and AE+LDM.
tQl7mn9iR0.claimed_gains: Models outperform baselines in stabilizing activity at target setpoints and in restoring movement trajectories after simulated lesions; no numbers are stated.
tQl7mn9iR0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers like the control-oriented pipeline that identifies dynamics from limited open-loop stimulation data and uses online Kalman-filter state estimation for closed-loop control.
tQl7mn9iR0.main_concern: The baseline set is narrow (no other state-space models, RNNs or Mamba), and real-time operation and sample efficiency are claimed but not quantified.

0ar58OZ6ah.one_liner: Learns visual RL representations by flow-matching generative models of future latent outcomes at arbitrary horizons plus behavioral cloning.
0ar58OZ6ah.problem: Visual RL representations are usually learned through reward prediction, value estimation or pixel reconstruction, and long-horizon targets typically need compounding rollouts.
0ar58OZ6ah.method: LSM combines bootstrapped flow matching, horizon conditioning and self-predictive representation learning in one objective, plus behavioral cloning. Distant future outcomes sampled under a policy form value-estimation targets without predicting every intermediate state.
0ar58OZ6ah.key_idea: Bootstrapped flow-matching velocity targets let a horizon-conditioned latent successor model sample distant futures directly, replacing reward and value prediction and pixel reconstruction.
0ar58OZ6ah.evidence: Visual offline RL benchmarks covering 38 tasks against model-free and model-based baselines including LUHM, plus an analysis that directly predicting future outcomes gives more accurate value estimates at longer horizons.
0ar58OZ6ah.claimed_gains: Substantial improvements over prior model-free and model-based approaches across 38 visual offline RL tasks, with particularly large gains on challenging long-horizon tasks; no other numbers are stated.
0ar58OZ6ah.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the method clear and well motivated, with strong results across many benchmarks and a coherent bootstrapped flow-matching successor-model objective.
0ar58OZ6ah.main_concern: The gain over LUHM is not isolated, since LUHM also differs in return estimate and policy extraction, and reviewers ask for ablations that change only the bootstrapped velocity objective.

ZnM9Zs90UO.one_liner: Two symmetry reductions for Markov games, over states and over interchangeable agents, that preserve the Nash gap against all deviations.
ZnM9Zs90UO.problem: A smaller symmetric game is useful only if equilibria found there are equilibria of the original, but a symmetric policy that cannot be improved symmetrically may still be beaten by an asymmetric deviation.
ZnM9Zs90UO.method: State symmetry collapses the game to groups of equivalent states, and agent symmetry replaces the separate policies of interchangeable agents with one shared policy. Each reduction preserves the Nash gap against all deviations, and the two combine when compatible.
ZnM9Zs90UO.key_idea: Collapse equivalent states and tie interchangeable agents' policies so the reduced game's Nash gap equals the true gap against all deviations, not just symmetric ones.
ZnM9Zs90UO.evidence: Theory on gap preservation, tighter convergence bounds, a shared-policy bound and pooled generative-model queries, plus experiments on cooperative and zero-sum tabular games (a 3-agent Ring and a 10-position game, per reviewers).
ZnM9Zs90UO.claimed_gains: not stated; the abstract claims tighter convergence bounds and fewer generative-model samples from pooling symmetric queries, with no numbers.
ZnM9Zs90UO.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that certifying symmetric or parameter-shared policies as Nash equilibria of the original game matters for multi-agent RL, and that the construction is clean.
ZnM9Zs90UO.main_concern: Novelty is questioned against prior symmetry results in multi-agent RL, and the experiments cover only two small tabular settings.

CAA8vPOPNc.one_liner: RLVR where one model states a position, argues against it, rules on the argument, and trains on the ruling.
CAA8vPOPNc.problem: Models give up correct answers under wrong counter-reasoning, and the ability to hold or yield (dialectical competence) does not follow from first-answer accuracy or from inference-time reflection or sampling.
CAA8vPOPNc.method: The model states a position, generates the strongest case against it (its antithesis), rules on whether the case stands, and is trained on the ruling with RLVR. The same check that scores the answer against its reference scores the ruling, so no second model, reward model, preference data or annotation is needed.
CAA8vPOPNc.key_idea: Train the model with RLVR on its own rulings about a self-generated antithesis, scored by the same reference check used for answers.
CAA8vPOPNc.evidence: Per reviewers, Qwen3-8B and Gemma-2 9B evaluated across 9 benchmarks including math and code, 17 challengers and 4 extra models, with controls and ablations against accuracy-only RL and a Revise-RL baseline.
CAA8vPOPNc.claimed_gains: not stated (the abstract is truncated before the results)
CAA8vPOPNc.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the distinction between answering accurately and responding to disagreement matters in practice, and they credit the controls and external-challenger results.
CAA8vPOPNc.main_concern: The increment over self-correction training such as SCoRe and S2R is not established, and gains look more like holding answers (correct yielding drops) than better discrimination, notably on Qwen3-8B.

Cx5GsIJgpZ.one_liner: Verifies chain-of-thought traces step by step in iGSM and shows models answer correctly without producing valid traces.
Cx5GsIJgpZ.problem: Chain-of-thought traces are read as records of how models reach answers, but natural-language traces are rarely mechanically verifiable, so whether correct answers come with valid traces is untested.
Cx5GsIJgpZ.method: The authors train GPT-2-size models from scratch on iGSM, varying only the trace attached to each training problem (reference, swapped between problems, partially shuffled, non-minimal), and check generated traces step by step against the quantities and dependencies a correct solution must use.
Cx5GsIJgpZ.key_idea: Use iGSM's exact dependency structure to verify every trace step mechanically, and corrupt training traces to test whether answer correctness depends on trace validity.
Cx5GsIJgpZ.evidence: GPT-2-size models trained from scratch on iGSM with clean, swapped, shuffled and non-minimal traces, evaluated in and out of distribution with a step-level verifier.
Cx5GsIJgpZ.claimed_gains: Clean models reach almost 100% in-distribution accuracy; models trained on swapped traces still answer 82% of in-distribution problems correctly; shuffled-trace models stay near clean accuracy, with a valid derivation after the shuffled block 81.6% of the time on the hardest instances.
Cx5GsIJgpZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that iGSM makes trace validity mechanically checkable and that the swapping, shuffling and non-minimal-trace interventions give consistent evidence that correct answers and valid traces can decouple.
Cx5GsIJgpZ.main_concern: The experiments use a single 124M GPT-2-style model on synthetic data, and the verifier checks the generator's dependency graph rather than any equivalent valid derivation, which limits generality.

mgCcq6Ed6l.one_liner: Early-stopping for long-video QA that predicts the current answer's advantage under an expanded view and calibrates a stopping bound conformally.
mgCcq6Ed6l.problem: Confidence from partial video observations can mislead because later evidence may change the answer, yet scoring every frame is costly.
mgCcq6Ed6l.method: A lightweight linear predictor combines current confidence, observation progress and coarse cues from the remaining video to estimate the answer's advantage over alternatives under a fixed expanded reference view. Calibration across videos yields a lower bound that triggers stopping when positive and controls early-stop reference disagreement under exchangeable video sampling.
mgCcq6Ed6l.key_idea: Stop when a calibrated lower bound on the current answer's advantage under an expanded reference view is positive.
mgCcq6Ed6l.evidence: Held-out Video-MME videos with Qwen2.5-VL-7B and a 64-frame budget; reviewers add multiple backbones, stopping-strategy comparisons, and a guarantee defined against a fixed 128-frame reference view.
mgCcq6Ed6l.claimed_gains: 1.40x speedup over scoring all 64 budgeted frames once, with 68.02% versus 67.65% accuracy and 5.19% observed video-level early-stop reference disagreement at a 10% target.
mgCcq6Ed6l.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper tackles a real limitation of confidence-based early stopping and that video-level conformal calibration gives a meaningful finite-sample guarantee with practical speedups at comparable accuracy.
mgCcq6Ed6l.main_concern: The guarantee covers agreement with a fixed 128-frame reference view rather than correctness, and the comparisons are incomplete (differently tuned baseline thresholds, no same-risk comparison, no agent-based methods).

usUW4xWoxQ.one_liner: NLHF with convex risk measures of preference loss replacing expected payoffs, keeping self-play convergence and adding tail robustness.
usUW4xWoxQ.problem: NLHF optimizes expected pairwise payoffs, conflating policies with similar win rates but different tail behavior, so strong average performance can mask failures across prompts, annotators or safety-critical strata.
usUW4xWoxQ.method: Players optimize convex risk measures of their preference loss. Translation invariance preserves constant-sum structure at the level of risk-adjusted payoff operators, retaining monotonicity for sample-efficient self-play, and the paper proves algorithmic stability and offline sample complexity bounds that scale with risk.
usUW4xWoxQ.key_idea: Replace expected pairwise payoffs with convex risk measures whose translation invariance keeps the risk-adjusted payoff operator constant-sum and monotone.
usUW4xWoxQ.evidence: Theory on equilibria of symmetric self-play fixed points, convergence, stability and offline sample complexity, plus a controlled LLM preference study on 100-136 prompts per stratum with a single training seed, including OMD and OMD-Ent comparisons (per reviewers).
usUW4xWoxQ.claimed_gains: Tail robustness without sacrificing average preference win-rate; the visible abstract gives no numbers.
usUW4xWoxQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree it is a clean, unifying generalization of NLHF with solid convergence, equilibrium and bias-correction results.
usUW4xWoxQ.main_concern: Empirical support for the headline robustness claims is thin (single training seed, 100-136 prompts per stratum, and risk adjustment alone not consistently beating risk-neutral baselines).

ME9fL9xjfe.one_liner: Forecasts misalignment before fine-tuning by having an LLM rate a dataset's pull toward misbehavior, then combining that with base rates.
ME9fL9xjfe.problem: Fine-tuning on data with a narrow flaw can make a model broadly misaligned, and today this is caught only by auditing the model after training.
ME9fL9xjfe.method: A forecaster takes a target model, a fine-tuning dataset and a failure mode and outputs the probability that fine-tuning meaningfully increases that failure mode. An LLM reads the dataset and rates how strongly and broadly it pushes toward misbehavior, and a simple learned model combines that rating with the failure mode's base rate and the target model's prior tendency.
ME9fL9xjfe.key_idea: Combine an LLM's rating of how strongly and broadly a dataset pushes toward misbehavior with the failure mode's base rate and the target model's prior tendency.
ME9fL9xjfe.evidence: AlignmentForecastBench has over 5,000 forecasting questions across 17 target models, 32 datasets and 16 failure modes, with ground truth from real fine-tuning, and is compared against prompted frontier models, a model fine-tuned on the task, and a forecaster that sees weaker models' post-fine-tuning behavior.
ME9fL9xjfe.claimed_gains: Forecasts well above chance and beats a model fine-tuned on the task and a simple forecaster allowed to see how weaker models behaved after fine-tuning; no accuracy numbers are stated.
ME9fL9xjfe.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that predicting alignment failures before training is an important direction and that the benchmark, built from real fine-tuning outcomes, is a real contribution.
ME9fL9xjfe.main_concern: The forecaster relies mostly on dataset-level features and failure-mode priors with little target-model-specific signal, and the evaluation depends heavily on multiple-choice measures.

Pz5Z1oz70O.one_liner: Shows punctuation and chat-template boundaries strengthen induction and shift which context models retrieve, traced to specific attention key/value pathways.
Pz5Z1oz70O.problem: It is unclear how discourse boundaries such as punctuation and chat-template delimiters influence which information language models retrieve from context.
Pz5Z1oz70O.method: Controlled random-token sequences and natural-language prompts vary boundary placement across many model families, and mechanistic analysis in GPT-2 small localizes the forward-salience effect to the representation of the token following the first occurrence of a repeated cue.
Pz5Z1oz70O.key_idea: A boundary boosts retrieval of adjacent content via the contextualized representation of the token after the first cue occurrence, carried through a few attention-head key/value pathways.
Pz5Z1oz70O.evidence: Random-token and natural-language tasks across Pythia 2.8B, Qwen 2.5, Gemma 4, SmolLM2, Falcon 3 and OLMo 2, plus mechanistic analysis in GPT-2 small.
Pz5Z1oz70O.claimed_gains: not stated (analysis paper; the abstract only says boundary effects on post-boundary evidence weighting sometimes reach an order of magnitude)
Pz5Z1oz70O.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the synthetic experiments are tightly controlled, the effect appears across many model families, and the mechanistic analysis goes beyond attention visualization.
Pz5Z1oz70O.main_concern: The GPT-2 circuit analysis does not clearly explain the natural-language results, where a new user turn may be read as an update, and the paper lacks discourse-aware baselines.

dqgbGsaGXM.one_liner: Contact-geometry-preserving neural architectures built from lifted symplectic maps, with universality proofs and inversion of folded Hamilton-Jacobi fronts.
