zQZVpPwjbo.claimed_gains: Grounding refusal trails VQA refusal by 31–59 percentage points across domains, and fine-tuning reports grounding-refusal gains of 77–95 percentage points for Qwen3-VL-8B and VisionReasoner-7B.
zQZVpPwjbo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that matched requests reveal a consequential safety gap between free-text answers and visual grounding outputs.
zQZVpPwjbo.main_concern: Safety outcomes rely on a single LLM judge without human validation.

0FOmeaaWot.one_liner: Learned latent generation actions let an adversarial teacher modify imagined worlds as a student explores.
0FOmeaaWot.problem: Existing world-model environment design offers limited control over generated trajectories for adaptive curricula.
0FOmeaaWot.method: DyMGen learns a controllable world-model interface from offline experience. An adversarial teacher selects latent generation actions online to shape the student's training environment without a handcrafted dynamic-generation interface.
0FOmeaaWot.key_idea: Learn latent actions that control world-model generation and let a teacher choose them dynamically during student exploration.
0FOmeaaWot.evidence: Experiments compare adversarially controlled generation with random generation and other world-model baselines across three environments, including comparisons with DEGen.
0FOmeaaWot.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value learning a dynamic environment-generation interface for adversarial curriculum training from offline trajectories.
0FOmeaaWot.main_concern: Experiments use environments with available handcrafted simulators and do not demonstrate practical advantages over the cheaper, stronger DEGen baseline.

dk3SXiMek0.one_liner: Local context density reweights discrete-flow sampling rates and token training losses.
dk3SXiMek0.problem: Factorized discrete flow objectives mix predictable tokens with ambiguous targets without accounting for their available local context.
dk3SXiMek0.method: The method modifies the discrete-flow CTMC using neighborhood context and introduces a scaled cross-entropy loss that reweights token supervision. The context-weighted sampler also applies to pretrained models without retraining.
dk3SXiMek0.key_idea: Use nearby available context to weight token transition rates and cross-entropy contributions.
dk3SXiMek0.evidence: OpenWebText results compare matched discrete-flow baselines and semi-autoregressive block diffusion, with additional text and molecular generation experiments and ablations.
dk3SXiMek0.claimed_gains: Scaled cross-entropy reduces generative perplexity by up to 63% on OpenWebText, while the method matches a strong semi-autoregressive block diffusion baseline in quality.
dk3SXiMek0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize simple sampling and training changes that are easy to incorporate and improve matched-baseline generation results.
dk3SXiMek0.main_concern: The link between lower uncertainty from local context and more informative training supervision lacks direct justification.

djcC2yzHq4.one_liner: Factor-space drift analysis derives convergence rates for federated LoRA under heterogeneous client data.
djcC2yzHq4.problem: The effect of low-rank factorization on federated local drift and convergence under heterogeneous data is not fully understood.
djcC2yzHq4.method: The paper analyzes full-batch federated LoRA with full client participation, simultaneous factor updates, and server-side factor averaging. A one-round descent bound tracks factor norms, local steps, and step size to derive non-asymptotic stationarity rates.
djcC2yzHq4.key_idea: Translate weight-space heterogeneity into factor-space drift bounds and control factor trajectory growth to bound federated optimization.
djcC2yzHq4.evidence: Theoretical convergence analysis accompanies experiments varying architectures, client heterogeneity, and learning rates.
djcC2yzHq4.claimed_gains: The analysis gives an O(1/log T) rate with harmonic step sizes without uniform factor-norm bounds, and O(T^{-2/3}) under additional uniform trajectory bounds.
djcC2yzHq4.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value theoretical bounds connecting heterogeneous client gradients to LoRA factor drift and convergence.
djcC2yzHq4.main_concern: The theoretical contribution is insufficiently differentiated from existing centralized LoRA descent and convergence analyses.

HuRqGEh1x0.one_liner: Shared-attention max-margin analysis shows how a second prediction head favors cues predictive of both future tokens.
HuRqGEh1x0.problem: The mechanism by which multi-token supervision changes contextual cue selection remains unclear.
HuRqGEh1x0.method: The study analyzes a one-layer linear-attention model with two heads, first learning readouts and then freezing them while training shared attention by gradient flow. Structural assumptions permit explicit max-margin growth and prediction-rule characterizations.
HuRqGEh1x0.key_idea: A second future-token head adds margin constraints that concentrate leading attention growth on cues jointly predictive of both targets.
HuRqGEh1x0.evidence: Proofs characterize cue growth and recombined-context predictions, with synthetic validation and illustrative TinyStories experiments.
HuRqGEh1x0.claimed_gains: In an illustrative recombined context, correct next-token probability tends to one under MTP and to zero under NTP as training time grows.
HuRqGEh1x0.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the explicit, controlled account of how additional prediction constraints alter shared attention.
HuRqGEh1x0.main_concern: Strong architectural, data, and two-stage-training assumptions limit the theory's relevance to practical multi-token prediction.

EVDlM8XYoM.one_liner: Coordinate-wise specialist mixing and a low-rank residual preserve factual knowledge during model merging.
EVDlM8XYoM.problem: Merged models can maintain benchmark performance while losing information learned during specialist fine-tuning.
EVDlM8XYoM.method: The paper introduces factual datasets that directly measure specialist-taught knowledge. LUMEN jointly learns coordinate-wise mixtures of specialist updates and a low-rank correction from a small subset of specialist data.
EVDlM8XYoM.key_idea: Optimize coordinate-wise update gates together with an additive low-rank correction using limited specialist examples.
EVDlM8XYoM.evidence: Ten factual datasets examine multilingual and coding specialists, including merges of two to six specialists and per-specialist retention.
EVDlM8XYoM.claimed_gains: Using 1–5% of specialist data, LUMEN improves normalized factual retention by 21.2 percentage points on average over the strongest reported baseline at each merge size and reports 71.1% retention at six specialists.
EVDlM8XYoM.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that factual retention reveals losses hidden by standard model-merging benchmarks and that LUMEN improves reported retention.
EVDlM8XYoM.main_concern: Missing gate-only and correction-only ablations prevent separating better merging from residual fine-tuning.

uDjPyhYmD1.one_liner: Expert-audited Lean tasks require agents to build missing definitions and lemmas around advanced mathematical results.
uDjPyhYmD1.problem: Isolated theorem benchmarks often provide supporting formal infrastructure that real mathematical formalization must construct.
uDjPyhYmD1.method: AutoformBench pairs advanced target statements with informal proofs and asks agents to construct Lean proofs plus missing supporting infrastructure. Lean-experienced mathematicians formalize and audit targets before model evaluation.
uDjPyhYmD1.key_idea: Evaluate advanced proofs in broader developments where agents must supply missing formal definitions and intermediate lemmas.
uDjPyhYmD1.evidence: The benchmark contains 341 Lean 4 tasks from 24 graduate and research-level sources, with frontier-model comparisons, tool and scaffold ablations, and independent verification.
uDjPyhYmD1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value expert-curated advanced formalization tasks and the careful construction and verification process.
uDjPyhYmD1.main_concern: The largely descriptive analyses do not establish why missing infrastructure causes difficulty rather than reflecting model-specific proof choices.

eIJH6HV9LZ.one_liner: Replaying frozen historical agents constrains improver updates to retain earlier editing effectiveness.
eIJH6HV9LZ.problem: Rising task performance can hide deterioration in an agent's ability to generate effective future updates.
eIJH6HV9LZ.method: Improvement Function Replay evaluates candidate improvement strategies on frozen historical agent states. It selects updates that improve current problems while limiting declines from fixed historical reference gains without requiring identical edits.
eIJH6HV9LZ.key_idea: Replay historical editing problems and constrain new strategies by their retained gains relative to fixed references.
eIJH6HV9LZ.evidence: Experiments span five benchmarks and three frozen backbones, with common-state diagnostics, retention ablations, and controlled alternatives including Current-only + search.
eIJH6HV9LZ.claimed_gains: With Qwen3-32B, IFR improves unseen ALFWorld success, OfficeQA exact accuracy, and Seal-Hard accuracy by 2.3, 2.5, and 2.6 percentage points over Current-only + search.
eIJH6HV9LZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value distinguishing task performance from improvement ability and explicitly preserving historical editing effectiveness.
eIJH6HV9LZ.main_concern: The experiments do not directly establish that preserving historical editing ability improves subsequent multistep adaptation.

Qb1S3aJ2Ir.one_liner: mBFV aggregates worst-case parameter contributions and branches over perturbation locations to verify robustness against simultaneous bit flips.
Qb1S3aJ2Ir.problem: Existing quantized-network verifiers cannot efficiently handle simultaneous faults across multiple parameters because enumerating flip locations is combinatorial.
Qb1S3aJ2Ir.method: Multi-parameter bound propagation directly aggregates the m worst-case contributions without enumerating parameter combinations. Branch-and-bound partitions possible flip locations into smaller neuron groups to tighten certificates.
Qb1S3aJ2Ir.key_idea: Cardinality-constrained bound propagation aggregates the m worst-case parameter effects, then location-based branching tightens the resulting robustness bounds.
Qb1S3aJ2Ir.evidence: Evaluation covers 625 verification instances on feedforward networks and compares against a prior single-parameter verifier and an exact mixed-integer linear programming baseline.
Qb1S3aJ2Ir.claimed_gains: mBFV verifies 293 of 625 instances versus 38 and 0 for the baselines, scaling to 1.15M parameters and up to four simultaneous parameter flips versus baselines limited to 13k parameters.
Qb1S3aJ2Ir.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize multi-parameter bit-flip verification as a meaningful gap and find the bound-propagation and branching approach computationally useful.
Qb1S3aJ2Ir.main_concern: The evaluation covers only feedforward networks, leaving support for broader architectural scalability limited.

iohlEQGDm5.one_liner: Cross-trial latent prediction learns brain-only fMRI embeddings that permit unsupervised alignment and decoder transfer between participants.
iohlEQGDm5.problem: Sensory-evoked fMRI decoding has scarcely explored self-supervised representations that transfer across participants without images or shared stimuli.
iohlEQGDm5.method: Participant-specific JEPA encoders learn from brain data using cross-trial prediction and prediction of unmasked parcels. Independently learned representations are aligned without paired stimuli, allowing a decoding head trained on one participant to operate on another.
iohlEQGDm5.key_idea: Predicting across repetitions isolates stimulus-linked brain activity, while unpaired distributional alignment connects independently trained participant embeddings.
iohlEQGDm5.evidence: Natural Scenes Dataset experiments assess brain captioning, image reconstruction, encoder components, and cross-participant transfer without decoder fine-tuning.
iohlEQGDm5.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value brain-only representation learning and cross-participant alignment without shared stimuli, demonstrated through useful decoder transfer.
iohlEQGDm5.main_concern: Missing matched denoising and contrastive baselines leave the specific advantage of the JEPA formulation unestablished.

4HVGSrk9Pm.one_liner: SCALE correlates latent distances with task-state distances during world-model training to reshape the metric used for planning.
4HVGSrk9Pm.problem: Avoiding representation collapse does not ensure that latent distances reflect task-relevant differences needed for planning.
4HVGSrk9Pm.method: SCALE adds an objective correlating sampled pairwise latent distances with distances in task-relevant state space to LeWorldModel training. It uses privileged state during training while retaining the architecture and planning-time computation.
4HVGSrk9Pm.key_idea: Pairwise distance correlation makes task-relevant state differences influence the latent metric used as a planning cost.
4HVGSrk9Pm.evidence: Manipulation and navigation experiments with multiple planning solvers compare SCALE against LeWorldModel and analyze representation geometry and state decodability.
4HVGSrk9Pm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers recognize the relevance of shaping JEPA representation geometry for downstream planning beyond merely preventing collapse.
4HVGSrk9Pm.main_concern: The chosen privileged task-state distance may not reliably encode planning progress, particularly when state relevance or obstacle-induced path length matters.

mMhgWXIrOh.one_liner: SAIL accumulates structural occurrences without normalization and uses the accumulated state to correct LLM graph-prediction scores.
mMhgWXIrOh.problem: Making graph structure explicit in serialized inputs does not ensure that LLMs use category counts correctly for prediction.
mMhgWXIrOh.method: GraphMACC separates category recognition from counting and comparison in controlled graph tasks. Motivated by an analysis of normalized-attention response compression, SAIL accumulates occurrence-level structural information without normalization and corrects the LLM's candidate scores.
mMhgWXIrOh.key_idea: Unnormalized occurrence accumulation preserves multiplicity information in a structural state that adjusts the LLM's original prediction scores.
mMhgWXIrOh.evidence: GraphMACC controls degree across recognition, counting, and comparison tasks, with evaluations across LLMs, graph topologies, serializations, node orders, and native graph benchmarks.
mMhgWXIrOh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the controlled distinction between recognizing graph categories and using their counts for prediction.
mMhgWXIrOh.main_concern: The gains are not adequately separated from the added supervised prediction head, leaving the specific contribution of structural accumulation unclear.

kVDcjySgTG.one_liner: Transfers cluster-level reliability patterns learned on labeled known classes to calibrate unlabeled novel-class clusters.
kVDcjySgTG.problem: Generalized Category Discovery methods optimize clustering accuracy while leaving novel-class confidence miscalibrated, and standard sample-level post-hoc calibration fails because miscalibration varies by cluster and novel classes lack labels.
kVDcjySgTG.method: The paper introduces cluster-conditional expected calibration error (cluECE) to measure calibration within each predicted cluster without cross-cluster error cancellation, alongside Known-to-Novel calIbration Transfer (KNIT). KNIT characterizes cluster reliability using model self-assessment and vision-language model text features on labeled old-class clusters and transfers this class-agnostic mapping to novel-class clusters.
kVDcjySgTG.key_idea: Estimates a class-agnostic mapping from model self-assessment and vision-language semantic checks to cluster-level confidence offsets on known clusters, then applies it to novel clusters.
kVDcjySgTG.evidence: Evaluated on Generalized Category Discovery benchmarks including CIFAR-10, fine-grained, and Office-Home datasets, with component ablations and domain-shift comparisons reported in the reviews.
kVDcjySgTG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that addressing confidence miscalibration in Generalized Category Discovery via known-to-novel cluster-level reliability transfer is an important and well-motivated problem formulation.
kVDcjySgTG.main_concern: Empirical gains and component necessity are weakly substantiated across small test groups and few-cluster settings, alongside concerns over presentation clarity and overlap between cluECE and prior top-label calibration metrics.

jZIAMQEVr7.one_liner: Combines principal-subspace Adam updates with a normalized residual sign update and single BF16 momentum for QAT.
jZIAMQEVr7.problem: AdamW incurs high optimizer-state memory overhead in quantization-aware training (QAT) of LLMs, whereas low-rank projection optimizers such as GaLore and LDAdam degrade accuracy by discarding momentum outside the top-r singular subspace.
jZIAMQEVr7.method: ResQAdam stores a single BF16 momentum state, runs adaptive Adam updates only within the r-by-r principal subspace, and adds a normalized sign update derived from the out-of-subspace residual.
jZIAMQEVr7.key_idea: Maintains one BF16 momentum matrix while fusing r-by-r principal-subspace Adam updates with a normalized sign update computed from the discarded subspace residual.
jZIAMQEVr7.evidence: Evaluated across two from-scratch QAT methods (200M and 430M models) and three QAT fine-tuning pipelines (including Qwen3-4B) with weights quantized down to 2 bits, alongside subspace and rank ablations.
jZIAMQEVr7.claimed_gains: Reduces optimizer-state memory by 71% to 74% relative to AdamW while lowering training throughput by less than 2%.
jZIAMQEVr7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree ResQAdam is a clear, practical optimizer design backed by solid ablations and measured memory and throughput savings across multiple QAT configurations.
jZIAMQEVr7.main_concern: The paper omits QAT comparisons against other optimizers that retain out-of-subspace updates (FiRA and FRUGAL) and lacks direct evidence isolating quantization-error compensation as why the residual sign helps.

pP3cy1htQV.one_liner: Decomposes mid-denoising class-switched diffusion outputs into a noisy source-class image plus target-class conditional PCA components.
pP3cy1htQV.problem: Existing explanations of diffusion generalization focus on early stopping or score estimation errors without explaining how denoising guidance combines features across distinct classes.
pP3cy1htQV.method: The authors analyze a mid-generation denoising switch mechanism from a source image class S to a target class T and derive a linear decomposition of the generated output into a noisy image from S, a PCA term over reweighted images in T, and an error decaying exponentially with switch time.
pP3cy1htQV.key_idea: Approximates class-switched denoising trajectories linearly as a frozen noisy source-class structure plus principal components of reweighted target-class images governed by local denoiser geometry.
pP3cy1htQV.evidence: Supported by theoretical error analysis and empirical validation using an ImageNet-pretrained diffusion transformer.
pP3cy1htQV.claimed_gains: Establishes a linear decomposition of class-switched outputs with an approximation error of O(e^{-switch time/2}).
pP3cy1htQV.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the connection between mid-trajectory conditioning switches, local denoiser geometry, and cross-class feature composition intuitive and clearly presented.
pP3cy1htQV.main_concern: The theoretical conditional-PCA derivation assumes zero classifier-free guidance weight and local Jacobian stability, leaving a gap to nonzero guidance scales alongside an imprecise operational definition of creativity.

5tHb46nG32.one_liner: Benchmarks text-based world models on 1,632 execution-grounded state-transition tasks using deterministic gates and semantic judging.
5tHb46nG32.problem: Text-based world models lack a standardized benchmark with execution-grounded references to evaluate state-transition prediction across diverse environment rules and object dependencies.
5tHb46nG32.method: GlobeBench provides 1,632 next-state prediction tasks across five domains and 19 simulation skills conditioned on full agent trajectories. Model predictions are graded against execution-derived ground-truth states using a hybrid evaluator combining deterministic gates with an LLM semantic judge.
5tHb46nG32.key_idea: Pairs trajectory-conditioned action-transition prompts with execution-derived reference states and grades predictions through deterministic verification gates before invoking a semantic judge.
5tHb46nG32.evidence: Evaluates 20 general-purpose LLMs and specialized text world models across 1,632 tasks spanning five domains and 19 simulation skills.
5tHb46nG32.claimed_gains: Across 20 evaluated models, GPT-6 Astra achieves the highest task success rate at 49.57%, average task success drops to 5.1% when changes propagate to dependent objects, and 631 tasks remain unsolved by any model.
5tHb46nG32.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers strongly commend the execution-derived ground-truth states, fine-grained 19-skill task isolation, and deterministic-first hybrid grading pipeline.
5tHb46nG32.main_concern: Impact radius, reach-back history length, task operators, and prompt length are correlated by construction, confounding causal claims about why model performance drops, while single-step evaluation omits multi-step compounding error.

N7pc8LQlwG.one_liner: Injects each token's original input embedding into Transformer residual states using a state-predicted positive weight.
N7pc8LQlwG.problem: Pre-norm Transformers implicitly amplify each token's own input embedding projection across depth only indirectly through attention and MLP layers that observe embeddings mixed with prior updates.
N7pc8LQlwG.method: Explicit Embedding Reweighting (EER) retains the standard identity residual shortcut while adding the token's original input embedding at each layer scaled by a positive coefficient predicted from the current state, requiring no extra embedding tables or stored layer outputs.
N7pc8LQlwG.key_idea: Predicts a positive coefficient from the current layer state to re-add the original token embedding into the residual stream.
N7pc8LQlwG.evidence: Analyzes embedding projections in six pretrained language models across four families and trains EER models from 356M to 900M parameters alongside Attention Residuals, SATFormer, identity Hyper-Connections, and coefficient ablations.
N7pc8LQlwG.claimed_gains: Lowers validation loss by 0.022–0.025 nats across 356M–900M models with about 0.007% additional parameters, and raises 900M average zero-shot accuracy across seven tasks by 1.39 points.
N7pc8LQlwG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree EER is simple, lightweight, and well-presented, consistently improving over standard Transformer baselines with informative depth-projection observations and ablations.
N7pc8LQlwG.main_concern: Experiments stop at 900M total parameters leaving larger-scale LLM generalization unclear, and the paper does not directly verify that explicit reweighting resolves a bottleneck in implicit embedding amplification.

ljFzvvUlxK.one_liner: Enforces post-hoc agent accountability by verifying harness execution traces against smart-contract policy commitments backed by escrow payouts.
ljFzvvUlxK.problem: Preventive safeguards cannot eliminate all destructive AI agent behaviors, leaving users without verifiable post-hoc accountability or financial recourse when agents violate behavioral policies.
ljFzvvUlxK.method: Verifiable Agent Insurance (VAI) embeds programmatically specified policy promises and provider monetary escrow into a blockchain smart contract while logging execution traces through the agent harness's shared tool-execution path. When a user reports a violation, a verifier checks the committed trace logs and triggers automatic escrow payouts upon confirmation.
ljFzvvUlxK.key_idea: Hooks shared agent tool-execution paths to log verifiable traces and settles programmatic policy violations automatically via smart-contract escrow on an immutable ledger.
ljFzvvUlxK.evidence: Implemented end-to-end on an Ethereum layer-2 network (Base mainnet) and evaluated across three agent benchmarks, including two benchmarks re-annotated with task-level policy-compliance labels.
ljFzvvUlxK.claimed_gains: Reports a 63.6% violation detection rate in the abstract (while reviews cite 42.2% measured detection on original benchmark traces and an 83.0% estimated rate with added structured records).
ljFzvvUlxK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that operationalizing post-hoc agent accountability through a working prototype of trace logging, programmatic policies, and smart-contract escrow is a practical and worthwhile contribution.
ljFzvvUlxK.main_concern: All reviewers point out that the 83.0% violation-coverage figure relies on retrospective analytical estimation rather than rerunning instrumented agents, overstating the 42.2% measured benchmark detection rate.

kTBxuidcFI.one_liner: Allocates client mini-batch sizes via multinomial sampling for decentralized nonconvex nonsmooth Goldstein-stationary optimization.
kTBxuidcFI.problem: Decentralized optimization of nonsmooth nonconvex Lipschitz-continuous local objectives faces high computational and communication complexity across networked clients.
kTBxuidcFI.method: The paper proposes a stochastic first-order decentralized algorithm that allocates a total gradient sample budget across clients using a multinomial distribution combined with Chebyshev acceleration. It proves computational and communication complexity bounds for reaching a (delta, epsilon)-Goldstein stationary point on every client.
kTBxuidcFI.key_idea: Draws client stochastic-gradient mini-batch sizes from a multinomial distribution so zero-sample clients skip gradient evaluations while preserving unbiased network-averaged estimators.
kTBxuidcFI.evidence: Supported by theoretical computational and communication complexity proofs for (delta, epsilon)-Goldstein stationarity and numerical experiments.
kTBxuidcFI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the focus on decentralized nonconvex nonsmooth optimization and the complexity analysis combining multinomial client-data sampling with Chebyshev acceleration.
kTBxuidcFI.main_concern: Reviewers question both the decentralization and system practicality of centralized multinomial batch allocation and a proof gap that uses expected disagreement bounds where pointwise neighborhood inclusion is required.

GedeRvDLsJ.one_liner: Jointly trains autoregressive next-token prediction with latent diffusion over representations of future token sequences.
GedeRvDLsJ.problem: Myopic next-token prediction causes autoregressive language models to fail at lookahead planning, global coherence, and diverse solution exploration.
GedeRvDLsJ.method: The proposed hybrid model pairs autoregressive decoding with a latent diffusion process trained jointly to denoise a continuous latent representation of future output before generating discrete tokens.
GedeRvDLsJ.key_idea: Generates a continuous latent plan via iterative diffusion over encoded future sequences prior to autoregressive discrete token decoding.
GedeRvDLsJ.evidence: Evaluated on synthetic algorithmic benchmarks including star-graph and Sudoku tasks as well as the GSM8K mathematical reasoning benchmark against autoregressive, pause-token, and looped baselines.
GedeRvDLsJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the synthetic star-graph and Sudoku experiments clearly expose autoregressive myopia and demonstrate strong empirical gains with informative diagnostic analyses.
GedeRvDLsJ.main_concern: Comparisons are not budget- or supervision-matched (using more epochs and an uncounted pretrained encoder/autoencoder), and GSM8K ablations indicate Pass@1 gains stem largely from joint training rather than sampled diffusion plans.

YiG8Avw3KL.one_liner: Trains a 0.6B Mathlib lemma retriever iteratively from proof agents' own calls and Lean-verified proof dependencies.
YiG8Avw3KL.problem: Theorem-proving agents repeatedly query evolving formal libraries like Mathlib using approximate formal statements, requiring retrievers that match agent query distributions while remaining cheap to run and re-index.
YiG8Avw3KL.method: PocketLean trains a 0.6B encoder using query-level weak supervision that pairs recorded agent retrieval calls with lemmas used in Lean-verified final proofs, refined across generations via Replay-to-Rollout Evolution (R^2Evo) on recorded trajectories and fresh rollouts. The authors also curate ProofCall, a benchmark of 1,999 recorded agent retrieval calls across five sets.
YiG8Avw3KL.key_idea: Pairs agent retrieval queries with lemmas appearing in Lean-checked final proofs and iteratively retrains the retriever on rollouts collected using updated checkpoints.
YiG8Avw3KL.evidence: Evaluated on the Lean Finder benchmark, the five-set ProofCall benchmark (1,999 calls), and end-to-end theorem proving on curated subsets of miniF2F and ProofNet.
YiG8Avw3KL.claimed_gains: Reaches 78.9% mean Recall@10 on Lean Finder versus 77.9% for the 7B Lean Finder model, outperforms the strongest external system by 4.3 to 7.6 hit@10 points across all five ProofCall sets, and more than doubles end-to-end proving success on curated miniF2F and ProofNet subsets.
YiG8Avw3KL.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree PocketLean delivers strong retrieval accuracy and encoding efficiency at 0.6B scale while grounding training and ProofCall evaluation in actual proof-agent queries.
YiG8Avw3KL.main_concern: ProofCall selects queries only from successful verified proofs without human label validation, and ablations do not cleanly separate R^2Evo's online rollout loop from additional training data and procedural differences.

OJu98RijIf.one_liner: Uses controlled graph-fact interventions, early activation edits, and linear response maps to measure task-dependent attention-head interactions.
OJu98RijIf.problem: Identifying attention heads shared across tasks does not explain how those same components alter their factual sensitivity and downstream interactions under different task contexts.
OJu98RijIf.method: Holding input directed-graph facts constant across tasks, the authors measure component influence on later activations and importance to final answers via causal interventions and early internal task-switching activation edits. They also fit condition-specific linear response maps predicting later attention-head responses from intervened earlier heads before and after task edits.
OJu98RijIf.key_idea: Applies causal interventions and task-switching early activation edits on identical graph-fact prompts to track how task context reshapes inter-head linear response maps.
OJu98RijIf.evidence: Evaluated on synthetic graph-fact tasks across five open-weight language models spanning four families (1.5B–14B parameters), with task-edit and linear-response experiments on Gemma-2-9B and Qwen3-14B.
OJu98RijIf.claimed_gains: Condition-specific linear response maps reduce mean squared prediction error on separate factual interventions by 53.6% in Gemma-2-9B and 5.0% in Qwen3-14B compared with the average of pre- and post-edit maps.
OJu98RijIf.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers praise the controlled experimental setup that holds graph facts constant across tasks alongside clear intervention definitions and multi-model testing.
OJu98RijIf.main_concern: Key analyses examine a single selected head trio in a toy graph setting and cannot distinguish heads changing their internal function from downstream layers reading fixed-function heads differently.

ueWwNVqhQo.one_liner: Aligns multi-scale hierarchical jet-clustering views via DINO-style self-distillation for unlabeled high-energy physics pretraining.
ueWwNVqhQo.problem: Supervised jet tagging in high-energy physics suffers from simulation-to-data bias, while standard self-supervised learning augmentations lack physics-grounded inductive biases for particle jets.
ueWwNVqhQo.method: RINO constructs multi-scale views of particle jets across energy resolutions using hierarchical k_T clustering and aligns teacher and student representations via DINO-style self-distillation. It pretrains without labels exclusively on quantum chromodynamics (QCD) background jets before fine-tuning for downstream classification and out-of-distribution signal transfer.
ueWwNVqhQo.key_idea: Constructs coarse- and fine-scale particle jet views from hierarchical k_T clustering stages and aligns them through label-free DINO self-distillation.
ueWwNVqhQo.evidence: Pretrained on unlabeled QCD jets (JetClass) and evaluated on label-efficiency and out-of-distribution jet/top-tagging transfer benchmarks including JetNet and JetClass.
ueWwNVqhQo.claimed_gains: Matches fully supervised training on JetNet when fine-tuned on only 1% of the labeled data.
ueWwNVqhQo.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that generating multi-scale views via hierarchical k_T jet clustering provides an intuitive, physically motivated inductive bias for self-supervised jet representation learning.
ueWwNVqhQo.main_concern: Selecting RINO's teacher hyperparameters using target-domain JetClass OOD accuracy while leaving baselines untuned—alongside pretraining on target-domain QCD data—undermines strict OOD transfer fairness.

KM5mrefTv2.one_liner: Refines separated hyperspherical identity embeddings for source-attribute compatibility to condition flow-matching face de-identification.
KM5mrefTv2.problem: Selecting face de-identification targets solely by embedding distance from the source ignores non-identity attributes encoded in face-recognition features, causing unwanted attribute drift and visual artifacts.
KM5mrefTv2.method: HIDE (Hyperspherical Identity Target Editing) first constructs a target identity embedding well separated from the source on the hypersphere and refines it to preserve compatibility with source attributes such as age, gender, ethnicity, and pose. This edited target conditions a flow-matching generator trained with an inverse branch to synthesize anonymized faces.
KM5mrefTv2.key_idea: Edits an identity-separated target embedding on the hypersphere to match source non-identity attributes before conditioning a flow-matching face generator.
KM5mrefTv2.evidence: Evaluated on face de-identification and retrieval benchmarks including CelebA-HQ using face-recognition models such as ArcFace, CosFace, and CurricularFace alongside target-editor ablations.
KM5mrefTv2.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that enforcing source-attribute compatibility directly during identity-target construction clearly addresses attribute drift and ghosting in generative face de-identification.
KM5mrefTv2.main_concern: Reviewers note incomplete evaluation protocol specifications and an inconsistency in reported CelebA-HQ retrieval metrics (R@5 lower than R@1), alongside questions on disentangling attributes within ArcFace embeddings.

OWHkAJsQ3v.one_liner: Uses activation patching to localize the VLM-to-action cross-attention interface in VLAs and simplify policy conditioning.
OWHkAJsQ3v.problem: Little is known mechanistically about how vision-language backbones transform perceptual and instruction representations into motor actions inside vision-language-action (VLA) robot policies.
OWHkAJsQ3v.method: The authors apply counterfactual activation patching across three VLA models (pi_0.5, MolmoAct2, and MolmoBot) to trace where object identity and spatial movement cues enter the action expert. Identifying a narrow mid-to-late cross-attention band—the action-conditioning interface—enables simplifying VLM-to-action conditioning and modality compression for faster inference.
OWHkAJsQ3v.key_idea: Identifies via causal activation patching a narrow mid-to-late cross-attention band transmitting spatial and target cues to the action expert, enabling interface simplification.
OWHkAJsQ3v.evidence: Evaluated via causal patching and closed-loop robot manipulation benchmarks across pi_0.5, MolmoAct2, and MolmoBot (including 12-seed evaluations reported in reviews).
OWHkAJsQ3v.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value bridging mechanistic activation-patching analysis across multiple VLA architectures with concrete interface simplifications that reduce inference cost while preserving closed-loop task success.
OWHkAJsQ3v.main_concern: Layer-wise patching interventions do not fully disentangle whether interfaces transmit pure spatial coordinates versus joint semantic-layout cues or whether early noun patching goes beyond simple instruction replacement.

TgYNK4tv0A.one_liner: Trains first-frame-guided video editors on action-matched object-presence video pairs with VLM-predicted temporal interaction guidance.
TgYNK4tv0A.problem: Existing video object insertion methods struggle to make newly inserted objects participate coherently in physical interactions such as grasping or manipulation.
TgYNK4tv0A.method: ALIVE curates 35,800 paired videos (combining 3D-rendered, model-generated, real-world, and ROSE pairs) that differ in target object presence while preserving surrounding actions to train a first-frame-guided video editor. It additionally trains a vision-language model to infer interaction guidance from the edited first frame and object name, routed temporally during generation.
TgYNK4tv0A.key_idea: Supervises first-frame-guided video editing on action-aligned video pairs differing only in object presence, augmented by VLM-predicted interaction guidance.
TgYNK4tv0A.evidence: Evaluated on the proposed ALIVE-interaction benchmark and a general video object insertion benchmark, with data-composition and prompt-guidance ablations.
TgYNK4tv0A.claimed_gains: Without VLM guidance, ALIVE improves Overall score over the strongest baseline by 43.9% on ALIVE-interaction and 4.4% on general object insertion, while VLM-predicted guidance adds a further 0.95 points on ALIVE-interaction.
TgYNK4tv0A.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that curating action-preserving interaction video pairs addresses a challenging video-editing limitation and yields strong quantitative and qualitative object-interaction improvements.
TgYNK4tv0A.main_concern: Headline interaction scores rely on a single GPT/VLM judge evaluating sampled frames without human or cross-family judge validation, leaving the small 0.95-point guidance gain and dataset reproducibility uncertain.

GqWrHDLgy3.one_liner: Optimizes a shared multi-drone payload control program offline by alternating LLM code revision with parameter search.
GqWrHDLgy3.problem: Coordinating multi-drone formation, obstacle avoidance, and stabilization for cable-suspended payloads is difficult with black-box neural policies whose control decisions cannot be easily inspected or revised.
GqWrHDLgy3.method: The framework uses a pretrained LLM offline to iteratively revise a shared, human-readable control program from diagnostic simulator feedback while alternating with local parameter search on matched task instances. Deployment executes the resulting frozen program atop a fixed low-level flight controller without online LLM inference.
GqWrHDLgy3.key_idea: Alternates execution-guided LLM code revision with local parameter search to optimize a shared control program offline before deployment.
GqWrHDLgy3.evidence: Evaluated in simulation on a constructed cooperative multi-drone cable-payload benchmark spanning standard transport, commanded emergency setdown, and disturbance stress conditions against PPO, handwritten, and code-generation baselines.
GqWrHDLgy3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate tackling coupled multi-drone payload transport with an inspectable shared control program that executes without online LLM inference across diverse simulated scenarios.
GqWrHDLgy3.main_concern: Comparisons against PPO do not match simulation or compute budgets (showing a modest overall margin where PPO outperforms on emergency setdown), alongside limited methodological novelty and no real-hardware validation.

MYXgOex05m.one_liner: Interpolates familiarity-biased SFT checkpoints with their pretrained base model before RL to restore output diversity.
MYXgOex05m.problem: Supervised fine-tuning methods that upweight high-probability or self-generated familiar tokens contract policy support and collapse output diversity, degrading subsequent reinforcement learning.
MYXgOex05m.method: The authors theoretically analyze support contraction in familiarity-preferring SFT objectives and propose Base-Model Merging (BMM), which interpolates the fine-tuned model's weights with its pretrained base model prior to RL training.
MYXgOex05m.key_idea: Merges familiarity-weighted SFT model parameters with the pretrained base checkpoint before RL to recover collapsed token-distribution support.
MYXgOex05m.evidence: Supported by theoretical support-contraction analysis and experiments across mathematical reasoning and code generation benchmarks (including Qwen2.5-Coder-3B) comparing DFT, SFT variants, and KL regularization on Pass@1, Pass@8, entropy, and post-RL accuracy.
MYXgOex05m.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper clearly identifies the tension between familiarity-biased SFT accuracy and RL exploration, pairing useful theoretical analysis with a simple, effective base-model merging fix.
MYXgOex05m.main_concern: Checkpoint weight interpolation with base models is closely related to prior model-merging work, while the theoretical scope is restricted to simplified token-weighting rules and pre-RL merging gains on DFT remain incompletely explained.

0vjCA2f691.one_liner: Learns directed gene regulatory graphs and perturbation responses by separating residual functional activity from transcript abundance.
0vjCA2f691.problem: Genetic perturbation models typically assume ideal complete knockouts or unconstrained mechanism shifts, failing to distinguish incomplete functional loss from measured RNA transcript levels when jointly learning causal structure and responses.
0vjCA2f691.method: RISCAL formulates a nonlinear gene-level structural causal model under residual-activity interventions that decouples latent gene-specific functional activity from observed transcript abundance, jointly estimating directed acyclic regulatory structure and perturbation responses.
0vjCA2f691.key_idea: Models imperfect genetic perturbations by separating gene-specific residual functional activity from measured transcript abundance within a nonlinear structural causal model.
0vjCA2f691.evidence: Evaluated on staged synthetic DAG benchmarks (up to 3,710 genes per reviews) and LINCS L1000 perturbation profiles across ten cell lines with CollecTRI/SIGNOR interaction enrichment checks.
0vjCA2f691.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that decoupling latent functional gene activity from measured transcript abundance is biologically well-motivated and supported by a detailed staged synthetic generator and careful real-data evaluation.
0vjCA2f691.main_concern: The method assumes paired control-perturbation data requiring bulk well-averaged L1000 assays rather than single-cell data, while synthetic benchmarks closely mirror RISCAL's own modeling assumptions and gene-specific attenuation is not isolated.

wMZdwUmnGh.one_liner: Trains a multimodal agent via SFT and multitask RL to orchestrate augmentation, generation, and verification video tools.
wMZdwUmnGh.problem: Standalone video generation models often fail on prompts demanding external procedural knowledge, multi-entity identity preservation, physical consistency, or multi-shot temporal ordering.
wMZdwUmnGh.method: VideoGen-Agent trains a shared multimodal policy via supervised fine-tuning on teacher trajectories followed by multitask reinforcement learning with a category-aware hybrid reward to coordinate augmentation, generation, and verification tools over multiple turns. The authors also introduce VABench, a 600-prompt benchmark spanning six video-generation capability categories.
wMZdwUmnGh.key_idea: Optimizes a multi-turn multimodal agent policy with category-aware hybrid rewards to adaptively invoke augmentation, video generation, and verification tools.
wMZdwUmnGh.evidence: Evaluated on the 600-prompt VABench benchmark across six capability categories against standalone base video generators (including Seedance models), prompt rewriting, and fixed-workflow baselines.
wMZdwUmnGh.claimed_gains: Improves VABench score by 19.1 points over its base video generator (from 56.5 to 75.6), reaching 86.1 when paired with upgraded generation tools.
wMZdwUmnGh.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the modular augmentation-generation-verification toolset and six-category VABench benchmark effectively target key compositional and physical failure modes of standalone video generators.
wMZdwUmnGh.main_concern: Evaluations do not match inference-time generation budgets against fixed workflows, omit prior agentic baselines like VISTA, and show shrinking marginal gains over stronger base video models.

yM5j0AR8qQ.one_liner: Benchmarks foundation models on four behavioral science task families using both individual-level and distributional-alignment metrics.
yM5j0AR8qQ.problem: Existing evaluations of foundation models in behavioral science lack systematic coverage across task types and fail to separate per-subject prediction accuracy from population-level distributional validity.
yM5j0AR8qQ.method: BehaviorBench evaluates general-purpose LLMs and behavior-specialized foundation models across behavior prediction and simulation, strategic decision-making, subject-trait inference, and behavioral knowledge application using both individual-level and distributional-level metrics. The study also examines fine-tuning models on diverse behavioral datasets.
yM5j0AR8qQ.key_idea: Jointly measures per-subject prediction accuracy and population-level distributional alignment across four behavioral-science capability axes to expose response-diversity collapse.
yM5j0AR8qQ.evidence: Evaluates 20 general-purpose and behavior-specialized foundation models (plus fine-tuned variants) on data from behavioral experiments, personality surveys, scientific literature, and economic games.
yM5j0AR8qQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the large-scale, well-organized benchmark and find distinguishing individual-level accuracy from distributional alignment insightful for diagnosing diversity collapse.
yM5j0AR8qQ.main_concern: The benchmark omits simple non-foundation supervised baselines to contextualize absolute task predictability and relies heavily on stylized games and surveys with uncertain real-world behavioral transfer.

SrRLZloL9l.one_liner: Isolates low-rank residual-stream subspaces for positional, lexical, and reflexive entity binding read additively by retrieval heads.
SrRLZloL9l.problem: While positional, lexical, and reflexive entity-binding heuristics are known in language models, how their signals are stored in activations and reconciled during retrieval remains unclear.
SrRLZloL9l.method: Using centered contrastive subspace estimation and QK attention decomposition, the authors isolate low-rank residual-stream subspaces at the final token for positional, lexical, and reflexive binding. They perform targeted single-subspace causal interventions to test whether individual retrieval heads additively read all three subspaces to steer attention and output.
SrRLZloL9l.key_idea: Decompose retrieval-head query-key logits across mechanism-specific low-rank residual subspaces so single-subspace interventions selectively redirect entity attention and predictions.
SrRLZloL9l.evidence: Evaluated via causal restoration, single-subspace edits, and non-interventional QK decompositions on a synthetic multi-fact entity-binding task across two language models.
SrRLZloL9l.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper is clearly written and uses complementary causal subspace interventions to show how multiple binding signals feed into shared retrieval heads.
SrRLZloL9l.main_concern: Additivity in QK space follows linearly by construction, and studying mainly one retrieval head on a single synthetic task across two models makes the advance over recent binding papers narrow.

8qlkkwGIod.one_liner: Forms an implicit RL critic via Bayes' rule using a return-conditioned flow policy anchored to TD targets.
8qlkkwGIod.problem: Discriminative and distributional Q-learning train critics solely from scalar or return-distribution targets, leaving rich supervision from observed actions unused.
8qlkkwGIod.method: Generative Value Classifier (GVC) reverses conditioning via Bayes' rule, using a return-conditioned flow-matching policy to score state-action likelihoods across candidate returns and induce an implicit Q-function. The critic trains jointly with action-supervising flow matching and a squared-error loss anchoring induced Q-values to bootstrapped Bellman targets.
8qlkkwGIod.key_idea: Invert return-distribution prediction with Bayes' rule so a return-conditioned flow policy scores actions across returns while squared TD loss anchors Q-values.
8qlkkwGIod.evidence: Evaluated on offline, online, and offline-to-online reinforcement learning benchmarks against discriminative, actor-matched, and distributional RL baselines.
8qlkkwGIod.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the Bayes-rule flow critic formulation is simple, clearly presented, and achieves strong empirical performance across offline and online RL benchmarks.
8qlkkwGIod.main_concern: Experiments do not isolate whether gains come from the generative Bayes critic rule itself or merely from auxiliary action-modeling supervision alongside scalar TD anchoring.

KWim28wajX.one_liner: Mitigates protagonist bias in LLM relation extraction by separating sentence-by-sentence candidate proposal from local-evidence selection.
KWim28wajX.problem: LLM knowledge-graph extractors systematically under-extract relations between supporting entities while over-confidently favoring relations involving a document's primary protagonist entity.
KWim28wajX.method: Through cross-corpus audits, entity-swap counterfactuals, and mechanistic analyses, the authors trace extraction disparities and confidence inflation to global document-role cues. They decouple generation into a sentence-by-sentence extractor that proposes evidence-anchored candidate relations and a local-evidence selector that filters unsupported pairs.
KWim28wajX.key_idea: Decouple document-level entity prominence from extraction by proposing candidate relations sentence by sentence and filtering them solely on local sentence evidence.
KWim28wajX.evidence: Supported by cross-corpus error audits, entity-swap counterfactuals, and attention interventions across three biomedical datasets, with full-pipeline evaluation on BioRED using Qwen3.5-27B.
KWim28wajX.claimed_gains: On BioRED, the two-stage pipeline improves Qwen3.5-27B by 0.07 F1 over standard fine-tuning and raises supporting-entity precision from 0.54 to 0.68.
KWim28wajX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the empirical and counterfactual diagnosis of lower extraction recall on supporting versus protagonist entities is thorough and convincing.
KWim28wajX.main_concern: Full-pipeline mitigation gains are small and tested mainly on 100 BioRED abstracts (with negative transfer on BC5CDR), while prominence bias is intertwined with sparser textual evidence.

5MJt9SIJOF.one_liner: Adapts the Muon optimizer to verifiable-reward RL by orthogonalizing QKV heads separately and removing momentum.
5MJt9SIJOF.problem: Applying standard pretraining Muon configurations directly to reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards yields inconsistent gains and premature training plateaus.
5MJt9SIJOF.method: The authors modify Muon for on-policy RLVR by splitting fused QKV matrices so Newton-Schulz orthogonalization operates per attention head—preserving cross-head gradient agreement—and setting momentum to zero to avoid scale-invariant displacement from uncorrelated policy gradients.
5MJt9SIJOF.key_idea: Apply Newton-Schulz orthogonalization separately to each QKV head linear operator and disable momentum during on-policy verifiable-reward reinforcement learning.
5MJt9SIJOF.evidence: Evaluated on RLVR post-training using AdamW-pretrained Qwen3-4B-Base and Muon-pretrained Moonlight-16B-A3B-Instruct against AdamW and SignSGD baselines.
5MJt9SIJOF.claimed_gains: Reaches 29.17% versus 24.47% macro-averaged Pass@1 against AdamW on Qwen3-4B-Base and 32.60% versus 31.29% macro-averaged Pass@1 against SignSGD on Moonlight-16B-A3B-Instruct.
5MJt9SIJOF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the paper identifies practical, zero-overhead Muon implementation choices that improve RLVR accuracy and analyzes why standard settings fail.
5MJt9SIJOF.main_concern: Per-head QKV splitting and momentum removal have prior precedent, experiments cover only two models, and missing zero-momentum AdamW and learning-rate sweeps weaken causal attribution.

97ONWAXMps.one_liner: Synthesizes diverse cooperative teammate populations by prompting LLMs for behavioral descriptions and executable policy code.
97ONWAXMps.problem: Trajectory-based diversity metrics in multi-agent reinforcement learning conflate low-level state variations with genuinely distinct high-level coordination strategies.
97ONWAXMps.method: PopGen prompts an LLM to generate a semantically diverse set of high-level behavioral descriptions for an environment and translates each description directly into executable Python policy code with iterative refinement. A cooperator RL policy is then trained against this scripted population to generalize to unseen partners.
97ONWAXMps.key_idea: Specify teammate strategy diversity in natural language via an LLM and ground each behavior directly as executable policy code.
97ONWAXMps.evidence: Evaluated on zero-shot coordination and population-scaling experiments across four collaborative multi-agent environments including Overcooked and Level-Based Foraging.
97ONWAXMps.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that specifying teammate diversity in natural language and compiling behaviors directly into fast executable code policies is clean, modular, and avoids costly partner RL.
97ONWAXMps.main_concern: Purely scripted code policies struggle to scale beyond simple grid-worlds, evaluation lacks human partners, and the semantic-generation pipeline is incremental over SemDiv.

KtkWYpSSDB.one_liner: A recurrent diagonal preconditioner replaces Newton solves with first-order warm-start iterations for interior-point optimization.
KtkWYpSSDB.problem: Interior-point Newton directions require costly second-order information and linear solves, while barrier singularities complicate learned updates and warm starts.
KtkWYpSSDB.method: pdLIP uses a coordinate-wise recurrent network to predict positive diagonal scalings of reduced Newton right-hand sides, recovers other directions analytically, and trains on self-supervised merit and residual losses.
KtkWYpSSDB.key_idea: Predict a positive diagonal scaling of the reduced Newton right-hand side, recovering remaining primal-dual directions analytically.
KtkWYpSSDB.evidence: Evaluations reported in reviews cover quadratic programs and nonlinear problems including a quadrotor task, measuring pdProj refinement iterations and total runtime.
KtkWYpSSDB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that structured learned diagonal scaling naturally targets the main solve cost and shows promising refinement and runtime reductions.
KtkWYpSSDB.main_concern: Reviewers most often cite missing matched nonlearned-scaling controls and limited evidence on general nonlinear problems.

2tyOKrDMss.one_liner: Autoregressive Gumbel couplings distill token generation into straight one-step or two-step continuous flow maps.
2tyOKrDMss.problem: Few-step continuous language generation needs noise-data couplings and objectives that preserve useful pretrained autoregressive behavior.
2tyOKrDMss.method: GSF uses an autoregressive teacher's Gumbel-noise and one-hot-token coupling to create non-intersecting linear paths, with a flow-map semigroup objective guided by the teacher's tangent.
2tyOKrDMss.key_idea: Couple Gumbel noise to one-hot tokens through an autoregressive teacher, yielding non-intersecting linear paths for flow-map distillation.
2tyOKrDMss.evidence: Pretraining and downstream benchmarks compare one-step and two-step generation against language-generation baselines at comparable model sizes and training data.
2tyOKrDMss.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the Gumbel coupling is original and theoretically motivated, with controlled comparisons showing few-step improvements.
2tyOKrDMss.main_concern: Reviewers most often question low absolute generation quality and the failure to isolate Gumbel coupling from teacher initialization and other changes.

5EWKGwfsax.one_liner: Two-stage memory evolution turns unlabeled agent cases into safety rules without changing model parameters.
5EWKGwfsax.problem: It remains unclear whether LLM agents can improve safety through memory evolution alone without labels or changes to other components.
5EWKGwfsax.method: MOSE first distills safety-relevant knowledge from cases and trajectories using the agent's assessments, then refines memory by contrasting cases with different safety outcomes.
5EWKGwfsax.key_idea: Distill case-level safety assessments into memory, then refine rules by autonomously contrasting cases with different safety outcomes.
5EWKGwfsax.evidence: AgentHarm experiments measure harmful behavior and benign utility, with zero-shot transfer to Agent-SafetyBench and small-unlabeled-support adaptation.
5EWKGwfsax.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that memory-only safety evolution is an interesting option and that experiments include useful transfer, cross-model, and phase ablations.
5EWKGwfsax.main_concern: Reviewers most often question the reliability of self-generated safety judgments and the limited statistical evidence for safety-utility improvements.

Q5fGk7srce.one_liner: A frozen prior-fitted network adapts continually through Bayesian in-context inference over latent concepts.
Q5fGk7srce.problem: Continual parameter optimization risks overwriting prior knowledge when models encounter new domains and classes.
Q5fGk7srce.method: Latent Concept PFN is meta-trained and frozen, adding exemplars to an evidence set for posterior inference over latent concepts, with concept annotations used only as soft meta-training anchors.
Q5fGk7srce.key_idea: Replace gradient updates with posterior updates over latent concepts as new exemplars extend an in-context evidence set.
Q5fGk7srce.evidence: Class-incremental and domain-incremental datasets test adaptation without task identity, including EMNIST-to-MNIST transfer noted by reviewers.
Q5fGk7srce.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that frozen in-context adaptation is a clean probabilistic alternative with competitive results and interpretable concept readouts.
Q5fGk7srce.main_concern: Reviewers most often question evaluation fairness because concept supervision and architecture differ from baselines and concept contributions are not isolated.

G2opIiGYPk.one_liner: Auxiliary verifiable roles transfer across shared parameters to improve a language model's primary reasoning task.
G2opIiGYPk.problem: Single-role reinforcement learning optimizes answer correctness without auxiliary goals that decompose problems or relate examples.
G2opIiGYPk.method: RBRL trains one model in several task-and-reward roles, including distractor identification and template-general solution writing, then evaluates only the primary role without auxiliary inference.
G2opIiGYPk.key_idea: Train one model on primary and auxiliary verifiable objectives over related examples so improvements persist through shared parameters alone.
G2opIiGYPk.evidence: GSM-Symbolic with a distractor clause tests arithmetic transfer, with reviews also reporting reading-comprehension experiments, prompt controls, shuffled rewards, rollout budgets, and view ablations.
G2opIiGYPk.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that removing auxiliary information at inference gives clean evidence of shared-parameter transfer across two task domains.
G2opIiGYPk.main_concern: All reviewers question whether the role formulation adds enough beyond established auxiliary-task reinforcement learning.

t7ryJLliBv.one_liner: Transition, episodic, and confusion memories improve verified speculative execution for LLM agents.
t7ryJLliBv.problem: Stateless agent speculators cannot exploit experience accumulated across earlier tasks and trajectories.
t7ryJLliBv.method: The speculator uses a contrastive transition table, episodic retrieval, and confusion tracking, while verification and side-effect-free pre-launch restrictions preserve the actor's trajectory.
t7ryJLliBv.key_idea: Let the speculator retrieve recurring transitions and past errors while keeping the actor's context and verified trajectory unchanged.
t7ryJLliBv.evidence: Six benchmarks span action, observation, and chained prediction across three speculation types and speculators of varying cost.
t7ryJLliBv.claimed_gains: Memory augmentation improves action-prediction accuracy by approximately 20–39% and achieves up to 2.5 times the observation-prediction accuracy on benchmarks with repetitive structure.
t7ryJLliBv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that attaching memory to the speculator is well motivated and improves prediction across all six benchmarks with thorough ablations.
t7ryJLliBv.main_concern: Reviewers most often find acceleration evidence overstated because estimated savings omit realistic delays and integrated end-to-end overhead.

5IK7HoK09U.one_liner: Boundary-aware contraction bounds sharpen global cyclic coordinate-descent rates for box-constrained SVM duals.
5IK7HoK09U.problem: Global linear convergence alone gives little instance-specific guidance for cyclic coordinate descent on box-constrained convex quadratics.
5IK7HoK09U.method: The certificate combines successive-update interactions from the normalized Hessian's triangular part with a matrix lower bound on objective growth, covering singular Hessians, nonunique minimizers, and clipped updates.
5IK7HoK09U.key_idea: Combine successive-coordinate interactions with boundary-dependent objective growth to certify contraction even for singular Hessians and clipped updates.
5IK7HoK09U.evidence: Theoretical comparisons with Wang–Lin bounds, a singular two-coordinate construction, and numerical evaluations assess instance-specific worst-case contraction certificates.
5IK7HoK09U.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that incorporating active-boundary geometry is mathematically insightful and strictly improves prior guarantees under matched assumptions.
5IK7HoK09U.main_concern: Reviewers most often question practical value because certificates remain far looser than observed rates and require expensive dense spectral computations.

mzpcQFwCfJ.one_liner: Coupled sparse autoencoders jointly enforce complementary objectives for instance-level concept alignment.
mzpcQFwCfJ.problem: Concept-alignment methods optimize different properties under shared terminology, and success on one property does not imply the others.
mzpcQFwCfJ.method: The framework separates representations from concepts and instance-wise from distributional alignment, introduces InterVenchA, and proposes CoSAE to jointly enforce complementary objectives with paired-data anchoring.
mzpcQFwCfJ.key_idea: Jointly optimize translation and concept consistency at instance and distributional levels, using scarce paired examples to anchor alignment.
mzpcQFwCfJ.evidence: Theory and experiments combine real embeddings, controlled shared/private factors, human judgments, and InterVenchA measurements of extraction, translation, and concept consistency.
mzpcQFwCfJ.claimed_gains: The abstract reports that as little as 0.1% paired data is sufficient to recover instance-level alignment.
mzpcQFwCfJ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that separating translation and concept consistency is useful and that the benchmark and controlled evaluations clarify alignment quality.
mzpcQFwCfJ.main_concern: Reviewers most often cite unclear loss, metric, and regularization descriptions, with one review also identifying errors in the linear CCA analysis.

NWeKVnkpis.one_liner: Public transition priors and DP record-conditioned adaptations synthesize coherent longitudinal image pairs.
NWeKVnkpis.problem: DP image synthesis focuses on individual images rather than coherent longitudinal changes that agree with associated sensitive records.
NWeKVnkpis.method: DPLongSyn learns a transition prior from public pairs, generates DP synthetic records, adapts transitions with DP-SGD, and applies record-conditioned deformations to public source images.
NWeKVnkpis.key_idea: Learn longitudinal transitions from public pairs, then privately adapt record-conditioned deformations applied to public source images.
NWeKVnkpis.evidence: Three benchmarks compare synthetic-data quality, longitudinal consistency, and downstream utility against DP synthesis baselines.
NWeKVnkpis.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that dividing public appearance learning from private transition adaptation is well motivated and performs well across datasets.
NWeKVnkpis.main_concern: Reviewers most often question comparison fairness and reproducibility because baselines use different training protocols and lack equivalent public-source information.

02y1I1bF6v.one_liner: Scale-conditioned source-pair attention and frequency-banded residuals extrapolate physical fields to more sources.
02y1I1bF6v.problem: Physical-field prediction must extrapolate from low-source supervision to higher-order configurations without exhaustive characterization.
02y1I1bF6v.method: ScaleComposer separately attends over sources and source pairs by location and scale, sharing parameters across source counts and projecting decoded residual corrections onto prescribed frequency bands.
02y1I1bF6v.key_idea: Aggregate source and pair relations separately at each location and scale, then restrict decoded residual corrections to prescribed frequency bands.
02y1I1bF6v.evidence: Measured multi-ceiling-fan airflow and six controlled two-dimensional Navier–Stokes regimes test extrapolation from one or two sources to as many as six.
02y1I1bF6v.claimed_gains: On measurements, ScaleComposer reduces MAE by approximately 8.2% relative to the strongest evaluated baseline; separate source and pair attention lowers MAE by 4.8%, while band restriction lowers it by 11.8%.
02y1I1bF6v.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that source-count extrapolation is meaningful and that airflow and controlled Navier–Stokes experiments provide useful comparisons and ablations.
02y1I1bF6v.main_concern: Reviewers most often question statistical support because the real test set contains only one configuration per higher source count.

F2Gf9kssdG.one_liner: Per-token gauge symmetry decouples rotational motion from recurrent reasoning to accelerate quotient-space convergence.
F2Gf9kssdG.problem: Slow oscillatory modes bottleneck recurrent reasoners, but indiscriminate damping can disrupt the computations those modes support.
F2Gf9kssdG.method: QRR introduces exact token-local phase-rotation symmetry so motion along gauge directions leaves reasoning-relevant quotient representations unchanged and dynamically decoupled.
F2Gf9kssdG.key_idea: Add token-local phase rotations that leave reasoning-relevant quotient dynamics unchanged, separating gauge motion from convergence and halting.
F2Gf9kssdG.evidence: Local dynamical analyses and interventions motivate QRR, with empirical comparisons on Sudoku, Maze, and Mini-ARC measuring convergence and task performance.
F2Gf9kssdG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the oscillation diagnosis is rigorous and quantitatively tested and that gauge symmetry gives a principled architectural response.
F2Gf9kssdG.main_concern: Reviewers most often question whether the theory and quotient-space metrics establish faster reasoning rather than a changed halting measurement.

2ZouxEEncH.one_liner: Simplicial wavelet encoders and transport-preserving latents represent and generate high-dimensional point-cloud cohorts.
2ZouxEEncH.problem: Cohort-level point-cloud analysis needs representations that preserve transport geometry while supporting generation of entire datasets.
2ZouxEEncH.method: RhinoNet encodes Vietoris–Rips simplicial complexes with wavelets and MLPs, regularizes autoencoder latents by optimal-transport distances, and decodes samples from flow matching or geodesic interpolation.
2ZouxEEncH.key_idea: Encode each point cloud as a Vietoris–Rips simplicial complex and regularize latent distances to preserve pairwise optimal-transport geometry.
2ZouxEEncH.evidence: Single-cell and spatial patient cohorts evaluate phenoscape organization and point-cloud generation through latent flow matching and geodesic interpolation.
2ZouxEEncH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that population-level transport-aware representations and decoding address a useful biological analysis problem.
2ZouxEEncH.main_concern: Reviewers most often question novelty and missing close baselines, alongside scalability and unclear biological validation.

MqteSjzV2T.one_liner: Injects sparsely sampled short-term visual history into VLA backbones via cross-attention and gated intermediate feature fusion.
MqteSjzV2T.problem: Vision-language-action policies conditioned only on current observations suffer from temporal ambiguity when identical states require different actions based on history.
MqteSjzV2T.method: HIPPOVLA maintains a Short-Term Memory Bank (STMB) of sparsely sampled historical visual features across selected layers and camera views. It retrieves relevant context via cross-attention and merges it through learnable gates into intermediate visual pathways without lengthening the language-model token sequence.
MqteSjzV2T.key_idea: Fuses cross-attended historical visual features into intermediate backbone pathways via learnable gates without appending extra history tokens to the VLM.
MqteSjzV2T.evidence: Evaluated on CALVIN ABC->D, four LIBERO suites, and real-world repeated pick-and-place manipulation against no-STMB baselines and ablations.
MqteSjzV2T.claimed_gains: On CALVIN ABC->D, HIPPOVLA raises average completed sequence length from 4.085 to 4.619 and five-instruction success from 71.2% to 83.0%, reaches 98.5% mean success on LIBERO, and improves real-world two- and three-cycle pick-and-place success by 30.0 and 26.7 percentage points.
MqteSjzV2T.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that injecting historical visual features into intermediate layers avoids sequence-length overhead and shows solid gains on CALVIN and real-robot tasks.
MqteSjzV2T.main_concern: Reviewers note limited novelty over existing memory-based VLAs, single-level fusion outperforming the proposed multi-level design in ablations, and ceiling effects on LIBERO.

PABg2rnvQm.one_liner: Measures LLM sycophancy across tasks, models, and pressure tactics, showing verification cost and task type dominate concession rates.
PABg2rnvQm.problem: Sycophancy is typically reported as a single aggregate rate per model, obscuring when models yield to user pushback and why.
PABg2rnvQm.method: The authors evaluate eight LLMs (and two with maximum reasoning) across 200 items, 13 pressure tactics, and four-turn dialogues graded by two LLM judges. They fit a logistic model and vary solver-certified clue counts on logic puzzles to isolate task type, verification cost, model family, and tactic effects.
PABg2rnvQm.key_idea: Uses solver-certified clue-count logic puzzles and multi-factor logistic regression over 103,939 replies to separate task verifiability from model and tactic effects.
PABg2rnvQm.evidence: Experiments on 103,939 responses from eight LLMs across 200 items and 13 pressure conditions, with human annotation and dual-judge robustness checks.
PABg2rnvQm.claimed_gains: Removing task type from a logistic model costs 0.485 of McFadden R^2 versus 0.139 for model family and 0.009 for pressure tactic; anchored facts are conceded 1.3% of the time, personal choices 77.0%, and deep-puzzle adoption at maximum reasoning drops from 19.2% and 12.5% to 0% when models complete their first answer.
PABg2rnvQm.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the large-scale, multi-factor experimental design and the solver-based manipulation of verification cost.
PABg2rnvQm.main_concern: Reviewers question whether personal-choice endorsement counts as sycophancy, note confounding between verification cost and puzzle difficulty, and observe that final-turn pooling may mask first-turn tactic differences.

4kLlUj4bJa.one_liner: Adds per-query learned gating to decay-based positional encodings so each token independently balances recency bias and long-range recall.
4kLlUj4bJa.problem: Existing positional encodings trade off language modeling, long-range recall, and length extrapolation rather than excelling at all three.
4kLlUj4bJa.method: Query-Dependent Decay (QDecay) attaches a lightweight query-conditioned control on top of a decay-based encoding like ALiBi. Each query independently scales its attention decay intensity, choosing between strong local recency or zero decay for distant recall without affecting other queries.
4kLlUj4bJa.key_idea: Lets each query independently modulate its attention decay intensity on top of ALiBi to switch between local recency and zero-decay distant recall.
4kLlUj4bJa.evidence: Evaluated on language modeling benchmarks, RULER 32K+ long-context recall, length extrapolation, and hybrid architectures at 250M and 800M scales.
4kLlUj4bJa.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that query-dependent decay is simple and meaningfully extends ALiBi's usable context window and long-range recall at low cost.
4kLlUj4bJa.main_concern: Reviewers point out missing baselines such as ALiBi + NoPE and RoPE context-extension methods (e.g., YaRN), single-seed training, and small 250M-800M model scales.

ii2utca7ga.one_liner: Applies sparse autoencoders and an automated feature-characterization pipeline to map and steer representations in time series foundation models.
ii2utca7ga.problem: Time series foundation models perform strongly zero-shot, yet their internal latent representations remain largely uncharacterized.
ii2utca7ga.method: The authors train sparse autoencoders (SAEs) on TSFM activations to extract disentangled temporal features. They introduce Zeitgeist, an unsupervised pipeline that builds a characterizing atlas of each feature's activating geometry, automated caption, frequency, locality, and positional affinity, and uses features for activation steering.
ii2utca7ga.key_idea: Trains sparse autoencoders on TSFMs and automatically characterizes latent features across five geometric, temporal, and semantic dimensions for interpretability and steering.
ii2utca7ga.evidence: Tested across 9 TSFMs spanning 3 architectural families, with synthetic concept probing and activation-steering case studies.
ii2utca7ga.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the broad, systematic empirical study across multiple TSFM families and the structured taxonomy of temporal feature properties.
ii2utca7ga.main_concern: Reviewers note limited algorithmic novelty over existing SAE pipelines, lack of error bars and human caption validation, and anecdotal steering evidence.

czygDRL3wv.one_liner: Aligns local ECG and EEG segments with paired global cross-modal context via contrastive learning for emotion recognition.
czygDRL3wv.problem: Segmenting long ECG-EEG recordings under recording-level emotion labels introduces noisy segment supervision and underuses cross-modal physiological synchrony.
czygDRL3wv.method: HB-IGCL replaces segment-level emotion supervision with bidirectional contrastive learning that matches local ECG or EEG instances against global representations of the paired modality within the same recording. A spatial-guided alignment module (SGAM) further relates lead-level spatial structure to global temporal context.
czygDRL3wv.key_idea: Trains bidirectional instance-to-global contrastive alignment between synchronized ECG and EEG segments instead of propagating noisy recording-level emotion labels.
czygDRL3wv.evidence: Subject-independent evaluations on AMIGOS, DREAMER, and MPED across five encoders and five random seeds.
czygDRL3wv.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that avoiding noisy segment-level emotion labels via within-recording ECG-EEG correspondence is well-motivated and thoroughly tested across encoders.
czygDRL3wv.main_concern: Reviewers note inconsistent pretraining gains over random initialization across datasets, limited novelty over MIL-NCE, and missing state-of-the-art cross-subject emotion baselines.

Hg1CwPAhbK.one_liner: Decouples chance-constrained optimization from feasibility via single-scenario subproblems and GPU-batched simulation.
Hg1CwPAhbK.problem: Standard chance-constrained stochastic programming approaches either embed scenarios directly at high computational cost or use conservative reformulations that sacrifice objective quality.
Hg1CwPAhbK.method: ACCESS generates candidate solutions by solving inexpensive parameterized single-scenario subproblems and evaluates feasibility separately using GPU-batched simulation over many scenarios. This reduces search to a two-dimensional parameter space over conservatism and scenario diversity, with an ACCESS(delta) variant offering certified feasibility.
Hg1CwPAhbK.key_idea: Generates candidates from parameterized single-scenario subproblems and evaluates feasibility via GPU-parallel simulation over a two-dimensional conservatism and diversity space.
Hg1CwPAhbK.evidence: The framework is supported by a theoretical feasibility guarantee for ACCESS(delta) with probability 1-delta and numerical experiments across three benchmark problem classes and multiple uncertainty distributions.
Hg1CwPAhbK.claimed_gains: ACCESS(delta) provides certified feasibility guarantees with probability 1-delta, while numerical experiments across three benchmarks show gains in solution quality and feasibility.
Hg1CwPAhbK.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that decoupling candidate generation from GPU-based feasibility evaluation is intuitive, computationally effective, and well supported by the two-parameter formulation and experiments.
Hg1CwPAhbK.main_concern: Reviewers question whether Bayesian optimization is needed over random or grid search, note unfairness in conservative baselines, and highlight missing scalability and convergence guarantees.

m98SlxCOQT.one_liner: Diagnoses VLM visual self-correction by replaying single false visual premises alongside the original image.
m98SlxCOQT.problem: Vision-language models fail to overturn their own earlier erroneous visual claims during multi-step reasoning even though the original image remains available.
m98SlxCOQT.method: The authors introduce false-premise replay, extracting a single answer-relevant visual claim contradicted by the image from a failed trace and replaying it with the image and question. They consolidate 217 premise pairs into a shared evaluation set to test 19 model configurations and correction baselines.
m98SlxCOQT.key_idea: Extracts one image-contradicted visual claim from a failed trace, discards the remaining trace, and replays it with the original image and question.
