m98SlxCOQT.evidence: Experiments evaluate 19 model configurations (3 proprietary and 16 open-weight, up to 975B parameters) across three model-reviewed evaluation sets and a shared 217-pair set.
m98SlxCOQT.claimed_gains: Across three model-reviewed evaluation sets, false-premise replay lowers accuracy relative to a fresh query by 25.8–31.0 percentage points.
m98SlxCOQT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that the paper addresses an important problem in VLM multi-step reasoning and provides a methodical, diagnostic false-premise replay protocol.
m98SlxCOQT.main_concern: Reviewers raise concerns about the small 217-pair dataset size, low candidate acceptance rate (4.9–6.7%), incomplete human verification, and unclear sampling details.

TSf1dTaq6g.one_liner: Analyzes clustered conformal calibration via threshold-indicator correlation and tail dependence to derive design effects and cluster floors.
TSf1dTaq6g.problem: Clustered calibration data makes conformal prediction coverage highly variable across calibration sets and new deployment sites, which raw intraclass correlation fails to capture.
TSf1dTaq6g.method: The authors derive an exact finite-sample design-effect identity governed by the correlation of the threshold indicator and show its convergence to the upper tail-dependence coefficient at high confidence. They also prove a distribution-free PAC cluster floor and propose a pooled design-effect correction and finite-sample certification rule.
TSf1dTaq6g.key_idea: Characterizes calibration variability through threshold-indicator correlation and its high-confidence limit as upper tail dependence, yielding a pooled design-effect correction.
TSf1dTaq6g.evidence: The work is supported by finite-sample theorems and evaluations on real-world imaging and cellular datasets with multiple clusters.
TSf1dTaq6g.claimed_gains: Distribution-free PAC validity requires at least log(delta)/log(1-alpha) calibration clusters, which equals 22 when alpha=delta=0.1.
TSf1dTaq6g.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that clustered conformal calibration is a highly relevant problem, particularly in medical domains, and appreciate the mathematical analysis and real-world evaluation.
TSf1dTaq6g.main_concern: One reviewer notes restrictive assumptions that new test sites come from the same marginal distribution without covariate shift and lack worst-case site guarantees.

0qGAC6KQj3.one_liner: Accelerates batched MoE decoding without retraining using dual-sparse route deletion and offline gate-weight rectification.
0qGAC6KQj3.problem: Batched decoding in Mixture-of-Experts models activates many experts across requests, increasing latency, while naive expert skipping degrades accuracy and uncalibrates surviving gate weights.
0qGAC6KQj3.method: DelMoE builds a backbone from high-priority native routes, reuses its experts across requests, and deletes out-of-set routes via a custom vLLM CUDA backend for variable-length workloads. It also applies an offline-calibrated rectification coefficient per model to rescale surviving gate weights.
0qGAC6KQj3.key_idea: Deletes non-backbone token-expert routes to cut active experts and routes simultaneously, then rescales surviving gate weights with an offline-calibrated coefficient.
0qGAC6KQj3.evidence: Experiments evaluate DelMoE in vLLM across three MoE models and eight benchmarks, measuring both accuracy and end-to-end decoding latency.
0qGAC6KQj3.claimed_gains: DelMoE accelerates batched MoE decoding by up to 2.49x at comparable or higher average accuracy without retraining.
0qGAC6KQj3.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that deleting routes alongside expert reduction is clear and intuitive, and appreciate the retraining-free vLLM implementation and controlled comparisons.
0qGAC6KQj3.main_concern: Reviewers point out that the evaluated MoE models are small or outdated (<30B), benchmarks are near saturation, and accuracy and speed are measured under different batching setups.

TEk0otWLkb.one_liner: Synthesizes most-exciting-inputs for early and intermediate human visual cortex using receptive-field-constrained encoding models.
TEk0otWLkb.problem: Synthesizing most-exciting-inputs for early and mid-level retinotopic visual cortex areas from fMRI data fails without spatial constraints due to small receptive field sizes.
TEk0otWLkb.method: The authors introduce RF-DiVE and RF-GO, which both use a population receptive field (pRF)-constrained voxelwise encoding model. RF-DiVE pairs this model with a pretrained latent diffusion model, whereas RF-GO uses regularized gradient ascent to optimize stimuli for single voxels.
TEk0otWLkb.key_idea: Combines a pRF-constrained voxelwise encoding model with either latent diffusion (RF-DiVE) or regularized gradient ascent (RF-GO) to synthesize localized single-voxel stimuli.
TEk0otWLkb.evidence: Experiments apply both frameworks across two encoding backbones on Natural Scenes Dataset fMRI data from four subjects and areas V1-hV4, validated in silico by independent encoding models.
TEk0otWLkb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that incorporating receptive field constraints to synthesize single-voxel stimuli in early visual areas and validating them in silico across models is relevant and systematic.
TEk0otWLkb.main_concern: Reviewers question the methodological novelty over BrainDiVE and existing encoding models, note the lack of real brain response measurements, and request quantitative cross-backbone comparisons.

4D95LPpoMp.one_liner: Couples diffusion sampler trajectory losses through path-measure importance weighting to penalize mode collapse without extra forward passes.
4D95LPpoMp.problem: Single-trajectory reverse-KL estimators for diffusion samplers evaluate trajectories independently and suffer from mode collapse.
4D95LPpoMp.method: The authors introduce Inter-Trajectory Importance Sampling (ITIS), a multi-sample training loss that couples trajectory losses via analytical path-measure importance weights, preserving the expected gradient and i.i.d. inference without extra forward passes or heuristic particle forces.
4D95LPpoMp.key_idea: Reweighting batch losses with cross-trajectory path-measure importance weights assigns lower realized loss to diverse batches while preserving the unbiased reverse-KL gradient.
4D95LPpoMp.evidence: Theoretical analysis of expected gradients and loss ratios, plus experiments integrating ITIS into DDS, DIS, and PIS on standard benchmarks and interacting-particle systems.
4D95LPpoMp.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate that ITIS is a simple, versatile drop-in loss modification that requires no extra forward passes and improves DDS, DIS, and PIS.
4D95LPpoMp.main_concern: Reviewers warn that cross-trajectory importance weights suffer from exponential variance growth and weight degeneracy in high dimensions or small noise regimes, and note missing variance analysis and O(K^2) runtime tests.

MLm03UHRyi.one_liner: Trains block-sparse featurizers on VLA models to recover multi-dimensional features for causal action steering and data shaping.
MLm03UHRyi.problem: Standard scalar sparse autoencoders struggle to cleanly represent multi-dimensional continuous features in vision-language-action (VLA) robot models.
MLm03UHRyi.method: The authors train block-sparse featurizers (BSFs) on VLA activations to represent features in low-dimensional subspaces, validate them via activation steering of perception and action, and use feature-based data attribution to identify and mask training tokens linked to failure recovery.
MLm03UHRyi.key_idea: Grouping latent features into low-dimensional blocks matches the multi-dimensional geometry of robot perception, state, and control variables for steering and data attribution.
MLm03UHRyi.evidence: Controlled BSF vs. SAE comparisons on unpooled VLA activations, closed-loop semantic steering (60 trials across 3 object pairs), and DROID failure-recovery masking experiments.
MLm03UHRyi.claimed_gains: Masking fewer than 1.4% (1.38%) of training tokens delays failure recovery (sevenfold increase in gripper reopening time) while preserving task success; closed-loop semantic steering reaches 93.3% task completion.
MLm03UHRyi.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the controlled BSF-vs-SAE comparison on unpooled activations and the compelling data-attribution experiment for failure recovery.
MLm03UHRyi.main_concern: Reviewers note limited novelty over prior BSF and VLA-SAE work, narrow closed-loop evaluation (only semantic steering on 3 object pairs, 5 recovery trials, single seed), and inconsistent advantages over SAEs.

N3H3E6kgHZ.one_liner: Learns predictive spectral skill latent interfaces and orthogonal skill directions for hierarchical humanoid whole-body control.
N3H3E6kgHZ.problem: Hierarchical humanoid controllers require a planner-controller command interface that executes accurately, predicts easily, and composes behaviors without reconstruction-based limitations.
N3H3E6kgHZ.method: They learn compact latent spectral skills from short motion segments by predicting subsequent motion rather than reconstructing inputs, using an affine predictor to extract orthogonal skill directions. A frozen skill-conditioned controller chains skills without transition policies and composes behaviors by adding orthogonal directions to base skills.
N3H3E6kgHZ.key_idea: Encodes short motion segments into predictive latent skills and extracts orthogonal affine-predictor directions for compositional humanoid control.
N3H3E6kgHZ.evidence: Evaluated on a 29-DoF humanoid, Unitree G1 hardware with a language-conditioned planner, and tracking, chaining, and composition tasks.
N3H3E6kgHZ.claimed_gains: Reduces global tracking error by 62% relative to the state-of-the-art on a 29-DoF humanoid.
N3H3E6kgHZ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the predictive skill interface problem is well-motivated and achieves strong motion tracking performance.
N3H3E6kgHZ.main_concern: Reviewers note that Proposition 3.1's affine linearity holds only for single-step denoising rather than full physical rollouts, and compositionality/unseen-combination evidence is limited.

YLPNslzjLs.one_liner: Introduces a 1.9K-image layer decomposition benchmark with operational editability metrics and a human-preference-aligned reward model.
YLPNslzjLs.problem: Existing layer decomposition evaluations prioritize pixel reconstruction, allowing uneditable flat copies to score well while ignoring human preferences.
YLPNslzjLs.method: LayerBench curates 1.9K multi-layer images and 13,979 expert pairwise comparisons to train LayerReward, a five-dimensional evaluator combining rule-based editability/alignment probes and VLM scores that also guides LayerCompass post-training.
YLPNslzjLs.key_idea: Pairs operational editing probes with a five-dimensional reward model trained on 13,979 expert comparisons for evaluation and RL post-training.
YLPNslzjLs.evidence: Benchmark evaluations on LayerBench, out-of-distribution shadow separation, blind human studies, and LayerCompass post-training experiments.
YLPNslzjLs.claimed_gains: LayerReward exceeds 80% overall pairwise accuracy on human preferences.
YLPNslzjLs.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that LayerBench addresses a genuine blind spot by evaluating operational editability and human preference rather than reconstruction alone.
YLPNslzjLs.main_concern: LayerCompass evaluation partly reuses its training reward (LayerReward) and shared VLM backbone, untuned VLM judge baselines are missing, and most benchmark examples have only two or three layers.

XLXTYlzcFF.one_liner: Analyzes and tests how introducing forget-set data early versus late in pretraining affects machine unlearning difficulty.
XLXTYlzcFF.problem: Unlearning benchmarks typically inject forget sets via post-pretraining fine-tuning, leaving unclear whether knowledge acquired earlier during pretraining is harder to unlearn.
XLXTYlzcFF.method: The authors theoretically analyze forget-set influence along optimization trajectories and in a two-layer linear model. Empirically, they train language models from scratch while varying when the forget set is introduced, then apply multiple unlearning methods at matched initial forget-set perplexity.
XLXTYlzcFF.key_idea: Controls when forget-set data enters pretraining to show earlier acquisition causes greater parameter displacement from retain-only solutions along shared feature directions.
XLXTYlzcFF.evidence: Supported by optimization-trajectory theory, two-layer linear model analysis, and from-scratch language model training across two model families and four unlearning methods.
XLXTYlzcFF.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that questioning whether post-training unlearning benchmarks transfer to pretraining knowledge is important and well-motivated by theory and controlled training.
XLXTYlzcFF.main_concern: Reviewers note that keeping the forget set in training from introduction until the end confounds acquisition timing with total exposure duration and repetition count.

EiDDxv3BPQ.one_liner: Studies test-time compute for tabular foundation models via diagonal query-key adaptation, greedy ensemble selection, and retrieval.
EiDDxv3BPQ.problem: It is unclear which test-time compute mechanisms—adaptation, aggregation, or context construction—effectively improve modern tabular foundation models.
EiDDxv3BPQ.method: They evaluate three axes on TabPFN-3 and other TFMs, proposing DiagScale (a diagonal query-key similarity update), testing greedy selection over 96 configuration pools, and assessing attention-guided context retrieval.
EiDDxv3BPQ.key_idea: Decomposes TFM test-time compute into parameter-efficient diagonal query-key adaptation (DiagScale), selective ensemble aggregation, and attention-guided context retrieval.
EiDDxv3BPQ.evidence: Experiments across TabArena and wide/large OpenML tables spanning three independently pretrained TFM backbones.
EiDDxv3BPQ.claimed_gains: DiagScale trains only 0.003%-0.03% of parameters with gains comparable to full fine-tuning; greedy selection over 96 configurations reduces error by 2.4% relative to the default predictor.
EiDDxv3BPQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the systematic decomposition, controlled empirical comparisons, and lightweight DiagScale adaptation.
EiDDxv3BPQ.main_concern: The three test-time axes are studied in isolation without exploring interactions or unified compute budgets, and methodological novelty is modest.

3uy68kAVum.one_liner: Benchmarks single-cell temporal trajectory models on held-out cell fates, lineages, and starting populations.
3uy68kAVum.problem: Existing single-cell temporal benchmarks hold out time points within seen cell types, leaving model generalization to unseen biology untested.
3uy68kAVum.method: CellShift curates seven single-cell RNA-seq time-course datasets—extending three with held-out fates, lineages, and starting populations—and evaluates statistical baselines, neural dynamics models, pretrained models, and LLM agents under a shared evaluator tracking information access.
3uy68kAVum.key_idea: Evaluates single-cell trajectory predictors on held-out biological fates and lineages rather than in-domain intermediate time points.
3uy68kAVum.evidence: Evaluated across seven scRNA-seq time-course datasets including lineage-traced LARRY blood development.
3uy68kAVum.claimed_gains: On held-out fates, no fitted model without target-day cell access improves upon copying the latest observed snapshot by more than 5%.
3uy68kAVum.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree CellShift addresses an important generalization gap in single-cell temporal benchmarking with a broad evaluation.
3uy68kAVum.main_concern: Reviewers note mismatched context conditioning in headline comparisons, omitted established biological dynamics models, and limited diagnostic analysis of why models fail.

z7vXszTjJT.one_liner: Couples probe-based question routing with zero-mean control-variate gradient correction for training search agents.
z7vXszTjJT.problem: Search-agent reinforcement learning suffers from low reward contrast on too-easy or too-hard questions and high-variance policy gradients from sampled trajectories.
z7vXszTjJT.method: A frozen generator creates evidence-grounded questions and independent probes estimate agent success rates to route questions to SFT, RL, or reassessment. For RL, GC-GRPO constructs zero-mean reference gradients from current trajectories combined with weights learned from earlier batches.
z7vXszTjJT.key_idea: Routes questions by probe-estimated success rate and reduces GRPO gradient variance using zero-mean trajectory control variates weighted from prior batches.
z7vXszTjJT.evidence: Evaluates a trained 4B search agent across five search benchmarks (GAIA, BrowseComp, BrowseComp-ZH, SEAL-0, XBench-DS) alongside gradient-error and component ablations.
z7vXszTjJT.claimed_gains: The trained 4B search agent achieves 85.44% accuracy on GAIA, 48.66% on BrowseComp, 47.75% on BrowseComp-ZH, 47.75% on SEAL-0, and 82.00% on XBench-DS.
z7vXszTjJT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers appreciate the variance-reduction construction of GC-GRPO, direct measurement of gradient estimation error, and component ablations.
z7vXszTjJT.main_concern: Reviewers raise that comparisons between adaptive training and direct RL do not account for probing and SFT compute budgets.

uJX9FOWSMd.one_liner: Maps cryo-EM conformational latent spaces to co-folding pair representations via a neural field to generate atomic ensembles.
uJX9FOWSMd.problem: Recovering continuous all-atom conformational landscapes from experimental cryo-EM data remains difficult for inference-time single-structure guidance methods.
uJX9FOWSMd.method: CryoCHEF learns a conformation-conditioned neural field that maps a precomputed cryo-EM conformational latent space into the pair representations of a pretrained co-folding model. This induces a continuous all-atom structural ensemble conditioned on experimental data.
uJX9FOWSMd.key_idea: Learns a neural field mapping from a cryo-EM conformational latent space to pretrained co-folding pair representations to generate continuous atomic ensembles.
uJX9FOWSMd.evidence: Evaluated on synthetic benchmarks and experimental cryo-EM datasets to test side-chain-level detail, conformational motion recovery, and trajectory generation.
uJX9FOWSMd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the framing is useful and that CryoCHEF is a lightweight, general approach for generating continuous atomic ensembles from cryo-EM latent spaces.
uJX9FOWSMd.main_concern: Reviewers note that fine-grained all-atom recovery is only demonstrated on synthetic data, and that advantages over closely related CryoSampler are not clearly established.

adXyi5U5nH.one_liner: Generates long-horizon electronic health records hierarchically by conditioning fine-resolution tokens on a coarse temporal scaffold.
adXyi5U5nH.problem: Fixed-resolution EHR generative models are computationally expensive and error-prone over long horizons, while existing multi-resolution approaches scale poorly.
adXyi5U5nH.method: MuRGEHR represents EHR time series as a hierarchical sequence of tokens across multiple temporal resolutions. It first generates a coarse temporal scaffold and then conditions progressively finer-resolution token generation on that scaffold.
adXyi5U5nH.key_idea: Models EHR trajectories as hierarchical multi-resolution token sequences, generating a coarse scaffold first to condition finer-resolution synthesis.
adXyi5U5nH.evidence: Evaluated across three EHR datasets and multiple prediction horizons (28, 30, 42, and 168 days) on downstream clinical prediction tasks.
adXyi5U5nH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that generating EHR trajectories at multiple temporal resolutions is a well-motivated problem for improving rollout speed and efficiency.
adXyi5U5nH.main_concern: Reviewers cite insufficient support for the multi-resolution design (greedy allocation favors coarse tokens, small vocabulary, and equal-time sample-count confounds) alongside presentation and reference issues.

D5vMct5dzz.one_liner: Splits persistent homology dimension into three minimum-spanning-tree quantile bands to separate lexical and long-range text embedding geometry.
D5vMct5dzz.problem: Standard persistent homology dimension collapses multi-scale token embedding geometry into one value that confounds lexical diversity with longer-range structure.
D5vMct5dzz.method: The authors introduce scale-resolved PHDim using quantile-trimmed minimum spanning tree energies and propose a fixed-budget three-band estimator tailored to the cell-skeleton geometry of contextual token embeddings.
D5vMct5dzz.key_idea: Computes intrinsic dimension separately over quantile-trimmed intervals of minimum spanning tree edge lengths to isolate fine lexical cells from coarse skeleton geometry.
D5vMct5dzz.evidence: Supported by asymptotic consistency theory, synthetic/controlled interventions, and experiments on AI-text detection and text defect profiling in English.
D5vMct5dzz.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers note that decomposing PHDim by edge-length scale clarifies how lexical diversity and repetition affect dimension estimates.
D5vMct5dzz.main_concern: There is a gap between asymptotic fixed-quantile theory and finite-sample scale differences, sensitivity to sample sizes and edge bands is untested, and average AI-human differences do not establish per-text classification.

1RSsIKmXCB.one_liner: Adapts frozen LLMs to EHR event tuples using biomedical text-description priors plus low-rank residuals for rare clinical codes.
1RSsIKmXCB.problem: Serializing EHR (time, modality, code) tuples as text inflates sequence length, while long-tailed clinical codes lack sufficient training examples.
1RSsIKmXCB.method: EHRAdapt maps each EHR tuple to one embedding position in a frozen LLM using learned modality embeddings, elapsed-time attention biases, and code vectors formed by summing a frozen biomedical-LM description prior with a learned low-rank evidence residual.
1RSsIKmXCB.key_idea: Represents each EHR event as a frozen biomedical-LM description prior plus a low-rank learned residual to generalize to rare clinical codes.
1RSsIKmXCB.evidence: Evaluated via continued pretraining on ~4M Kaiser Permanente patients using OLMo2 (1B, 7B) and Llama3 (1B, 8B) backbones, plus infectious-disease and syndromic classification.
1RSsIKmXCB.claimed_gains: Trains only 0.1--0.6% of all parameters while outperforming native-text inputs and next-event prediction baselines on reportable infectious-disease and syndromic classification.
1RSsIKmXCB.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers find the writing clear and the semantic-prior plus residual adapter design well-motivated and rigorously ablated.
1RSsIKmXCB.main_concern: Evaluation is confined to one proprietary dataset (excluding lab/vital numeric values) without comparisons to public EHR benchmarks like MIMIC/EHRShot or strong EHR foundation baselines.

XWfdv4bP6T.one_liner: Deferring RMS scaling until after projection and folding norm weights enables parallel execution without retraining Transformer checkpoints.
XWfdv4bP6T.problem: RMS normalization serializes vector and matrix execution units by blocking the subsequent linear layer during LLM inference.
XWfdv4bP6T.method: FlashNorm folds normalization weights into the following linear layer and moves scalar RMS normalization after matrix multiplication. The reformulation extends to LayerNorm and DyT and removes redundant RMSNorm in specific normalized architectures.
XWfdv4bP6T.key_idea: Exact algebraic reordering folds norm weights into projection weights and defers per-token scaling, allowing normalization and matrix multiplication to run concurrently.
XWfdv4bP6T.evidence: Latency tests use an NVIDIA T4 at SmolLM2-135M and Llama-7B scales, with weight-folding checks on three models and cancellation checks on four additional models.
XWfdv4bP6T.claimed_gains: FlashNorm reduces norm-then-project latency by 33-35% at SmolLM2-135M scale and 12-14% at Llama-7B scale in the compute-bound prefill regime.
XWfdv4bP6T.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that exact post-training reformulation is practically useful and that the paper explains architecture variants and limitations clearly.
XWfdv4bP6T.main_concern: Reviewers consistently cite overlap with established normalization folding and GEMM-epilogue work, leaving the standalone contribution unclear.

im6cgUcEk8.one_liner: Building topic hierarchies from private keyword histograms and LLM classification avoids embedding clustering in differentially private corpus analysis.
im6cgUcEk8.problem: Embedding-based topic discovery loses utility under differential privacy, especially when privacy budgets become restrictive.
im6cgUcEk8.method: CALLIOPE recursively synthesizes topic schemas with LLMs from differentially private keyword partitions, then assigns documents through non-private LLM classification. The top-down pipeline avoids vector-embedding clustering.
im6cgUcEk8.key_idea: Restricting private computation to keyword partition selection lets subsequent LLM schema generation and assignment use differential-privacy post-processing.
im6cgUcEk8.evidence: Experiments compare against embedding-based methods under DP using established clustering metrics and newly introduced utility metrics across privacy regimes.
im6cgUcEk8.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that private keyword histograms create a clear privacy boundary and that the modular recursive design degrades gracefully as privacy tightens.
im6cgUcEk8.main_concern: Two reviewers argue that the contribution is a small extension beyond URANIA and related private discrete-vocabulary discovery methods.

bH2a5BQqiD.one_liner: Audits cross-modal CoT distillation tools and decomposes its side effects into unstated answers, length-driven hallucination, and lost perception with targeted fixes.
bH2a5BQqiD.problem: Benchmark totals and biased evaluation tools obscure whether text-only chain-of-thought distillation truly improves VLM reasoning and what causes its hallucination and perception losses.
bH2a5BQqiD.method: The authors first repair answer-extraction and hallucination-matching evaluation tools, revealing no measurable gain across five benchmarks. They then decompose the distillation cost into three separable parts and apply targeted remedies: forcing conclusions at inference for unstated answers, distilling shorter teacher traces for hallucination, and interpolating weights back toward the base VLM to recover visual perception.
bH2a5BQqiD.key_idea: Repairs biased VLM evaluators and separates distillation side effects into inference-fixable unstated answers, length-induced hallucination, and weight-interpolation-recoverable perception loss.
bH2a5BQqiD.evidence: Evaluated across five benchmarks primarily on Qwen VLM models using repaired extractors, blind-teacher stratification, and training-free weight interpolation.
bH2a5BQqiD.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the thorough audit of evaluation biases, blind-teacher stratification, and simple, training-free mitigation levers.
bH2a5BQqiD.main_concern: Reviewers question generalization beyond Qwen models, note that original VOLD used VLMEvalKit/GPT-4o-mini rather than rule extractors, and view the answer-format and length fixes as mostly configuration tweaks.

6qz2SP77XH.one_liner: Compresses long movies into a persistent character-and-causality representation for agentic QA and introduces the open-ended NEXUS-OEBench benchmark.
6qz2SP77XH.problem: Long-video QA agents either ignore non-subtitle modalities or incur high per-query raw-frame costs, while multiple-choice benchmarks fail to test deep free-form causal reasoning.
6qz2SP77XH.method: NEXUS combines NEXUS-MF, a pipeline converting long videos into a reusable structured representation of character dynamics and causal events, with NEXUS-QA, an agent that verifies evidence chains over that representation. The authors also release NEXUS-OEBench, a human-annotated open-ended QA benchmark of 1,701 pairs across 150+ hours.
6qz2SP77XH.key_idea: Build a reusable multimodal structured representation of character dynamics and event causality once per movie, then run an evidence-verifying QA agent over it.
6qz2SP77XH.evidence: Evaluated on NEXUS-OEBench (1,701 questions across 14 movies/TV shows, 150+ hours), LVBench subsets, MINERVA-Ego, and visual retrieval.
6qz2SP77XH.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that a persistent multimodal representation is a sensible solution to per-query video cost and that open-ended long-narrative QA is a worthwhile resource.
6qz2SP77XH.main_concern: The keypoint-recall metric rewards exhaustive listing without penalizing hallucinations, benchmark questions concentrate heavily in 14 famous titles without contamination or inter-annotator checks, and the SCM framing exceeds prompt-based implementation.

ADINZPrHs1.one_liner: Uses Explorer, Manager, and Verifier LLM agents to build a shared fine-grained item-relation hierarchy for recommender reranking.
ADINZPrHs1.problem: Existing LLM recommender agents rely on coarse substitute/complement labels re-inferred per user, missing specific comparison criteria and shared cross-user relational knowledge.
ADINZPrHs1.method: FIRM constructs a shared hierarchical memory of fine-grained item-pair relations using three LLM agents: Explorer extracts pair relations, Manager merges redundant types and splits mixed criteria into a tree, and Verifier enforces definition consistency. At inference, retrieved item relations and summarized user behavioral tendencies prompt the reranker.
ADINZPrHs1.key_idea: Use three specialized LLM agents to extract, hierarchically canonicalize, and verify fine-grained item-pair relations into a shared memory retrieved for user-conditioned reranking.
ADINZPrHs1.evidence: Evaluated across three recommendation domains, eleven baselines, multiple reranking LLMs, component ablations, and cost analyses on 4,151-7,064 item catalogs.
ADINZPrHs1.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that sharing typed fine-grained item relations across users is well-motivated and backed by careful, consistent reranking experiments.
ADINZPrHs1.main_concern: Evaluation manually inserts ground-truth targets into 20-item candidate lists (83.5%-88.7% of users), the hierarchical Manager/Verifier modules add small gains over uncanonicalized relations, and top-0.1% pairing scales quadratically.

z703A6EB5A.one_liner: Constructs context-matched robust optimization uncertainty sets as unions of local balls around K nearest historical scenario trajectories.
z703A6EB5A.problem: Learned conditional uncertainty sets in two-stage robust optimization can admit unrealistic scenarios poorly matched to the observed context unless complex adversarial constraints are added.
z703A6EB5A.method: CUB-RO retrieves the K nearest historical contexts under a prespecified dissimilarity measure and defines the uncertainty set as a union of local neighborhoods around their paired complete historical scenarios. This embeds context matching directly into set geometry and comes with asymptotic support-convergence and finite-sample excess-cost bounds.
z703A6EB5A.key_idea: Form a conditional uncertainty set as the union of local radii around the complete historical scenarios paired with the K nearest contexts, avoiding extra adversarial constraints.
z703A6EB5A.evidence: Supported by asymptotic convergence and finite-sample bounds plus benchmarks on newsvendor, portfolio optimization, and security-constrained unit commitment (SCUC).
z703A6EB5A.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that anchoring uncertainty sets to retrieved complete historical trajectories is operationally simple and avoids implausible corner-point scenarios.
z703A6EB5A.main_concern: Empirical gains over SAA and KNN-RO are statistically indistinguishable from zero on newsvendor and SCUC (paired bootstrap intervals cross zero), and combining kNN with local balls has limited novelty.

26oJz53EUT.one_liner: Recycles a gated, region-informed contextual state across hierarchical latent grids for entropy modeling and synthesis in overfitted image codecs.
26oJz53EUT.problem: Overfitted image codecs discard entropy-model features after decoding each latent grid, leaving cross-scale contextual dependencies underused for probability estimation and reconstruction.
26oJz53EUT.method: PRISM progressively updates a compact shared contextual state across the latent hierarchy using gated, region-informed updates that adapt to spatially varying structure. The accumulated state conditions both subsequent entropy models and the final image synthesis network.
26oJz53EUT.key_idea: Maintain and recycle a gated, region-informed contextual state across hierarchical latent grids to jointly condition downstream entropy modeling and image synthesis.
26oJz53EUT.evidence: Evaluated on Kodak and CLIC2020 against VTM-19.1, overfitted codecs (including Cool-chic 5.0), and learned codecs like LIC-HPCM, with component ablations.
26oJz53EUT.claimed_gains: Achieves BD-rate reductions of 9.56% on Kodak and 20.35% on CLIC2020 over VTM-19.1.
26oJz53EUT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that recycling cross-scale entropy context in overfitted codecs is an interesting entry point yielding strong rate-distortion performance.
26oJz53EUT.main_concern: Implementation details (e.g., mapping SAM proposals to N=2 regions) are unclear, wall-clock encode/decode times and capacity-matched baselines are missing, and the state-modeling update lacks theoretical justification.

ECMhMhrx4X.one_liner: Compresses smart-glasses VLM split inference via shape-specialized INT8 vision graphs and 256-d INT8 protected packets selected by on-device profiling.
ECMhMhrx4X.problem: Privacy-preserving split VLM inference on smart glasses remains slow and thermally expensive due to on-device vision encoding, wide protected tokens, and hardware-unaware execution.
ECMhMhrx4X.method: SAGE keeps raw images on-device, lowers visual input cost, runs shape-specialized INT8 vision graphs, and compresses protected tokens into 256-dimensional INT8 packets before phone transmission. Operating points are chosen jointly from downstream QA quality and real Mentra Live glasses measurements of latency, memory, and temperature.
ECMhMhrx4X.key_idea: Combines reduced-resolution shape-specialized INT8 on-device vision graphs with 256-dimensional INT8 protected token compression tuned using real smart-glasses latency and thermal profiling.
ECMhMhrx4X.evidence: On-device measurements on Mentra Live smart glasses for a matched Qwen workload, glasses-to-phone transmission tests, and cross-family transfer across four additional VLM families.
ECMhMhrx4X.claimed_gains: Reduces glasses inference latency by 39.18% (40.7% in TL;DR), device-sensor temperature rise by 21.91%, and protected packet size by 96.56% (98.3% transmitted bytes in TL;DR), retaining 85.62% relaxed utility (88.9% in TL;DR) and cutting median packet-plus-ack time from 71.3 to 10.0 ms.
ECMhMhrx4X.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the real-device latency, memory, thermal, and transmission measurements on commercial smart glasses are rare, practical, and valuable.
ECMhMhrx4X.main_concern: Reviewers view the technical novelty as limited—combining standard downscaling, linear compression, INT8, and TGAP—and note missing latency-matched baselines and attack-based privacy evaluations.

Gvz6Z1gWvI.one_liner: Uses label-derived Gaussian-center and interior-distance priors to build Soft-KNN hypergraphs and endpoint prototype contrastive losses for brain tumor segmentation.
Gvz6Z1gWvI.problem: Geometric supervision in medical segmentation typically supervises final outputs without guiding which intermediate decoder features participate in relational representation learning.
Gvz6Z1gWvI.method: DGP-HPCL uses training-label Gaussian center and interior distance priors to select decoder feature locations, connects them via feature-similarity Soft-KNN hyperedges, and constructs two prototypes from the low- and high-center-response tails. Endpoint embeddings are contrasted against both prototypes while middle-ranked nodes aid aggregation, complemented by auxiliary prior prediction and bidirectional consistency during training only.
Gvz6Z1gWvI.key_idea: Selects decoder nodes with dual geometric priors, aggregates Soft-KNN hyperedges, and applies contrastive prototype supervision exclusively to the low- and high-center-response tails during training.
Gvz6Z1gWvI.evidence: Five-fold validation on BraTS 2019, evaluation on BraTS 2021, cross-year transfer tests, and ablations of sampling, aggregation, and prototype supervision.
Gvz6Z1gWvI.claimed_gains: Achieves 82.38% DSC, 73.54% surface Dice, and 6.91 HD95 on BraTS 2019 five-fold validation, and 88.87% DSC, 84.52% surface Dice, and 5.14 HD95 on BraTS 2021.
Gvz6Z1gWvI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the training-only auxiliary design adds no inference overhead and improves BraTS segmentation and boundary metrics with useful ablations.
Gvz6Z1gWvI.main_concern: Reviewers question the motivation and isolation of individual components, noting Soft-KNN hyperedges resemble standard KNN pooling, whole-tumor priors ignore tissue classes, and endpoint ablations confound sparse supervision with tail selection.

xSTazUY0Bd.one_liner: Learns forward-backward successor-measure world models on frozen DINO visual features with a lightweight adaptor for zero-shot pixel control.
xSTazUY0Bd.problem: Predictive world models require test-time planning or policy optimization for new rewards, whereas pixel-based forward-backward (FB) successor-measure models trained from scratch with CNNs struggle.
xSTazUY0Bd.method: SWM extracts frozen DINO visual embeddings from stacked frames and trains a lightweight LayerNorm-Linear adaptor alongside forward and backward successor-measure representations to factorize policy-conditioned future occupancy. At test time, reward-labeled observations are projected onto the backward basis to select a zero-shot policy without online interaction.
xSTazUY0Bd.key_idea: Pairs a frozen DINO encoder and a lightweight LayerNorm-Linear adaptor with forward-backward successor-measure factorization to enable zero-shot policy selection from pixels.
xSTazUY0Bd.evidence: Zero-shot visual control evaluations across 16 pixel-based locomotion and robotic manipulation tasks (Walker, Quadruped, Cheetah, Jaco) and camera/color perturbation tests.
xSTazUY0Bd.claimed_gains: Achieves higher mean zero-shot return than CNN-FB on all sixteen evaluated tasks.
xSTazUY0Bd.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree SWM consistently outperforms CNN-FB across all 16 pixel-based tasks and degrades less under visual perturbations.
xSTazUY0Bd.main_concern: Reviewers judge the methodological novelty limited—mainly plugging frozen DINO features and a LayerNorm-Linear projector into existing FB successor measures—and note the projector ablation does not isolate LayerNorm.

QxqPo2BsGT.one_liner: Jointly optimizes speculative-decoding draft trees and online stopping policies via alternating mixed-integer fractional programming and latency-calibrated net-gain updates.
QxqPo2BsGT.problem: Speculative decoding methods typically optimize draft-tree structures and online drafting-control policies separately, leaving complete-cycle throughput suboptimal.
QxqPo2BsGT.method: OGSPO maximizes expected committed tokens per expected complete-cycle time using a calibrated latency model and posterior verification records. It first solves a mixed-integer fractional program for posterior-optimal decision depths, then alternates policy learning (using residual-corrected same-trace net-gain estimates) and state-weighted tree-structure optimization.
QxqPo2BsGT.key_idea: Alternates mixed-integer fractional tree optimization and trace-corrected online policy updates under a shared latency-calibrated expected-tokens-per-cycle-time objective.
QxqPo2BsGT.evidence: Experiments across multiple LLM families, hardware devices, and temperatures, plus ablations separating tree-structure and controller gains.
QxqPo2BsGT.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree optimizing complete-cycle decoding time jointly over draft trees and online controllers is well formulated and clearly analyzed across models and hardware.
QxqPo2BsGT.main_concern: Reviewers note that evaluation is restricted to batch size 1 without testing concurrent serving or cross-setting transfer, and that novelty and margins over prior adaptive drafting methods are modest.

jPoQNcgeJA.one_liner: Enforces VLA safety at test time by optimizing initial sampling noise with a closed-form control-barrier-function quadratic program.
jPoQNcgeJA.problem: Action-space safety filters for pretrained Vision-Language-Action policies either ignore dependencies across an action chunk or push actions off the policy's learned behavior manifold.
jPoQNcgeJA.method: Noise Safe Corrector (NSC) treats the mapping from initial noise to an action chunk in a frozen VLA policy as deterministic and formulates a control barrier function (CBF) in noise space. It iteratively solves a closed-form quadratic program using policy Jacobians to adjust the noise and regenerate a coordinated, safe action chunk.
jPoQNcgeJA.key_idea: Applies iterative closed-form control-barrier-function QP updates to the frozen VLA's input noise so regenerated action chunks satisfy safety constraints coherently.
jPoQNcgeJA.evidence: Finite-iteration safety-recovery proof under mild assumptions, plus experiments in three simulation environments (including 2D and SafeDetour) and real-world robotic manipulation tasks.
jPoQNcgeJA.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree optimizing initial noise to coordinate full-chunk avoidance without retraining the frozen VLA is a coherent and relevant mechanism.
jPoQNcgeJA.main_concern: Reviewers note that noise-space updates are not compared at matched compute/latency against baselines, optimized noise can drift out-of-distribution, and theoretical recovery assumptions are unverified.

BFlbQe12XX.one_liner: Benchmarks search-augmented LLMs on 515 underspecified and indirectly phrased queries separating target entity recall from multi-answer validity.
BFlbQe12XX.problem: Search benchmarks focus on well-specified queries with a single predetermined answer, overlooking real-world underspecified queries with indirect cues and multiple valid answers.
BFlbQe12XX.method: The authors build a 515-query dataset split into 255 human-authored Entity Recall queries (partial or indirect cues for an intended entity) and 260 Open Discovery queries (explicit criteria with multiple valid answers). They evaluate target recovery, candidate precision/coverage via a criteria verifier, and calibration across seven search-augmented LLMs.
BFlbQe12XX.key_idea: Constructs 515 underspecified Entity Recall and Open Discovery queries and evaluates target recovery separately from web-verifiable multi-candidate precision, coverage, and confidence calibration.
BFlbQe12XX.evidence: Evaluations of seven search-augmented LLMs on 515 queries in a shared search environment, with human validation of the criteria verifier (kappa = 0.78).
BFlbQe12XX.claimed_gains: The strongest evaluated search-augmented LLM recovers only 67.5% of user-intended entities on Entity Recall.
BFlbQe12XX.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree underspecified abstract search is a timely, well-motivated gap and appreciate separating target recovery from candidate validity with human-validated verification.
BFlbQe12XX.main_concern: Reviewers point out that Entity Recall penalizes valid alternatives matching stated constraints when the annotator's hidden target is missed, and adversarial filtering confounds underspecification with general retrieval difficulty.

84vfd0YVhG.one_liner: Eliminates a memory-size shortcut in evidence-sufficiency benchmarks via size-matched construction and evaluates a cross-encoder plus set-transformer detector (MemSafe).
84vfd0YVhG.problem: Constructing insufficient-evidence examples by deleting supporting passages leaks the label through memory length, allowing a simple paragraph counter to achieve 0.979 AUROC.
84vfd0YVhG.method: The authors introduce a size-matched memory construction that provably removes the length shortcut and propose MemSafe, which cross-encodes the query with each memory unit and aggregates unit embeddings using a set transformer to detect insufficient evidence before answering.
84vfd0YVhG.key_idea: Replaces deleted supporting passages with size-matched distractors to remove count shortcuts, then detects evidence sufficiency via query-unit cross-encoding and set-transformer aggregation.
84vfd0YVhG.evidence: Evaluations across MuSiQue, HotpotQA, and 2WikiMultiHopQA over five seeds, plus SQuAD 2.0 transfer, ablations against mean pooling and frozen cross-encoders, and answer-gating tests.
84vfd0YVhG.claimed_gains: Paragraph counting drops from 0.979 AUROC on deletion-based MuSiQue; on size-matched data, MemSafe reaches 0.968 AUROC on MuSiQue and 0.983 on HotpotQA (+0.26 to +0.39 over a lexical baseline), with the set transformer adding 0.020 AUROC over mean pooling on MuSiQue.
84vfd0YVhG.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree exposing the paragraph-count shortcut (0.979 AUROC dropping to chance under size matching) is a clear, consequential finding supported by thorough controls.
84vfd0YVhG.main_concern: Reviewers note that most performance comes from the fine-tuned cross-encoder rather than set attention, synthetic multi-hop QA deletion lacks realism, and transfer to SQuAD 2.0 (0.639 AUROC) and reader gating are weak.

IeSUVoTzWQ.one_liner: Builds a 1M-record chip design dataset with EDA backend feedback using HLS and AI agents, plus 13 LLM evaluation tasks.
IeSUVoTzWQ.problem: AI for chip design lacks large-scale datasets that combine complex, diverse hardware designs with observable EDA feedback from simulation through place-and-route.
IeSUVoTzWQ.method: ChipFactory aggregates hardware designs from generators, compilers, external datasets, human accelerators, and software programs, expanding the latter two via HLS and AI agents into over 1 million records with EDA backend feedback. It also provides reusable agent skills, an open harness, and 13 benchmark tasks covering prediction, ranking, and generation.
IeSUVoTzWQ.key_idea: Combines generators, accelerators, and agent-driven HLS expansions into over 1 million RTL design records paired with simulation-to-place-and-route EDA feedback and a 13-task harness.
IeSUVoTzWQ.evidence: Over 1 million design records (averaging 36K lines of RTL) and evaluations of twelve proprietary, open-source, and domain-specialized LLMs across 13 instantiated tasks.
IeSUVoTzWQ.claimed_gains: Even the strongest evaluated model, Claude Fable 5.1, scores only 58.4 out of 100 on average across the 13 tasks, while the four smallest open-source models solve none of the generation problems.
IeSUVoTzWQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree ChipFactory addresses a major hardware-data shortage with substantial engineering effort, hierarchical agent-refactored designs, and linked EDA backend feedback.
IeSUVoTzWQ.main_concern: Reviewers question dataset quality and validation, noting under 9% of records have retained RTL simulation waveforms, unverified behavioral preservation in agent-written HLS/testbenches, and no finetuning study demonstrating scale value.

Smolv3zuxI.one_liner: Post-trains LLMs with reinforcement learning rewards derived from Integrated Information Theory postulates over discretized hidden-state transitions.
Smolv3zuxI.problem: Prior work only assesses consciousness-related properties in LLMs passively rather than testing what happens when models are explicitly trained to maximize quantitative consciousness metrics.
Smolv3zuxI.method: The authors formulate three RL reward functions inspired by Integrated Information Theory (IIT), including intrinsic information (I_int) and full Phi-based rewards, computed from discrete state transitions obtained via PCA and binary thresholding of hidden representations.
Smolv3zuxI.key_idea: Applies PCA and binary thresholding to LLM hidden states to compute Integrated Information Theory rewards (I_int and Phi) for reinforcement learning post-training.
Smolv3zuxI.evidence: RL training experiments on two base LLMs across reasoning and consciousness-related benchmarks measuring response length, accuracy, and faithfulness.
Smolv3zuxI.claimed_gains: The intrinsic information reward reduces response length by up to 70% while maintaining comparable accuracy and improving reasoning faithfulness; the Phi-reward shows null evidence.
Smolv3zuxI.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree extending IIT to RL training is an ambitious direction, appreciate the honest reporting of null Phi results, and note that I_int reliably shortens responses without explicit length penalties.
Smolv3zuxI.main_concern: Reviewers argue that PCA-binarized statistical transitions do not capture IIT's interventional causal structure, that I_int may simply act as implicit length regularization, and that consciousness claims are overstated.

IfbN0g3XUQ.one_liner: Audits Rényi differential privacy in a black-box setting using class-restricted Donsker-Varadhan variational estimators with finite-sample confidence intervals.
IfbN0g3XUQ.problem: Most privacy auditing targets approximate differential privacy via attack heuristics rather than directly auditing Rényi differential privacy (RDP) with finite-sample statistical guarantees.
IfbN0g3XUQ.method: The authors formulate black-box RDP auditing as hypothesis testing using a class-restricted Donsker-Varadhan (DV) variational estimator of Rényi divergence between neighboring executions. They derive explicit non-asymptotic confidence intervals separating statistical estimation error from privacy leakage and instantiate the auditor on DP-SGD.
IfbN0g3XUQ.key_idea: Estimates Rényi divergence between neighboring black-box runs via a class-restricted Donsker-Varadhan variational estimator with explicit finite-sample confidence bounds.
IfbN0g3XUQ.evidence: Non-asymptotic sample-complexity and confidence-interval proofs, plus black-box DP-SGD auditing experiments on MNIST and CIFAR-10 for Rényi orders in (1, 2].
IfbN0g3XUQ.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree directly auditing RDP with finite-sample variational bounds is valuable and achieves tighter empirical lower bounds in black-box regimes.
IfbN0g3XUQ.main_concern: Reviewers flag a theoretical error in Corollary 3 converting RDP violations to approximate-DP violations, missing citation to prior variational RDP auditing (DP-Auditorium), and instability for alpha > 2.

PaiR6xTSm7.one_liner: Evaluates whether populations of self-improving LLMs that revise and copy skill files outperform solo learners under a shared token budget.
PaiR6xTSm7.problem: Self-improvement typically optimizes one LLM in isolation while multi-agent setups share a joint goal, leaving unclear whether independent reward-seeking LLMs can achieve recursive social improvement.
PaiR6xTSm7.method: The authors study populations of LLM agents that allocate a single shared token budget across private search, peer copying, skill-file revision, and acting. They compare social versus solo populations under matched total compute in controlled bandit-like environments and skill-evolution tasks.
PaiR6xTSm7.key_idea: Tests matched-token-budget populations of LLMs deciding when and whom to copy skill files from against solo self-improving learners to measure recursive social improvement.
PaiR6xTSm7.evidence: Controlled social-learning algorithm comparisons across three LLMs and matched-cost skill-evolution experiments on two LLMs (including IFBench).
PaiR6xTSm7.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree the research question is interesting, well written, and rigorously framed via matched-cost comparisons that separate learning efficiency from effectiveness.
PaiR6xTSm7.main_concern: Reviewers note the main skill-evolution experiments are too narrow (two homogeneous LLMs on one benchmark) to support broad negative conclusions, and results are mixed across models.

83T30XzE8B.one_liner: Asymmetrically pools queries during prefill and keys during decode using inverse-density weighting and sort-free Bernoulli sampling.
83T30XzE8B.problem: Existing sparse attention methods typically accelerate either compute-bound prefilling or bandwidth-bound decoding, and rely on rigid top-k budgets or diluted mean pooling.
83T30XzE8B.method: WASP applies block sparse attention along opposite axes per stage—pooling queries in prefilling and keys in decoding—using Inverse Density Weighted (IDW) pooling to preserve distinctive vectors and an approximate Bernoulli sampler to allocate per-head budgets without sorting.
83T30XzE8B.key_idea: Pool queries for prefilling and keys for decoding via TF-IDF-style inverse-density weighting and sort-free Bernoulli sampling to adapt per-head sparsity budgets.
83T30XzE8B.evidence: Evaluated training-free across six text and multimodal long-context benchmarks on Qwen3-8B, Llama-3.1-8B, and Qwen3-VL-8B.
83T30XzE8B.claimed_gains: Matches dense attention accuracy on five of six benchmarks while accelerating the attention layer by 2.9x at prefilling and 2.6x at decoding for roughly 2x end-to-end speedup.
83T30XzE8B.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that asymmetrically targeting prefill compute and decode bandwidth within one training-free framework is intuitive and well-motivated.
83T30XzE8B.main_concern: Reviewers note missing baselines combining separate prefill and decode sparse methods, no block-size sensitivity sweeps or exact sink/window hyperparameters, and indirect rather than full-request end-to-end latency measurements.

r0y9tKtZyj.one_liner: Learns smooth exact-zero gates for per-edge adaptive early exit of tensor-product layers in equivariant interatomic potentials.
r0y9tKtZyj.problem: Equivariant tensor-product computations bottleneck the length and time scales of machine learning interatomic potentials in molecular dynamics.
r0y9tKtZyj.method: BranchIP adds learned smooth exact-zero gates and sparse execution to equivariant MLIPs so individual atomic interactions dynamically skip deeper tensor-product layers while preserving smooth, conservative potential energy surfaces.
r0y9tKtZyj.key_idea: Gate equivariant tensor-product layers per interaction using smooth functions with a flat exact-zero region so skipped edges preserve conservative energies, forces, and Hessians.
r0y9tKtZyj.evidence: Evaluated with bespoke and fine-tuned foundation MLIPs on a heterogeneous catalysis system (CO/Pt), a solid acid electrolyte (CDP), and SPICE 2, including NVE molecular dynamics checks.
r0y9tKtZyj.claimed_gains: Achieves up to 2.4x faster inference and 2.6x lower memory usage while preserving physical fidelity.
r0y9tKtZyj.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers agree that smooth exact-zero gating is a coherent way to achieve conservative adaptive depth in equivariant MLIPs and yields interpretable chemical routing patterns.
r0y9tKtZyj.main_concern: Reviewers argue that learned routing is not compared against compute-matched smaller dense models or simpler baselines, accuracy degrades notably on the CDP foundation model (40% higher force MAE), and evaluation lacks standard benchmarks.

wautlfGlwb.one_liner: Extracts short-horizon research decision tasks with rubric rewards from scientific papers to RL-train LLMs for AI research.
wautlfGlwb.problem: Training LLMs on open-ended AI research suffers from sparse credit assignment across intermediate decisions and expensive execution-based feedback.
wautlfGlwb.method: PESTO decomposes ICML, ICLR, NeurIPS, and arXiv papers into structured research decisions (gap identification, method proposal, experiment design, result analysis) paired with criterion-level rubric rewards, and trains a 27B LLM via SFT and RL on these surrogate tasks.
wautlfGlwb.key_idea: Decompose scientific papers into connected short-horizon research decision tasks scored by criterion-level rubric rewards for reinforcement learning.
wautlfGlwb.evidence: Trained a 27B model on paper-derived tasks and evaluated on held-out rubric tasks plus execution-based benchmarks (including nanoGPT and GRPO).
wautlfGlwb.reviewer_consensus: Reviewers value the execution-based evaluation of proposed research ideas and the controlled comparisons separating rubric RL from SFT and continued pretraining.
wautlfGlwb.main_concern: Reviewers point out that the entire QA, rubric, and judging pipeline relies solely on uncalibrated LLMs, single-paper tasks diverge from real multi-paper research, and component ablations are incomplete.
